Most of us love to sleep. Some also take a nap in the afternoon to keep themselves fresh.
Similarly we must also sleep for 6 - 8 hours at night.
If you don't sleep well, you have headache, are in a bad mood, have puffy eyes, feel drowzy and are not able to work well.
6-8 hours of sleep gives your body ample rest and rejuvenates it.
Sleep is very important.
Can you imagine surviving without sleeping for 60 years?
You would say it is impossible.
But it is a fact. Let me tell you.
Thai Ngọc was born in 1942 in Vietnam.
Currently he is working as a farmer and lives with his wife and 2 sons.
When Thai was 20 years, he had high fever.
The fever subsided, but in 1972 - 73, his insomnia started and he was not able to sleep.
He tried his best to sleep but he couldn't and always remained awake.
Even the afternoons he couldn't sleep. He remained awake for days.
Since that time Thai has never slept. It has been 60 years!
Surprising isn't it?
You might be thinking that without sleep Thai would have fallen sick, or would have had headache etc
as without sleep, you know, it is impossible to remain healthy.
But inspite not sleeping for 60 years, Thai is healthy, fit and is foloows a good diet.
Surprising!
Thai has green tea everyday and eats healthy food.
Thai too wants to have a peaceful sleep like others around him but he just cannot sleep.
He brews wine and is also fond of drinking it and is healthy.
He also goes to work at night. Wow!
Thai’s story of not sleeping since 60 years is widespread in Vietnam.
However, some people after seeing the videos did not believe it and thought it was impossible.
Upon researching they found it to be true. The man really did not sleep at all.
People were stunned by this and couldn't believe it. A normal person just can not stay awake like that.
After the news went viral,
A YouTuber by the name Drew Binsky interviewed Thai Ngoc and the video has over 4 million views.
People were surprised by his strange condition.
Experts say that Thai was part of the Vietnam-US war during the 1950-1960. The war went on for a long time.
The violence during the war would be the reason for his sleepless nights. His dreams may have been filled with the trauma.
This is called PTSD. May who survive dangerous car crash and flight crash may never be able to sit in a car or flight again.
This is called PTSD. Maybe Thai is suffering from PTSD after the war
The traumatising scenes of the war may continue to haunt him, which is why he may be unable to sleep.
Experts say this could be the reason for his condition.
Hmm so what do you think? Is this condition real? Let us know in the comments.

Yakutsk in Russia is the coldest place on earth with a temperature of -50 degrees celsius!

Temperature fall down to minus -50 degrees celsius.
At minus 5C, the cold is quite refreshing and a light sweater and scarf are all that's required to keep warm.
At minus 20C, the moisture in your nostrils freezes, and the cold air starts making it difficult to breathe.
The cold irritates the lungs and the person keeps coughing.
At minus 35C, the air will cold enough to numb exposed skin. Parts of your body will get frostbite and can fall off.
Your nose can also fall off. Your toes, fingers, etc can get frostbite and fall off. It is because of loss of circulation.
This is at minus -35 degrees.
And at minus 45C, your eye glasses sticks to your cheeks and will tear off chunks of flesh when you remove them.
This is why Yukutsk resident warn people to not wear glasses in the region
Residents say you can not fight the cold. You have have to wear multiple layers of clothing to stay warm.
They say you have to dress like a cabbage to stay alive.

You would have seen many salaried people taking leave from office
for wedding or travelling, holidays, or to spend time with their families etc.

Many face this type of disturbance by office colleagues during their holidays.
However, Dream11 company is trying to bring a resolution to this problem.
Dream 11 was founded in 2008 by Harsh Jain and Bhavit Seth.
The founders thought about and announced a policy.
When a Dream 11 employee went on a holiday, their colleagues disturbed them by repeatedly calling them.
Since the employee is on holiday and enjoying, such calls spoilt their holiday mood.
This in turn affects the productivity and they tend to make mistakes as they are not in work mood.
The employee cannot focus on work. Better not to disturb.
Secondly, it would be that the office is dependent on the employee.
In order to stop this dependence, the founders thought of an unplug policy.
Which has been named as Dream 11 Unplug.
Plug in means 'to connect'. Unplug means 'to disconnect'
Similarly when an employee goes on leave, for a week in a year,
they would unplug or disconnect from the compnay's work.
This is to try and reduce the dependence on the employee and also to let the employee enjoy and spend time with family.
The aim is to make other employees take responsibility for the work and reduce the dependence on a particular employee.
So, they came up this solution and announced the same.
If any co-worker reaches out to another employee during the Unplug or leave time,
then he/she has to pay a fine of Rs 1 lakh rupees.
No excuses would be accepted as there are backup plans ready and the person has to pay the fine.
A co-worker can call up a colleague who is on leave to talk about their wellbeing.
However if the call is work related, they will have to pay a fine of Rs 1 Lakh.
The founders want employees to work independently and reduce dependence on each other.
The aim is also to let the employee enjoy their holiday
Interesting, isn't it?

then suggest the solution that is being followed by Dream 11.

A group of 7 people initiated this idea of travelling wearing only an underwear.
They pretended not to know each other and, if asked, claimed that they had just forgot their pants.
People felt happy seeing them and the mission expanded.
It started with men and grew into an international celebration with dozens of cities around the world participating each year.
The event is celebrated every year once in the month of January.
In New York it is known as 'No Pants Subway Ride.'
In London the same event has a different name and it has now gone viral.
In New York the event was not initiated for awareness or fund raising.
The founder said, "The aim of the day was to enjoy and a make everyone laugh and smile.
People are stressed and when they see something like this, they get amused. It spreads  positivity. That is the only aim.
In London too it was started for the same reason.
In New York it started from 2002 and went till 2020.
Amazing that they have been doing this for so long!
Since 2 years the event has been cancelled due to Covid-19 pandemic and other reasons.
However in London, the day was celebrated in the month of January.
Now even women participate and enjoy travelling in their underwear. It has become viral.
The founder of The Stiff Upper Lip Society, Ivan Markovic said
This is just for entertainment and fun.
It is not to raise money or awareness.
If you do it for raising money, someone might object to it.
It is better to just do it for enjoyment and fun.
No Pant Ride was also initiated in Tokyo, Japan and other places.
In Moscow, Russia the No Pant Ride drew attention from local police who after a few days called the organizer for questioning.
He was released without charges.

During summer, Srinagar is the capital. However now Jammu Kashmir has become a Union Territory.
There are several countries around the world that have 3 capitals.
While India has just 1 capital, some have 3.
They have seperate Legislative capital, Judicial capital and Administrative & Executive Capital.
Let me tell you about some of these places.
1. Africa is one of the 7 continents.
South Africa is a country in the African continent.
South Africa has 3 capitals. Surprising!
While Cape Town where the parliament is based is the Legislative Capital,
Bloemfontein is the Judicial Capital.
The Administrative and Executive Capital is Pretoria where government offices are based.
These are the 3 different Capitals.
2. Sri Lanka is a small island situated in the Indian Ocean.
It has 2 separate Capitals.
Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the Administrative Capital of Sri Lanka where all government ministries are located.
The Commercial and Judicial Capital is Colombo.
3. Georgia has 2 seperate capitals.
Georgia's official Capital is Tbilisi where its government offices and judiciary are based.
Legislative Capital of Georgia is Kutaisi as the Parliament is located there.
That is why it has 2 capitals.
4. Malaysia too has two capitals.
Kuala Lumpur is the official Capital of Malaysia which houses the parliament and the judiciary.
While Putrajaya is the Administrative Capital where government offices are located.
These are the 2 capitals.
5. The Netherlands is a major country in the European continent.
Netherland has 2 capitals.
The official Capital of the Netherlands is Amsterdam,
while Hague is the Administrative Capital.
These were the 5 countries. There are a many more such countries.
You may have been thinking that every country like India has just one capital.
But there are some countries which have 3 or 2 capitals as well.

However, let me tell you some strange incidents related to disability.
A child was born without any disability and was 100% sighted, had no problem with her limbs or hearing.
While growing up, they could see well, but were more comfortable being blind
and wanted to be blind. Can you imagine a sighted person wanting to become blind?
You would think it is impossible, right? But this has been experienced by many.
There are many able-bodied individuals who intentionally become blind,
while some amputate an arm as they feel it is a part of their body.
Similarly there are many who can walk well but are not comfortable with their limbs.
So to get relief they amputate their legs.
There are hearing people who identify themselves as Deaf & purposefully become Deaf signers.
Strange, isn't it? But there are many such people around the world.
Let me tell you about one such experience.
Jewel Shuping from USA's North Carolina shares her experience.
Shuping was born as an able-bodied child and had no disablity.
She was not comfortable being sighted and was more comfortable in being blind. She identified as a Blind person.
She said that at the age of 4, she regularly practiced walking around the house in darkness like a blind person.
Her mother did not understand her behaviour as it was crazy for a sighted girl to walk like a blind person.
Jewel's mother thought she was foolish. But Jewel continued the same and by the time she was 13 -14 years old,
she started wearing thick black glasses with which she couldn't see anything even with open eyes.
She was comfortable and happy that way. Strange!
By the time she was 20, she was fully fluent in Braille and had learnt all the mannerisms of Blind people.
Jewl even went to a Psychologist and explained that she fett more comfortable being blind.
After about 2 weeks of analysis, the psychologist diagnosed that Shuping had Body Integrity Identity Disorder (BIID).
It is a condition due to which sighted Jewel believed she was meant to be blind.
It was not a random thought and neither was she mad.
It was due to the BIID condition that she suffered which made her identify herself as blind.
She wanted to become blind but no doctor was ready to take away her eyesight.
It was unimaginable that a sighted person wanted to come blind.
Usually it is the blind who through eye donations etc can regain their sight.
Some who have lost a limb, use prosthetic limbs.
But Jewel's case was the opposite as she wanted to become blind and doctors did not agree to this at all.
Jewel went to multiple doctors but none of them agreed.
She put cleaning liquid in her eyes that helped her lose her vision and she was very happy with it.
She always wanted to become blind as she wasn't comfortable being a sighted person and was stressed.
Now after becoming blind she is relieved of all the stress. How unique!

as the disabled or a blind person has to face a lot of hardships.

When the person goes to a doctor saying that they would be comfortable if the limb is cut off, the doctor doesn't approve of it.

In India there are 3 types of political parties- National parties like the BJP, Congress, etc.
National parties are parties that contest elections across India.
Second is State Parties. For example after winning an election in Maharashtra or Odisha, the party does not contest elections anywhere else.
Parties that contest elections on a state level are known as State Parties.
Third is Regional Parties. This parties contest elections only on a regional level.
These are the 3 parties.
The election Commission has certain criteria that need to be fulfilled to become a national party.
Here is an example.
BJP should secure majority votes polled in four or more states and have 6% seats in the Lok Sabha.
This and many other criterias need to be met for a party to be a national party.
Currently there are 7 national parties - Congress, BJP, TMC, NCP, etc.
Except for AAP. They are not a national party.
This is because they have not yet fulfilled the Election Commission's criteria.
Once they fulfil the criteria's they will be made a national party and we will have total 8 national parties in India.

This is because they are contesting elections in Himachal Pradesh & Gujarat. If they fulfil the criteria's in this elections,
According to sources, this election will for sure make them a national party.
Results for Himachal & Gujarat are expected on 8th December 2022.
So why is this story important? It is because a National Party enjoys many benefits.
Here are the points.
The Election Commission will allotment a permanent election symbol to the party.
Just like how BJP, Congress, etc have a permanent election symbol.
State and Regional parties have to apply for the symbol and it takes a long time. But National Parties enjoy a permanent symbol.
Secondly, National Parties will get the get electoral lists from different constituency.
State and Regional parties do not enjoy this benefit. It is only reserved for National parties.
Third point. National parties will enjoy free airtime on national media platforms like Doordarshan Network or the Akashvani.
This priviledge is only reserved for National Parties.
However all parties have to pay private media platforms.
Fourth point. During general elections, political parties are permitted to nominate star Campaigners like celebrities or public figures.
Fifth point. The government provides land or a building for the National parties to erect their party headquarters.
AAP is all set to become the National Party as they are all set to fufil the election commission's criterias at the Gujarat & HP elections.

Surprisingly, for the first time in history a pregnant mummy along with the foetus has been found.
There are people who died thousands of years ago.
These bodies decompose and scientists use the skeletal structure to study how humans looked at that time.
They want to study the difference in facial features of humans now and then.
For this, the skull is scanned and reconstructed using 2D and 3D technique.
These techniques help us understand the shapes of their face and their features.
The bones also help us understand the person's height.
The bones help to reconstruct their face using 2D 3D techniques. Without the bones it is not possible.

The pregnant mummy was found in 1826. However nobody knew about the foetus.
Polish scientists found the foetus a year back.
Generally people are mummified alone.
The mummy was found in 1826 but the foetus was found last year. Since then no one knew about it!
The mummy's bones were still intact! Upon further research, scientists say the baby was 7 months old.
How did they know this?
The foetus head circumference was measured and it was found that it was in the 7th month of its life.
The foetus and the mother were mummified together for the first time in histoty.
Upon reconstructing her face they found how she looked at that time.
However this is not completely accurate.
Chantal Milani share what is the most useful to scientists.
She said when people die their body decomposes and only bones remain.
She said, 'Our bones give a lot of information about the face, height & dimensions of an individual.
A wide skeleton suggests a fat person, an elongated shape would mean a tall person.
A small skeleton means a short person. It also helps to learn more about their facial features and jawline.
Using 2D and 3D techniques one can actually put a face to the skeleton.
Its not completely accurate but helps us see how the person looked.
Hew Morrison said, " Fingerprint identification or DNA analysis are not an option in such bodies.
Only bones help in the 2D 3D reconstruction.

1. High fever

3. Coughing and sore throat
4. Runny Nose
5. Breathlessness

7. Nausea and vomiting
8. Diarrhea
Senior citizens with weak immunity are susceptible to Camel Flu.

India is now wants to start a unique bus journey from New Delhi to London, United Kingdom.
Preparations are done for the journey.
Earlier there were plans to start the bus journey
but the border tensions between India and Myanmar delayed the plan.
Now with the border tensions eased out, the bus service is expected to start soon.
The Delhi to London bus will cover approximately 20,000 km.
The bus will pass through 18 countries before reaching London, UK.
The price for the entire bus trip is around 15 lakhs per person.
To give travelers a comfortable journey, the bus will have drinking, dining, and sleeping facilities.
The enjoyable journey will take 70 days.
The 15 Lakh cost includes tickets, visas, and lodging in various countries for 70 days. Wonderful!
The bus will start from Delhi, pass through Myanmar, Thailand, China, Kyrgyzstan and reach France.
Further, a ferry will also be used to go from Calle in France to Dover in the UK.
Then the bus would take them to London. Wow!
Once the route is finalised, the travelers will be able to enjoy bus ride to London.
A similar bus service was initiated by a British bus company, Albert Tours, around 65 years ago.
In 1957, UK's Albert Tours started the bus service from Kolkata.
The bus connected Kolkata to London via Delhi and was in service for many years.
In 1976, the service was discontinued due to a few accidents,
and a continuous border tensions with Myanmar and with other nations.
After this there were no other similar bus service till date.
Now India is planning to start a similar bus route from India to London soon.
I am sure you all are excited to experience this enjoyable bus service.

However, there was pay disparity between the men's and the women's teams.
Let me give you an example.
For every international match, BCCI paid each player of the men's playing team a match fee.
For example, match fee for men player is Rs 6 lakh for a 50 overs ODI.
While the women cricketer was paid only Rs 1 Lakh.
The match fee for the men is Rs 15 Lakh for a Test match, while the women were only paid Rs 4 Lakh.
For T20 the male player is paid Rs 3 Lakh. Information is not available for women players.
In a good news, on 27th October 2022, BCCI announced that
a pay equity policy,which means men and women players would get the same match fees.
Thats wonderful! This means the women players will now get Rs 6 lakh for One-Day International,
Rs 15 lakh per Test match, and Rs 3 lakh for a T20 International. This is the same as the men's team.
However one thing has been kept the same.
When the players play a match, they get match fee.
There is annual retainership which is paid at the end of the year for the number of matches played by the player.
Based on the number of matches, the players are graded into A, B and C and they get a whopping amount.
A Grade player is the one who
B is lesser matches and C is the least number of matches which maybe due to injury, rest etc.
The Grade A men players get about Rs 7 Crore while Grade C get paid about Rs 1 Crore
While the women player get paid very less. Grade A - Rs 50 lakh, Grade B - Rs 30 lakh and Grade C Rs 10 lakh.
Women are paid Rs 50, 30 and 10 Lakhs while the men get Rs 1 - 7 Crores.
The pay disparity is because the men’s team play more matches than the women’s team every year.
However on 27th October 2022, BCCI announced on Twitter that the match fee for ODI, Test and T20 will be equal henceforth.
Everyone applauded BCCI's decision.
WIth BCCI's annoucement about equal pay, India has become the second country to implement equal pay after New Zealand.

If your daughter is mentally unstable will you keep her locked in a room for years?
You wouldn't, right? Even if you don't solution from doctors, you wouldn't keep her chained.
You understand they are humans too.
This is not the case with this father who kept his daughter locked in a dark room
and that too chained for 36 years.
You don't believe, right? Let me tell you.
The incident from Hathras came to light when a BJP MLA Anjula Mahaur informed about it.
When Anjula heard about the girl from some neighbours, she visited the place and was shocked.
She was so dirty that you can't even too at her.
Her clothes, her room everything was very filthy and dark.
When the girl, Sapna Jain was 17, her father Girish Chand felt that she was mentally unstable.
So he decided to chain her hands & legs and lock her up in a dark room so that she can't leave the house.
Sapna was chained and locked like an animal.
She was just 17. For bath, her father used to just throw water on her.
Noone helped her bathe and for bath water was just thrown on her.
Also food was slid to her from beneath the door. Heartwrenching!
She was kept in this condition for 36 years. She is now 53 years old.
She was chained inside a dingy room and had not seen the outside world since years.
She has no idea about life changes, technology etc. Heartbreaking!
BJP MLA Anjula heard about the girl and visited her along with Nirmala Singh, member of NGO, Seva Bharati.
They were shocked to see her condition.
Sapna was crawling, her hair and her body was all grimy and extremely fouled.
How could her father do this to her? Now her father is dead.
Sapna’s family refused to comment on Sapna and her condition.
NGO members immediately bathed her and got her some clean clothes.
MLA Anjula spoke to Sapna’s family and got her shifted to a mental health facility in Agra.
Gyanendra Singh, a doctor who examined her said that hopeful that she will recover soon, maybe within a few weeks.
When MLA Anjula questioned the family about Sapna's condtion they did not give any response.
Also whenever the neighbours repeatedly told the family to consult a doctor,
the family ignored them and asked the neighbours to stay away from their family matter.
The family told them that they knew what is best for Sapna.
The neighbours then had to back off.
I fail to understand why didn't the neighbours complain to the police since so long. It has been 36 years! Disgusting!
Now that she is shifted, hope she gets better. Heartwrenching!

For everyone, health is important.
If you are not healthy, in future you may suffer from diabetes, blood pressure, cancer, heart problems etc.
There is a lot of awareness and people do take care fo their physical health.
Everyone forgets about mental health. Only physical health is not important, mental health is equally important.
If you are not mentally stable, have negative thoughts or are stressed, your physical health will automatically be affected.
You can consult doctors for solution to your stress or take up yoga as mental health is utmost important.
I am telling you this now is because Indian government launched Tele - Manas service
on 10th October 2022 which is the World Mental Health Day.
The service is now launched as due to the Covid-19 pandemic and lockdown,
which led to a lot of stress as before Covid people could socialise and there was a balance in life.
However, during Covid-19 people were at home and couldn't meet others or go out.
and even the news were full of negativity about Covid-19. All this led to severe stress.
There was job related stress as well due to which people fell sick physically as well.
The Indian government felt that people should be provided counselling.
Hence, Tele - Manas service was launched.
Union Health ministry said it was important.
The service started with 20 states and UTs and will subsequently be expanded to the entire country including villages.
This is the Helpline number.
Callers will first get an IVRS, an automated robotic voice and they have to inform their details.
Then the call will be transferred to a trained counsellor or doctor in the caller's areas.
If the caller needs in-person services, they will be referred to the closest health centre.
The government is aware and charges have been kept negligible.
This service has been launched as mental health is important.
If mental health is ignored, physical health will also suffer. Happiness and peace of mind is important to work well.
Health Minister Mansukh Mandaviya shared a note on his twitter highlighting the importance of mental health.
Also Prime Minister Narendra Modi is committed towards enhancing mental health awareness.
This is a good initiative. Wonderful! But what about the Deaf?
There is no accessibility for the Deaf.
If the Deaf are not given accessibility in Sign language, they will be more stressed
and in case of any problem, the stress doubles as there is no communication.
We hope the Indian government realizes and provides accessibilty for the Deaf in this service.
Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

A Punjab based company called Neslak Biosciences had a product called 'HapiNes'
which was a easy-to-use and store powder form of mother's milk.

for violation of Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 which prohibits sell of mother's milk and its products.
The licence of the poduct 'HapiNes' was also suspended. Shoking!
The FSSAI agreed to the action taken
and also sent out an advisory to the State Food Commissioners and Licensing authorities
stating that they should inspect if businesses wrongly sell products made of mother's milk under the licence of dairy.
On the contrary they maybe selling mother's milk or products made from mother's milk.
They advised to inspect the companies strictly.
How was Neslak Biosciences' violation come to notice?
Breastfeeding Promotion Network of India (BPNI) is an NGO which promotes and supports breast feeding.
The NGO tried to contact Neslak Biosciences, but did not receive and response.
BPNI then filed a complaint with the Health Ministry.
The Health Ministry inquired and then took strict action the company.
Shocking!

The company's advertisement on its website and to doctors by its representatives
states that their product is the solution for breastfeeding.
Making such statments are not permitted under law.
According to them, the powdered mother's milk solves the problem in situations like rejoining work, night-time feeding etc.
This is not permitted under the law.
A subsidiary of a UK-based company was manufacturing products made from breast milk, under the name of Ayurveda.
The company's licence was cancelled. However, the company has reportedly gone to court.
This is the argument.
Minister of State for Health, Bharati Pawar said
Human milk cannot be used for commercial purposes. Remember!
Donation of mother's milk is allowed
only for babies whose mothers are unable to breastfeed them due to death or illness etc.
Commercially selling breast milk is not allowed. Remember!
Many people work very hard but get paid very little and find it difficult to survive.
When you look up to pilots, you think they are paid so well,
given accommodation, food, pick up and drop facility etc. and feel their life is better.
However, the pilots suffer a lot. Surprised? Confused?
A NGO called Safety Matters Foundation conducted a survey and interviewed Indian pilots.
Of the 542 Indian pilots surveyed, 358 pilots that is 66 % of the total said that they suffered a lot.
Shocking! The pilots said that unlike earlier they have to fly for more than 30 hours a week.
The pilots admitted sleeping in the pilot's seat while flying the aircraft
and this has been one of the reasons for accidents that occur during landing.
Inspite of being sleepy, they have to be extra careful as the life of the passengers depends on them.
It is not an easy job.
Another problem that they have is back to back morning flights from different time zones which lead to sleepiness.
With these time zone changes their life is not easy.
Pilot have to work for a lot more hours due to the back to back flights.
The interviewers were surprised by this.
They said that they get paid well but are not happy.
DGCA has policies and rules for pilots, however, the airlines companies do not implement the rules strictly.
Many airline companies violate the rules laid down by DGCA regarding hours of flying etc.
There is a demand of 1500 new pilots annually in India.
However, only 200 to 300 of these new pilots are hired.
The pilots are over worked. If more pilots are hired, the work hours will reduce drastically and they will get better sleep.
However, companies do not agree.
Due to inadequate number of pilots employed, work timings have gone up for most pilots.
This is the problem and their life is not easy.
Shockingly, they are sleep deprived.

Following Queen Elizabeth II's demise on 8th September, the world is mourning.

like in all Indian government buildings, the National Emblem is installed,
in UK, the Queen's crown and portrait - Royal Cypher is installed in all the buildings.
Her signatures are placed on post boxes and currency notes and coins.
However, now after her demise and her son becoming King Charles III
everywhere the Royal Cypher will have to be changed.
This is going to cost a lot of money.
Since taking over the crown in 1952, it was the Queen's Royal Cypher everywhere and now it has to be replaced with the King
for which the UK government will have to spend millions.
You would have seen the word ER, what does it mean?
R" stands for Regina, a Latin word which means Queen in English.
The latin word of King is "Rex".
Rex means King and Regina means Queen.
So, now the "R" would remain the same for Rex while "E" would be replaced with "C" for Charles III.
Many expenses need to be undergone to make these changes and it will also take a couple of years.
Let me tell you some of the things that will be changed.
There are currently approximately 100,000 post boxes in Britain,
which are marked with ERII
and the change that needs to be made will be CRIII.
The change will take time as all cannot be replaced at the same time.
It will take about 2 years to replace them. The new ones would be manufactured with the CRIII inscription
The old ones would be gradually replaced. Also the inscription at the door of the post office will be replaced to CRIII.
The currency notes have Queen Elizabeth's face on it and the coins have her face facing left.
Now after her demise, this has to be changed with that of King Charles III on the opposite side on the notes
and facing right on the coins.
That is as per the tradition followed by the British monarchy.
But this would not be done all of sudden. These will be replaced gradually until stocks are exhausted.
This will take a long time and also a lot of money.
The Queen was also the head of 15 other countires like Canada, New Zealand etc.
Some of the currencies in these countries also have the Queen's face.
They too said the changes would be done gradually until stock lasts.
The postal stamps had Queen Elizabeth's father photo. It was replaced with that of the Queen after his death.
A photographer, Dorothy Wilding took the portraits of the Queen in 1952 and those were in use till 1971.
Now, the portrait on the stamps too will be replaced with that of King Charles III
In UK's National Anthem, there are words like "queen" and "her",
will be replaced by "king," and "his" respectively.
The statements made in the passports alluding to "Her" Majesty
would be replaced by "His" Majesty.
The passports would not be called back for replacement.
The passports which go for renewal would be replaced with the new "his" word.
There will be no forced change. Everything will be changed in due course.
Now that Charles III is the new King, the country will have to bear many expenses to make necessary changes.

In a village in Tamil Nadu a young 13 year old girl was raped.
The girl then got pregnant and the pregnency advanced to 28 weeks.
Oh God! 28 weeks means 6 - 7 months.
A young 13 year old was pregnant! Her father is a farmer and she belonged to a poor family.
The family was to get the baby aborted. However Indian law does not permit abortion.
Looking for a solution, the father filed a plea in the Madras High court
stating that he did not want his young 13 year old to give birth to the baby.
If the baby is born, the girl is too young and physically her body is not fit enough like an adult woman to bear a child.
She was a playful child when she got raped and pregnant.
She would be in immense trauma and may even get suicidal thoughts.
Or delivering the baby would be risky for the girl's life. So, the father wanted abortion.
There is an act called Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971.
Let me clearly explain you what it means.
The law has been amended. Earlier this clause wasn't there.
For example if a wife for whatever reason wants to abort her child and goes to the doctor,
the doctor required consent from the husband or any elder family member.
As per rule the woman had no right.
Or if the woman is unmarried and gets pregnant, the father of the child or any other elder is called to give consent.
How shocking! The woman had no right to decide on abortion.
However, the law was modified in 2021 and the woman has the right to decide about abortion.
Upto 12 weeks or 3 months of pregnancy, the woman - married or unmarried has the right to abort an unwanted pregnancy.
She need not depend on the husband or any elder for consent.
If it is upto 12 weeks, she can directly decide about abortion with her doctor.
This amendment has brought a relief women as earlier they had to depend on others.
For pregnancy between 12 weeks to 20 weeks, that is 3 months to 5 months,
abortion is permitted but not for all.
It is permitted if the pregnancy is risky as the baby maybe be still born or born with mental health issue.
The court can permit abortion after considering reports from 2 doctors.
The rule is not for all.
For pregnancy between 20 weeks to 24 weeks, which is 5 - 6 months,
if the woman gets pregnant due to rape or incest rape,
court and the medical practitioners can permit abortion.
In this case, the girl is a 13 year old minor and 28 weeks pregnant which is 7 months.
The vital organs like the heart, eyes etc of the baby have already developed and so abortion is not possible.
Justice Abdul Quddhose of Madras High Court, reviewed the case and said,
The minor girl is 28 weeks pregnant, that is about 7 months.
If we go by the law, there will be grave danger to her mental and physical health.
The court has got wider powers than prescribed under the Act.
Considering the victim's age and other issues, the court allows the termination of pregnancy.
The judge further directed to nominate a team of specialised doctors to terminate her pregnancy
Also, during the period of her stay in the hospital, all financial and other assistance
would be provided by the Child Welfare Committee of Tiruvannamalai, TN.
The judge also ordered the removed fetus to be preserved
for carrying out medical and DNA tests against the accused so that he can be punished accordingly.
Once the case is closed, the fetus can be buried but till the case is going on, the fetus is to be preserved.
The accused has also been charged under various sections of the POCSO Act
It is a relief that the court understood and in India situation is better.
If the court would not have agreed and gone according to the law,
the minor girl could have had severe mental issues if the pregnancy was not terminated.
Court's decision to terminate the pregnancy will bring relief to the girl and she would be counselled for the truama.
Laws in India are becoming better. Let us know your thoughts in the comments section.

The flag has undergone several changes.
India got independence in 1947, however the Indian naval flag had a red cross with the UK flag on it.
From 1947 to 1950 the same flag was used.
India was now an independent country and so it was decided to change the flag.
The Union Jack was replaced with the Tricolour, and the red cross was retained.
The red cross known as the Saint George's Cross, is associated with Saint George, a military crusader. This red cross was used.
It was decided to remove the red cross, however from 1950 to 2001, the red cross had been retained.
George’s Cross was replaced with the naval crest in the middle while the Tricolour was kept on the top left corner.
The background was kept white.
However there were complaints that the blue colour merged with the blue colour of skies and the sea.
This flag was used from 2001 to 2004 and then in 2004 the red George’s Cross was brought back
but now it had the national emblem in the middle of the red cross.
The flag continued to be used till 2014.
In 2014, the cross was retained and only the words 'Satyamev Jayate’ were added below national emblem.
The same flag was used from 2014 to 2022. It was then decided to let go of the red cross
and make a flag indigenous to India with the tricolour on the top left with the blue twin bordered octagon in the centre.

and our focus is on the Deafness. The RPWD Act 2016 has provisions for the People with Disabilities in various areas like education,
accessibility, health, etc. However many of these laws can not be understood by the lay man.
The Draft National Policy for PWD Consists of guidelines for people to understand.
Deaf leaders from across India are here to discuss the Draft National Policy for PWD.
The workshop was organised by SHF and NAD. It was supported by AYJNISHD(D) & NCPEDP.
Deaf leaders have given discourses on education, health, accessibility, employment etc. all related to the Deaf. Many suggestions were made as well.
Mr Sibaji Panda is the founder of Happy Hands School for the Deaf in Odisha.

When the RPWD Act becomes difficult to understand, these policies provide a longer explanation.
Everyone has to follow these guidelines. The government has already created a draft policy with which were are not satisfied.
Why? Because there is no development in Deaf education.
Oralism is still being used. Sign Language is also mentioned but there is no training plan setup and teachers are teaching on their own.
We need to have discussion on how to take Indian Deaf education to level of USA, UK and Europe.
Sadly, no way has been found yet
More importantly, the policies and the RPWD Act mention quality education for the Deaf.
However it does not explain what constitutes 'Quality Education'.
Today and tomorrow we will try to add more ideas and suggestions to the policy
These are not meant to completely solve the education crisis, but it will gradually improve the situation.
This because of the tug of war between oralism & Sign Language practitioners.
I am hoping that government will accept the suggestions. It may discard our suggestions, who knows.
However, I am having a great time with these discussions.
These suggestions to the policies will be handed over to whom and whom will they connect with in the government?

When NAD complained about the english text, the policies were translated into Sign Language.
Now we are collecting feedback from Deaf people and Deaf leaders.
A.S.Narayanan team will compile all the suggestions and hand it over to the government, before 31st August as it is the deadline.

It will be a long process but the policies are very important for the life of Deaf people

In today's discussion related to the 'Education' topic, there was an interesting topic about inclusive education for Deaf and hearing.
This idea suggests Deaf should study with hearing as it will lead to growth. What do you think?

Instead of separating kids, the idea promotes inclusion. However there is no clarity on its usage.
It does not end at inclusion. There are many factors involved.
What do you mean by inclusion? It means giving appropriate options to all.
For example trains. Those living in Mumbai know about local trains.
Suppose there is no clarity regarding the coaches and everyone is allowed in.
Then hearing men, women, children, people with disability, vendors, etc. will all get into the train.
There is inclusivity but no comfort and clarity about one's position.
Hence, we have a compartment for men, women, handicap, luggage, etc.
Now people can travel with comfort.
Here the idea of inclusivity is clear.
Alloting seats to anyone and everyone is not inclusivity.
So this idea needs to be used in inclusive education. Putting Deaf, Blind, hearing students together,
is the same as allowing everyone to board the same compartment.
We have to figure out how to elaborate this concept and find appropriate options for all. This is inclusivity.
We are coming up with suggestions for the same.

The Indian Railways can take you to remote locations across the country.
These journey can be for as long as 2 - 3 nights or as shorts as a few hours.
The Indian Railways is the 4th longest railway network in the world.
Railway network is the length in kilometers of railway tracks laid.
India has a nationwide rail network of 65,000 km and is the 4th longest in the world.
The US rail network, is the longest in the world with 2,50,000km.
China with 1,00,000 km, ranks second in the world.
Russia with 85,500 km is the 3rd longest rail network in the world.
4th is India with 65,000 Km.
Indian Railway currently has over 13,450 passenger trains
which is used to carry approximately 24 million passengers daily.
Additionally, Indian railways also has 9,141 goods trains which carry coals, oil etc
The normal capacity of existing goods train is 90 coaches.
Each coach carries about 100 tonnes of goods.
The whole train carries about 9,000 tonnes in one journey.
Indian railways made a new and amazing train.
Indian railways has made an extremely long train which will take a long time to pass through.
The train was run between Korba and Rajnandgaon in Chhattisgarh coversing a distance of 267 Km.
The train has 295 coaches which were loaded with coal.
This is three times the capacity of existing railway rakes of 90 coaches. 295 coaches! Whoa!
Earlier the train carried 9,000 tonnes, now this train can carry 27,000 tonnes of goods.
Also, the train can't be pulled by 1 engine, so it was attached with a total of 6 engines.
The train rakes were formed by merging five goods trains into one and was attached to 6 engines.
The test run of the train was done on 15th August 2022 on the occassion of India's 75 years of Independence.
The train left Korba at around 1:50 in the afternoon.
It took about 11 hours and reached Rajnandgaon station at around 1:00 midnight.
This goods train takes about four minutes to cross a station! How one of a kind!
Coal carried in 90 coaches doesn't fulfil the demand.
Coal is needed to produce electricity and to meet the demand, a longer train was made which can supply more coal.
The Railways plans to use this train more frequently.
This is the first time Indian railways has started a 3.5 Km long train. Wow!
The train has been named Super Vasuki.

Balinese people have a belief that when a relative or a family member dies,

Everyone contributed for the mass cremation.

Bodies in various states of decay were exhumed and wrapped in a white cloth.
A structure of an elephant-headed fish was constructed and all the 117 bodies were placed in it.

Families carried photos of the deceased, they performed the rituals, and after completing the procession,
the bodies were cremated. The familes were happy to see their loved attain salvation.
Since the families were not able to afford the ritual, they did this.
Holding mass cremation every 5 years, also helped to free up land at the graveyards.
It helps save money and boosts harmony among the community.

There is an interesting history about the Commonwealth Games. So keep watching.
The Games were called the British Empire Games and started from the year 1930
Over the years the name has undergone many changes.
After the British Empire Games, it was known as the British Empire and Commonwealth Games.
The name was then changed to British Commonwealth Games.
Since 1976 it is being known as Commonwealth Games and are played every 4 years.
Commonwealth games are played between 56 countries.
Do you know why it was called as British Empire Games?
You are aware that earlier the Britishers had colonized a lot of countries in the world
and the vast majority of the of the 56 member countries were former territories of the British Empire
like India, Australia, Canada, Pakistan, Nigeria in Africa and many more.
The Commonwealth Games encourage independence from the British, democracy, human rights, development etc.
as these countries share the same history of oppression at the hands of the British.
So the name Commonwealth Games, traces it  roots to the Britishers.
Queen Elizabeth II, the Queen of England is the Patron of the Commonwealth Games.
The 56-member countries participate to encourage harmony among nations.

On 17th July 2022, the CM announced amended and stricter rules for drivers in Punjab.
Fines are still there but let me tell you what is new.
If someone is caught in a drink and drive case, they will be fined, their licence would be suspended for 3 months.
If the person is a repeat offender, like others, the fine would be higher and the licence would be suspended for 3 months.
Do you think that is the only punishment? They will break the rule again.
It is better to send the offenders for training to the driving school with an expert who teach them all traffic rules.
Once they are done with the training, they are sent to local schools for 2 hours to train the kids in traffic rules.
This can change their behaviour.
Another punishment is that they will be sent to a hospital to help or asked to donate blood.
These are different punishments that Punjab has come up with to teach a lesson.
These punishments for traffic law breakers are only in Punjab and nowhere else in India.

Now I am going to tell you about them.
Germany has a world famous highway.
Around the world, highways have a specific speed limit to be followed.
If ignored, the offender is fined.
Germany's highway is known for not having any speed limits.
However, you are not allowed to stop on the highway and you would be fined if you stop.
There is an exeption for emercency situations.
If you have no valid reason to stop, the cops would be there in no time and fine & arrest you for 5 years.
It is very strict. Even if you run out of fuel, you will still be punished.
Not having enough fuel before driving on the higways is considered as negligence of the driver and would be fined.
However there is no speed limit. Weird!
In Russia there is a very strange and a strict law.
The rule is so strict that even if you car is dirty, you will be fined.
The Russian authorities do not want even a speck of dirt on your car.
Also, this doesn’t apply just to the exteriors, it includes the interiors of the car as well.
If not, you will be fined under the law.
Also if the car is clean, it is up to the officer to determine what’s dirty and what’s not.
The rule is so strict as Russia wants the cars to be clean.
In India we wash the car wherever it is parked, even if it is on the road.
However, in Russia it is illegal to clean your car at any place apart from your residential area or an actual car wash center.
Unlike India, it is not allowed to wash the car on the road. Strange rule!
Cyprus has one of the strangest driving rules .
If you take your hand off the steering wheel while you are driving, you wil be fined.

Also eating and drinking while driving is illegal and you would be fined.
Cyprus has the strangest rule.

Mumbai is known for its local trains, which are always busy.
Anyone whether rich or poor are able to afford it.
However this is not the case with Pune.
Unlike high frequency local trains in Mumbai, in Pune the local trains frequency is very less.
Residents of Pune use Autorickshaws for travel.
Now auto fare has increased and people are extremely unhappy with this.
Why? Let me tell you.
Before October 2021 the base fare for 1.5km was Rs 18 and Rs 12 per kilometer after that.
Regional Transport Authority (RTA), Pune, then decided to increase the fare to Rs 20 as it had been a long time.
The base fare became Rs 20 and Rs 13 per kilometer after that.
The decision was met with huge protests from the autodrivers.
Unhappy with the Rs 20 fare, they demanded a higher fare price.
In October - November 2021, the fare was increased to Rs 21 as the base fare and Rs 14 per km after that.
You may think that the fare revision will be made after a year or two.
It is not even a year since the rates were increased, and now the fare has been increased for the third time!
From Rs 18, Rs 20, Rs 21, now the price is Rs 23!
The RTA announced that from 1st August 2022, the new fares will be Rs 23 for the first 1.5 km and thereafter Rs 15 for every kilometer.
What a hike in prices! People are extremely unhappy with this.
The reason is that autodrivers were protesting against the Rs 21 fare as they were unable to make ends meet.
This is because of hike in CNG prices. Prices of CNG have increased in the international market due to the Russia-Ukraine war.
Since CNG imports have become expensive, price increases and autodrivers can't afford the fuel with the minimal fare.
Earlier the price of CNG was Rs 63 per kg, after the war,
the price increased to Rs 85 per kg. Such a huge spike.
If the Rs 21 fare remains constant, then how would drivers manage. Hence they were protesting.
This is why the price was increased to Rs 23 to help the drivers and their families survive.
RTA also said that after the increase in fare, the meter up-gradation work needs to be done.
This is done only at specific government run organisations.
Since everyone can not do it at the same time, appointments are needed.
In the mean time, instead of the old meter, drivers can use the new fare price sheets and keep passengers updated.
Drivers have been instructed to complete the necessary meter up-gradation work by 30 September 2022.

Comparitively the 1st strain is more deadly.

Our parents work hard, save money, buy gold, create Fixed Deposits, Mutual Funds, Reccuring Deposits, etc.
They invest in homes, land, shops, etc. so that their son or daughter can inherit these. Or the siblings share these.
Parents do these out of love for their children. Everyone does this.
However this story is about devastating betrayals.
Parents are cared for, loved, helped, and when they sign agreements to name the property to their children,
these kids wash their hands of their parents. These senior citizens are forced to work as maids or they are kicked out of the house.
There are many such cases where parents are tormented. Their food is thrown, they are locked in rooms,
there are multiple stories where senior citizens are torture. It is very sad.
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 has rules that protect parents & the elderly
from children who oppress them. The law protects and has the power to investigate such matters.
The law protects the senior citizens from everything but once the property is made in the child's name,
there is no way the property can be given back to the parents.
Now the Bombay High Court said the law has been amended and parents can be relaxed.
When senior citizens are duped by children or when hearing children dupe their Deaf parents,
now you all need not worry. The law was updated in 2018. However there was no awareness on this.
I will now tell you about it.
This happened in Mumbai. A man named Natvar Sanghvi had a son named Pritish Sanghvi who was married.
Natvar Sanghvi was a widower and decided to remarry.
After his marriage he gave he gave a 50 per cent share of his flat to his son and they all lived together.
However Natvar claimed that his son and daughter-in-law started mistreating his second wife
after which he left the flat and started living in a rented flat.
He then decided to reclain the 50% property given to the son and approached the suburban collector and told him the entire story.
The collector directed his son, Pritish Sanghvi, to return back the share of his father’s property.
Pritish refused and challenged the order in the Bombay High Court.
On 18 July 2018 Bombay High Court's Justice Ranjit More and Justice Anuja Prabhudesai, while hearing the petition
upheld the collector's decision and Pritish has to give the house back to his father.
This was the amendment that was made in 2018.
The Bombay HC said if a senior citizen signs an agreement after 2007 to transfer the property,
then they can file a petition to take back their property if they are not taken care of.
This is their right and is the latest update. Prior to 2007, people will not be able to file a claim.
I am sure many of you are relieved. You can file the petition and I hope children live in fear now.
The law also says that senior citizens who do not have a family or children,
if they decide to name their property to their relative, then there are rules to this agreement.
Once the property is transfered the relative has to completely care of the senior citizen.
The court can make an agreement that after the senior's death the relative will inherit the property.
For this the senior is eligible to get upto Rs 10,000 monthly to help them meet their needs as they are unemployed as well.
Once the senior passes away, the relative inherits the property.

ML stands for Maternity Leave. It is a 6 month paid leave given to women working in private and government establishments.

Leave after the delivery is called as Maternity leave.

a government employed Deaf teacher delivered a baby in December 2020.
She asked the Principal for her 6 months maternity leave.
The principal refused saying that only 3 months would be given after which she has to resume duty.
The lady was shocked but had to give in to the Principal's orders.
She had always heard that maternity leave was for 6 months but wondered why she was only given 3 months.
She let go of the issue and resumed office after 3 months of delivery.
One other Deaf person, Sonu Verma - sign name - is the President of the Deaf Government Employee Welfare Association.
Verma working in ITI and the deaf lady lived in the same locality.
The lady met Verma and informed him that she was given on 3 months maternity leave.
Verma said that the rule is of 6 months and offered to help her.
Along with all the legal documents and a letter from the association
requesting the school to increase the Deaf woman's maternity leave to 6 months on humanitarian grounds.
The Principal refused to accept the letter from the association as it was an internal matter.
Principal said that their decision is final.
The Deaf lady was devastated by their blatant refusal and went back to Verma.
Sonu Verma then wrote a letter to the Haryana Governor who was also the head of the school.
He explained the situation and told them to not oppress the Deaf by giving 3 month maternity leave. He stated the law says ML should be for 6 months.
However, there was no response from them.
They then wrote to the State Disability Commissioner of Haryana.
The Disabilty Commissioner replied and even agreed to the request.
The State Disability Commissioner's name is Raj Kumar Makkad
& he presides over the State Disability Commissioner Court.
In a letter the commissioner ordered that the lady be given 3 more months of maternity leave.
He also reprimanded the principal for manipulating the leave rules when it is the government who pays the salary.
Sonu said the school did not allow him to interfere saying it is an internal matter, but then who will help the Deaf woman?
This is why Sonu intervened to get her justice.
The judge ruled in favour of Verma.
The court ordered the school to pay the Deaf lady 3 months salary of about Rs 1.25 lakh
and also permit her to avail the 3 month balance leave.
The order was to be impemented within 3 months failing which strict action would be taken against the Principal.
The Principal panicked and apologized. They agreed to pay the salary and sanctioned the leave.
The school promised henceforth they would not discriminate against any person with disability
and would follow the government rules.

Every year a large number of devotees visit the temple to see the gorwing Shiv Ling.

According to a 29 June 2022 news report, one such case was reported in Thailand.
Over there a father and son went to a doctor for a swab test, and both tested positive for COVID-19.
Both were placed under isolation.
They also had a cat and the cat was taken to a veterinary doctor.
As the cat was being swabbed, it sneezed in the face of a veterinary surgeon.
The surgeon was wearing a face mask and gloves. The cat tested positive and was in isolation like the rest of the family.
Three - four days later, she developed a fever, cough & sniffles.
She wondered how she fell sick when she wasn't in contact with infected persons.
Genetic analysis confirmed both the vet and the cat had the same variant. It proved the cat infected the doctor.
Researchers said she got infected because the doctor was wearing a face mask and gloves but had no eye protection. This is how the virus entered her body.
A minor lapse led to an infection.
However, research suggests cat-human transmissions are probably rare.
A word of caution, people must care for household pets who are infected and maintains safe distance.

You may have seen many children who are born able bodied but as they grow up they develop many forms of physical disabilities
This is because they have missed their polio vaccines.
This is why the government constantly advertises polio vaccines by creating informative adverts on TV, railway stations,
they even go door to door asking if children have been vaccinated, these children to get vaccinated every 3 months upto the age 5.
This is so that the child grows up healthy.
Polio is also known as Poliomyelitis.
Polio is a very dangerous illness. Let me tell you its origins.
Polio infection spreads when contaminated water mixes with drinking water.
Using unclean utensils to drink water, contaminated food or using contaminated water,
when an infected person defecates in the open,
or after defecation when the person does not wash hands properly and comes in contact with others,
these are the different ways the infection can spread.
Also when children play outdoors, upon returning home they don't wash hands and eat food. This can also cause an infection.
The virus then attacks the nervous system & the spinal cord, which then cause physical disabilities.
It can also cause paralysis of the body.
This is why the Indian government encourages polio vaccines to protect children's health.
According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, there are three wild types of poliovirus.
As of 2020, Type 1 affects two countries— Pakistan and Afghanistan.
Type 2 virus was virus detected in India in 1999. Type 2 was then declared eradicated in September 2015.
Type 3 was declared eradicated in October 2019.
However, Type 1 still there is Pakistan & Afghanistan.
IPV is a polio vaccine adminitered by an injection. It is used in the USA.
The Polio vaccine drops are called OPV is used widely across the world and in India.
In the USA the IPV vaccine is used and in India & the world the OPV is used.
India started distributing the OPV vaccines from 2 October 1994.
In 1994 immunization programme was launched because India accounted for around 60% of the global polio cases.
Since then the number of infections have reduced.
The last polio case was reported in Howrah, Kolkata in West Bengal on 13 January 2011.
Since then not a single polio case was reported
and India received ‘Polio-free certification’ from the WHO on 27 March 2014 to appluad the immunisation drive.
From 60% of the global infection, to complete eradication, shockingly there has been a resurgance of the polio virus.
The polio virus was found in Kolkata's Metiabruz
While testing one of the sewage, officials were shocked to find the polio virus in the sample.
A  West Bengal Health Department official went through the results and said
it was a "vaccine virus" and not a "wild virus." Both are different.
Wild Virus is the one responsible for spread and infections.
Whereas the ‘vaccine virus’ is an inactive virus. It undergoes genome sequencing to be made into a vaccine.
It can not cause cause infections.
This type of virus is also called VDPV and it is inactive.
Pune's National Institute of Virology also confirmed it to be an inactive virus and that it can not be infectious.
People then breathed a sigh of relief.
West Bengal Director of Health Services (DHS)  Dr. Siddhartha Niyogi said that
the possibility of finding the virus in sewage could be that the virus might have been excreted by a child who received the polio vaccine.
It is only the vaccine virus  not the wild virus. Another reason could be open defecation by children.
There is no possibility of infections.
There is nothing to worry about just be very careful.
Even WHO did genome sequencing and concluded it is a vaccine virus.
It is not wild polio. SO don't worry and take all precautions.

What is Ramsay Hunt Syndrome? Let me tell you about it.
The Ramsay Hunt syndrome is a condition caused by a virus varicella-zoster
that affects the nerves involved in the movements of the face and causes facial paralysis.
Moreover, Varicella-zoster is the same virus that causes shingles in adults.
Varicella-zoster also causes chickenpox in children.
The nerves are inflamed which can cause facial paralysis.
The illness can also cause blistering rashes in the mouth and ear.
Severe symptoms can affect the hearing ability either partially or completely.
Ramsay Hunt syndrome is the second most common cause of facial paralysis.
Delay in diagnosis at the onset of the symptomscan lead to permanent facial paralysis.
Steroid treatment within the first three days of the diagnosis, can give full recovery.
So be vigilant.

It has been announced that helmets will now be compulsory for pillion riders.
The police are not starting this rule immediately. This rule will be effective from 9 June 2022.
This is not a new rule. This law was always around but it was never implemented.
Wearing a helmet has always been compulsory for pillion riders under the Motor Vehicle Act.
Now the law will be strictly implemented from 9 June 2022.
Mumbai Police Commissioner Sanjay Pandey stated that
this rule is already being followed in the entire world and several cities in India as well.
Since it was not being followed in Mumbai we are enforcing it now.
Deputy Commissioner of Police for traffic Raj Tilak Roshan said,
“After analyzing data it was found that in accidents the rider would be safe but the pillion riders always suffered injuries.
That is why it has been made compulsory for the pillion to wear helmets.
If the rider does not wear the helmet, they will be fine Rs 500.
If the rider and the pillion are not wearing helmets, then both will be fined Rs 500 each.
The rider's license will also be suspended for 3 months.
There are many rules which have to be implemented.
Many are supportive of this rule whereas some says uneven roads are causing accidents
People should stop buying helmets from roadside shops instead buy ISI certified helemets.
Please remember to wear helemets from 9 June 2022.

The United Kingdom health authorities have now confirmed a case of monkeypox.
Let me tell you about it.
Monkeypox is a virus.
It is a member of the same family of viruses as chicken pox and smallpox.
It is much less severe and chances of infection are low as compared to coronavirus.
Let me tell you how it is identified.
Initial symptoms of Monkeypox include headaches, aching muscles, back pain,
fever and boils on parts of the body.
Monkeypox can be spread from an infected person to another person
through broken skin and blood,
through the respiratory tract or through the eyes, nose or mouth.
The infection usually clears up on its own and lasts between 14 and 21 days.
Monkeypox can sometimes be more severe and cause deaths.
It can also be spread by contact with infected animals such as rats, monkeys and squirrels.
People need to be careful.
In UK four cases of Monkeypox were found.
Two of the infected patients had returned from their travel to Nigeria.
The third was a healthcare worker who got infected from one of the patients.
Details of the fourth case are not known. These were the first identified cases.
The Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said
that it is different and better than coronavirus
but they will track the passengers who might have come in contact with the infected patients.
Monkeypox is not as transmissible and severe as coronavirus.
It is treated at home. The rash becomes a scab, which later falls off. The lesions can cause scarring.
Like Chickenpox, the infection usually lasts between 14 and 21 days.
There is vaccination for smallpox but there is no vaccination against Monkeypox.
The vaccination against smallpox has been proven to be 85% effective in preventing monkeypox.
Monkeypox occurs mostly in central and west African countries .
The introduction of a new viruses like corona, omicron, delta, tomato virus etc every now and then is definitely fearsome
but you need to be careful.

But there is one girl who is severely allergic to water and has to avoid it.
She won't be able to survive if she uses water.
That's so weird! Let me tell you about this shocking story.
Abigail Beck is from Arizona, USA.
She is 15 year old had an allergy because of water.
3 years back she started getting rashes after drinking water.
Drinking water made her vomit and taking a shower gave her rashes all over the body.
When she cries, her own tears make her face itch badly and her skin to turns red.
During rains, even a single drop of water makes her body burn and itch.
Since 3 years neither she nor the doctors could find a reason for this.
Doctors initially thought something was wrong with the water in her house or skin lotions she used.
However, symptoms got worse over time.
Finally last month after severe allergic reactions, doctors were able to find that she was allergic to water!
She was shocked as surviving without water is very difficult.
Abigail has to use alternatives as she cannot drink water.
She drinks pomegranate juice or energy drinks like red bull, monster, etc.
Though it's not healthy but she can only drink these. She cant have water because she is allergic to it.
She will have to continue drinking these
however it is difficult as whenever she goes to buy the energy drink, she has to check the label for water content.
Every drink has water. She has to carefully check and get something which has no water.
It is very difficult to get such a product. Shocking!

When she takes bath, her body burns and it feels like someone has poured "acid" on her skin.
She is so allergic that she gets painful rashes whenever she takes bath.

It is very difficult.
During rains, she has to cover up herself with layers of jackets and clothing so that no water touches her skin.
Because a drop of water will also cause allergy.
It is such a difficult condition, but she is not the only one.

Abigail had to educate doctors about her condition and the treatment.

Unconsensual, forceful sex with a woman is termed as 'Rape' by the law.
You all know this.
Another act called POCSO deals with sexual acts committed against children.
Like that there are various laws & punishments to deal with different kinds of offences.
Now what about a married couple?
Say the husband is drunk and extremely aroused to have sex and the wife refuses. To refuse is her right.
The husband then forcefully has sex with her. This is called 'Marital Rape'.
Marital Rape is a kind of rape which is a forceful sexual act done with a husband or a wife.
Sexual acts must be consensual. When done without the spouse's consent it is marital rape.
However, there are no laws for Marital Rape in India.
Despite multiple demands, the courts have been very hesitant to do anything.
India already has a large number of Rape cases which are later recognised as fake cases.
If marital rape is criminalised spouses can make false allegations of rape against their partners. This would lead to chaos.
Hence making a decision is very difficult.
So what is the latest debate? Keep watching.
However as per the Section 375 of the IPC
defines various acts that is done without a woman's consent, by force, fraud, or threat as rape.
The same section has an exception numbered 2.
It says sexual act performed by a man on his own wife is not rape. A man has the right to have sex with his wife it can never be called rape.
What a contradiction! In both cases it's forceful, so should be called rape.
When a person forcefully has sex with an unmarried it called rape.
So if a drunk husband forces his wife to have sex against her wishes, then it is not rape?
The argument was that sex without consent of married couple is not rape while some say that it should be considered as rape. That is why the decision is pending.
The Delhi High Court was hearing arguments on the same.
However yesterday the verdict was announced by them, but it was split.
The two-judge bench comprised of justices Rajiv Shakdher and C Harishankar.
While Justice Rajiv Shakdher supported the criminalisation of 'marital rape', Justice C Harishankar opposed it.
Now, the matter will have to be heard by the Supreme Court. The final decision will be theirs.
However earlier decisions on more such cases have been given by different high courts which are also contrasting in nature.
In August 2021, the Chhattisgarh High Court
has let a man free of marital rape by saying that sexual intercourse between husband & wife is not rape even if it is by force or against the wishes of the wife.
However in March this year, the Karnataka High Court,
was hearing a petition filed by a man seeking to remove charges of rape by his wife.
The court said that like people get a license to ride bikes, marriage is not a license to rape someone.
While Chhattisgarh High Court had dropped the charges. Now let's see what the Supreme Court decides.

The World Press Freedom Index ranks countries from 1-180

The ranking is based on these factors.

It actually means Reporters Without Borders. They are ones who give the ratings.
The country which is on first position is the one that gives a lot of freedom to its media.
Whereas the country which is ranked last on 180th position has the least freedom given to the press.
This is how the ranking is done every year.
The result is released on 3rd May every year since 2002,
It is released on 3rd May as that day is also celebrated as the World Press Freedom Day.

BSL is British Sign Language. It is used by the Deaf Community in the United Kingdom by England, Wales & Scottland.
However there was no law recognising BSL and there were many campaigns for it.
Rosie Cooper is a child of Deaf parents and is a member of Parliament in the House of Commons.
Rosie proposed a bill to recognise BSL in June 2021.
The bill was proposed in the House of Commons which is like India's Lok Sabha. The bill was then discussed by the members.
The BSL bill was then introduced by Christopher Holmes to the House of Lords which is like Rajya Sabha on March 2022.
In the House of Lords, at the 3rd reading of the bill on 27 April 2022 the bill was passed.
The BSL Bill has now become the BSL Act.
After years of campaigning people were very happy that BSL was finally recognised.
Generations of the Deaf community will leave hassle free because of this Act.
The Bill after receiving Royal Assent will be passed as the BSL Act 2022
Like in India the final approval after the bill is passed in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, the President approves it.
Its the same in UK. Now people are very happy.
Now that the BSL Act was recognised, let me tell you what will happen:
1. Recognise British Sign Language as a language of England, Wales and Scotland.
2. It will ensure that all government departments use of British Sign Language like banks, railways, aiport, etc.
As per the law interpreters and accessibility will have to be given.
3. Now that BSL is recognised, the government has to make guidelines,
to provide BSL interpreters for news channels, to have BSL in schools,
and various other forms of accessibility. All this has to be done henceforth.
David Buxton, Chair of the BDA said he is happy that after 19 years of campaigning, BSL has been recognised.
The Deaf Community is very pleased to have achieved their goals.
BSL is Britain’s fourth indigenous language, after English, Welsh, and Scottish Gaelic.
It is only right that BSL be accorded equal status and recognition.
However a lot of work is needed by the government to provide accessibility in schools and other areas.
The BDA looks forward to working hand in hand with the Government to provide accessibility to the Deaf Community.
151,000 people of Great Britain use BSL. To give them accessibility the Act was passed.
If it weren't for the Deaf, this would never happen.
They campaigned and demanded to make this happen. Their unity is commendable!
BSL Act will help those interested in learning the language, interpreters, bilingual professionals and allies of the Deaf community.
This time the Deaf Community will not feel excluded from the society.
They will all receive accessibility.
Now that BSL has been recognised I hope countries like India, Sri Lanka, etc. who are campaigning for their Sign Languages get inspired by the UK.
MP Rosie Cooper said, Now that the BSL Act has been passed, the government will have to quickly complete their tasks.

Since BSL is finally recognised people will not face any barriers.

As you all know this is a passport.
Countries around the world like USA, UK, Pakistan, India, etc all have Passports.
A passport is needed when a person of a particular country - say India -
wants to fly to another country. That time a passport must be shown to prove your identity.
Passports are given to citizens by their respective governments.
Whether you go by road, cycle, or even walk to cross a country's border,
you will be asked to show your passport. This is mandatory.
It is not optional and no other ID but a passport will be acceptable.
Even while travelling by ship you need a passport.
But do you know around the world there are some weird facts related to passports that you probably didn't know.
Are you excited to know? Let me tell you.
1. After taking a passport picture, If you get a face tattoo inspired by your friends,
then your prior passport will not be accepted and the passport will be rejected.
If you get any facial surgery to alter the look of your face, then you will be asked to get a new passport. How strange!
2. For the passport picture you are not allowed to wear military, government, school or any kind of uniform.
You can only wear your normal clothes and uniforms will not be allowed.
Sunglasses or hats are also not allowed.
Girls are not allowed to cover their face. The face should be clearly visible.
3. Various countries have their own passport.
Can you get a world passport?
Instead of your respective passports, can you show a world passport?
a Washington D.C.-based nonprofit in the USA, have collaborated with these countries, to provide a world passport to all those wanting visiting there.
With Indian, American, British passport, you have to apply for visas and complete formalities for certain countries.
With world passport you can visit any of these countries.
4. Do you think passports started 50-100 years ago?
No! It was started a very long time back in the 1200s by the British monarch King Henry the fifth.
He introduced this concept, to make it easier to prove his nationality and identity when traveling to foreign lands.
During that time, passports were very different. They were just papers which identified that the person was a UK national.
Since then we are using the passport. It's been almost 800 years for foreign travel.
King Henry started this concept. How surprising!
Here is another unbelievale fact. Let me tell you this surprising pointer.
The word “Passport” has also been mentioned in the ancient religious text of Christians ”The Holy Bible" and till date it is being used.
5. You all know that you, me, the PM, President, any official, MLA, billionaires, or anyone,
must have a passport. From a layman to the most famous actor, politician, president, PM everyone must have a passport.
However 1 person does not need a passport to travel.
British Queen Elizabeth ll is the only person in the world who does not need a passport but british citizens need a passport.
Why such a weird rule? Since passports in Britain are issued under the name of the queen,
she doesn't need a passport. She has different documents for travel. Strange!
What about the Queen's family? Like her spouse, children, grandchildren, etc.? They don't need passports?
Everyone in her family except the Queen need a passport. How strange!
6. There are certain passports that do not require a visa to travel by any mode of transport.
Like that UAE passport is the strongest and you can travel to 179 countries without a visa.
However Indian passport stands on the 83rd Position, where you can visit 63 Countries without a Visa. While UAE is the strongest.
7. Do you have a passport? I have. I am sure many of you have a passport.
Can you have a passport after your death?
Once you are dead you can not have right?
Only when you are alive you can travel. Once you are dead there is no need for passport.
Now here is a very strange and unbelievable fact.
You know about the Mummies found in the sarcophagus in Egypt.
Only the monarchy in Egypt were mummified.
It was not for the commoners. When the royals died, they were made into mummied and all their most loved items like
glass tumblers, chair, bed, gold, and all their possessions were named and kept with them in the pyramid.
The Egyptians believed that they would take all their possessions with them in the afterlife.
The mummy of Ramses ll was transported from France in the 70s to a museum.
When the Mummy was transported by the Egyptian authorities, they were asked for a passport as Ramses was an Egyptians.
Even though he was dead king, they had to make one. So the government made a passport for Ramses II.
This was how he was transported to the French museum.
How strange!
8. Passports have one image. Our parents, sibblings, etc. have different passports.
A family passport with a group image is not possible right?
Well it is possible! In Britain, in the year 1915, there were family photographs allowed on the passport. It was known as ''Family Passport''.
As long as the faces of all the members were clearly visible, their poses did not matter.
I am sure you are amazed by these 8 surprising facts about passports. How interesting to learn this general knowledge.
