So here's what happened.
On 15th April 2022 9:45pm, there were two long-distance trains Gadag Express which runs
between CSMT and Gadag Junction, Karnataka
and Chalukya Puducheri Express which runs between Dadar and Pondicherry
The Chalukya Express was moving slowly after leaving Dadar.
Gadag Express which had left CSMT and was going towards Dadar
came on the same track at a speed, ramming into the rear coaches of Chalukya Express.

as it tried to switch tracks even when the red light is given and collided with the train.
Here is an interesting fact. Mumbai local trains almost never had such collision accidents. It is extremely rare.
This is because of a technology called AWS that works through a series of magnets and sensors.
Let me give you an example. At home and in the office,
there are smoke detectors that detect smoke and sprinkles water.
Similarly the AWS sensor in trains does not allow the train to jump a red light.
This is why locals run without a hitch.
Once a local train had collided but it was found that the AWS was faulty and the motorman switched the sensor off. This is why the train collided.
The Indian Railways said the AWS is functioning well in Mumbai local trains but the Railways are working on installng them in Express trains.

You must be aware about different types of thefts like gold, wallet, car etc. It is not new.
Can you imagine a bridge used for commuting being stolen?
You would not believe it, right?  You may find it hard to believe that someone can steal a bridge.
But this has actually happened in Bihar. Let me telll you about it.
In Bihar's Rohtas district's Amiyawar village there was a 60-foot-long and 12 feet high bridge.
The bridge was built over the Arrah canal.
The bridge was built in 1972 and was being used by vehicles for commuting.
But later it was declared dangerous and locals started taking a nearby concrete bridge.
So this old bridge was not being used.
The villagers wanted the authorities to remove the bridge from there as it was just laying abandoned.
The villagers then agreed and submitted an application to the concerned department for dismantling the bridge on 5th April 2022.
Some people came with earthmover machines and gas cutters to demolish the bridge.
When the villagers asked them who they were, they said they were ordered by the government officials to bring down the bridge.
Villagers thought that the government acted quickly upon their letter and had sent the people.
Those people had actually lied and in reality were thiefs or smugglers
The bridge was actually a steel bridge.
Metal is very valuable.
That is why they dismantled the whole bridge.
The villagers were not aware and these people posed as government officials.
Later the villagers thought of letting the authorities know that the bridge had been dismantled.
So they went to the authorities and informed them that work was done.
The authorities were shocked that the bridge was already brought down.
They quickly rushed to the spot and saw that the bridge was completely taken down in just 2 days!
They had fled with truck loads of metal scrap. Now there was nothing left there.
Arshad Kamal Shamshi, a junior engineer from the government department said,
I can't believe it. Villagers informed that some people, posing as the officials came to the bridge.
They didn't have government orders to carry out the work.
They fooled everyone.
People would wonder why this steel bridge was so valued?
Selling metal scrap is a lucrative business in India.
That is why people posed as officials and uprooted the bridge.
A complaint was lodged at Nasriganj police station and the police started the investigation.
A police officer said that it was a gang and some members have been identified
they will be arrested and questioned.
How shocking that something like this could happen in India! Heist is the conspiracy to commit a theft without bringing to anyones notice.
Some said that like "Money Heist", "Bihar bridge heist” should be title for a new Netflix series.
India is not the first one. Such incidents have happened all around the world.
In 2004, a 36-foot steel bridge in Ukraine was stolen.
In 2011 thieves removed $100,000 worth of steel bridge in Pennsylvania, US.
In 2012, thieves stole a bridge in broad daylight in the Czech Republic.
Now the same has happened in Bihar.
My god! In India people come up with different ideas to commit burglary of steel which is why there are more thefts.

Albert Khoury, a 54-year-old, was working as a cement finisher for the city of Chicago, USA.
He began to experience back pain, sneezing, chills, cough and mucus in 2020.
At first, he assumed it was Covid, but called his doctor when he coughed up blood.
They discovered he did not have COVID but stage 1 lung cancer.
Khoury was shocked as he does not smoke.
By July 2020, his cancer progressed to stage 2, and, despite several rounds of chemotherapy, kept growing to stage 3 and stage 4.
Doctors told him there was no chance of survival and there can be no surgery.
But his sister, who had heard about the cancer research at Northwestern Medicine in Chicago, urged him to get another opinion.
Khoury came under the care of oncologist at Northwestern who tried other cancer-fighting treatments.
But his health kept declining. He ended up in the ICU with pneumonia and sepsis.
That’s when Dr Ankit Bharat got involved. He was the first to perform a double lung transplant on a woman in 2020.
Generally, when a person has stage 4 lung cancer, it is very difficult to perform a lung transplant
as cancer has already spread across the body.
Because Albert's cancer was confined only to his chest, they were confident to perform the surgery.
On 25 September 2021, after two weeks of waiting, a match for Albert's lungs was found.
When they started the surgery they removed his old lungs.
They had to be careful not to spill any cancer into his chest cavity or bloodstream.
The surgery lasted 6 hours. The doctors removed his old lungs & put the new lungs in his body and the surgery was successful.
Sometimes after a lung transplant surgery, the body can reject the lung.
At this time the lungs stop working.
The surgery was successful. But doctors had to take a lot of care and he was put on a lot of medication.
He had to wear oxygen masks to support his breathing and he had to take a lot of care.
Now there is some good news, yesterday on 24 March 2022, the doctors announced
that Khoury is now fit and fine, is leading a normal life and is enjoying himself.
Khoury said, ‘I am very happy and can't believe this. Doctors told me I would not survive.
My life went from zero to 100 because of these doctors. Thank you Dr Ankit!
You didn't see this smile on my face for over a year, but now I can't stop smiling.’
Doctors around the world are shocked and people with similar lung problems now have hope of a lung transplant.

Shockingly, last week India fired missile accidentally from the Indian side into an area in Pakistan on 9th March 2022.

The Ministry of Defence said in a statement, "On 9th  March 2022,
while the routine maintenance of the missile was going on
there was a technical problem because of which the missile got accidentally fired and landed into Pakistan.
Indian government regrets the error.
It is also a relief that there has been no loss of life due to the accident.
Pakistani military spokesperson Major-General Babar Iftikhar said that
a "high-speed flying object" originated from the Indian city of Sirsa, in Haryana state
crashed 100km near the city of Mian Channu, Pakistan.
If the warhead would have been on the missile, Pakistan would surely have retaliated as it would then have exploded.
But there was no warhead on the missile so it did not detonate. Everyone was safe.
But Pakistan's foreign office said it had summoned India's office in Islamabad
and said that it was an unprovoked violation of its airspace.
India said the incident is deeply regrettable and was not done purposely. It was by mistake.
Pakistan said it could have endangered civilian lives.
Pakistan could have responded to India.
Pakistan has proposed a joint probe into the incident to establish facts since the missile had landed into Pakistani territory
as it could have risked civilian lives.
India felt very sorry about it. This is the first time something like this happened.
Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday said
The missile landed in Pakistan without any provocation by Pakistan.
Pakistan could have responded but it observed restraint.
Be careful of such violations in future." India was relieved.
Pakistan warned India to be mindful such negligence and take effective measures to avoid such recurrence in future.
Sushant Singh, a senior staff at the Center for Policy Research said,
It's a relief that Pakistan understood it was a mistake. They have shown great maturity.
We have been lucky this time. We should not make the mistake again thinking we will be lucky every time.”

their hands were tied at their backs and they were walking in a queue.

According to Indian government data
at least 75% of the 277.1 million vehicles in India are two-wheelers.
In Delhi alone, out of the 13 million registered vehicles, at least 7.3 million are two-wheelers.
According to government data in 2020,
Over 2,700 children below the age of 14 and over 14,000 children below the age of 18 died in road accidents.
In 2016, the Center amended the Central Motor Vehicles Act to make it mandatory
for children above 4 years to wear helmets while traveling on two-wheelers.
Last year since October, the Union transport ministry had asked for feedback from the public on the issue.
The ministry then issued a final notification again amending the Central Motor Vehicles Act on 15th February 2022.
However, it stated that these rules will come into effect after one year which means they will be implemented from February 15, 2023.
So what is the new rule? Let me tell you.
The new rule states that children between the ages of 9 months and 4 years,
riding pillion on two-wheelers will have to wear a helmet
and a safety harness attached to the rider.
If you don't wear harness there are chances of falling. In order to avoid any incident, the new rule was created.
Safety harness should be of good quality, water proof, protect from air pollution, etc
It should be lightweight and there should also be a lightweight helmet for children.
They also announced that the speed limit for two-wheelers with children on them will have to be a maximum of 40km per hour.
Any violation of the rules will invite a fine of ₹1,000 and a suspension of driver’s license for three months.
People asked why the rule will be implemented after a year? Why not now?
Transport officials said that
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has specified rules
that for children it should be lightweight helmet and vest, adults can wear heavy helmets but not children.
Once the rule are created and implemented by the BIS
then the companies will start manufacturing as it will take time its not ready yet.
“Till the time European standards are to be followed in India.
Once the BIS make the rules then we will follow Indian rules.
Piyush Tewari, founder and chief executive of SaveLIFE Foundation said,
this is a great idea. It is working to improve road safety.
He said that each day, at least 30 children are killed on India’s roads.
Adults should be very careful while riding with pillion chilren to avoid any accident.

The Kurumbachi hills are 6km away from Cheradu, Palakkad, Kerala and it is a popular trekking spot.
The Kerala Forest Department had earlier warned visitors of the risks in trekking as the mountain is very steep.
R Babu aged 23 and his friends climbed up the Kurumbachi hills on 7 February 2022 morning.
After reaching the summit, when they started their downward trekk,
he slipped and fell. Instead of falling of the moutain, he fell into a tiny gorge within the hill.
Due to the steep nature of the mountain, there was no out.
There was a huge valley on one end and Babu was stuck in the tiny gorge.
Babu's friends used sticks and ropes but they were unable to rescue him.
They then reached down the hill and informed the cops about Babu's situation.
A unit of the Kerala Fire and Rescue and the police reached the spot.
They were trying to figure out how to resuce Babu but the mountain was too steep.
They then called for a helicopter but that failed as it was unable to get close to the steep mountain.
The helicopter had to return because of this.
That’s when Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan intervened and ordered the Indian Army,
to send a team that specialized in mountaineering. Even the NDRF arrived at the spot.
However this was not an easy task. Babu had a tough time.
He was stuck on the mountain for 45 hours. Whoa this is really dangerous.
The Kerala police & fire brigade were waiting at the foot of the mountain.
In the evening when they were figuring out ways of rescue.
The team lit flambeaus to keep wild animals away during the night.
The rescue operations went on for 2 days on 7th & 8th February. It was a very tedious task.
When the army reached the spot, they used a special drone
to capture videos and understand the terrain of the mountain where Babu was stuck.
They saw that he was asking for water.
On Wednesday 9th February 2022 early morning,
the army used thick ropes to reach the spot and gave him water.
He was drinking water after 45 hours.
Babu's family members and friends had gathered at the foot of the hills with prayers to get him back unharmed.
After the army gave him his first sip of water in 45 hours, he gratefully gulped it down.
News channels said that while Babu was stuck in the gorge,
he suffered a lot as the heat was searing and terrible during the day. In the evening it turned windy and chilly.

they took him along with the rope and they reached the top of the mountain.

On 1st February 2022, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman at the parliament,
announced the budget for financial year 2022-2023.
The Finance Minister's budget has keypoints that
give a boost to the country's development over the next 25 years – from India at 75 to India at 100.
This marked the 10th annual budget of Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led central government
and the fourth by Sitharaman as in-charge of the Finance Ministry.
The new budget has garnered both praise and criticism.
Here are all the key takeaways from Budget 2022.
1. Imitation jewellery, headphones, earphones, toys like remote controlled cars,
X-ray machine, solar energy panels, etc that are imported to India,
will face a hike in custom duty. Whether you import one piece or multiple pieces hike in duty is applicable on all.
2. Factories of parts of mobile phones like covers, screen gaurds, chargers, memory cards, etc.
will recieve duty concessions. This will result in cheaper mobiles.
3. Diamonds and gemstones will soon become cheaper as customs duty on such products has been reduced to 5%.
Diamonds that are cut but not polished are called simply sawn diamonds.
These diamonds will attract zero custom duty.
4. Currently you are all using 4G phones.
The government has announced that 5G services will soon be launched.
They will be first launched in major Indian cities like Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru,
Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Chennai, etc.
5. Currently there are Income Tax slabs which decide a person's taxation.
No change to Income Tax slabs was announced in the Budget speech, it would be same as last year.
Tax deduction limit for state government employees post retirement will be increased to 14% from 10%.
If you have made any errors while filling ITR for the previous 2 years,
taxpayers have now been allowed to correct errors and file updated Income Tax returns within two years of the concerned assessment year.
6. Under Section 80DD of the income tax,
Suppose a parent creates an insurance policy for their disabled child,
then after a certain period say 10 or 20 years, the child becomes the beneficiary.
The parents get tax deduction on this Insurance.
Secondly the beneficiary will recieve tax deduction on the lumsum amount, only if their parents are above the age of 60.
Thirdly, the disabled beneficiary will also get tax deduction on the lumsum amount in case of their parents death.
7. Sitharaman announced that a digital currency like Bitcoin, will be introduced by the RBI in the FY 2022-2023
Under this scheme, a 30% tax will be levied on the sale or acquisition of the virtual assets.

Many Deaf people were encouraged to apply for the card saying they would get monthly payments from the government.
Don't fall for this misunderstanding. This card is not for people with disability. This is very different.
Let me give you a clear explanation.
Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the E-Shram portal on 26 August 2021.
It is for applicants from the unorganized sectors.
The application will require Aadhar card, bank account, details of their skill,
their job details, qualifications, etc. Once all of this is submitted, the card is formed.
The E-Shram card consists of a 12-digit UAN number. This is a permanent card.
You may now wonder if you are a part of the unorganised sector.
Let me clearly explain the meaning of the unorganised sector.
You must have seen people such house helps, drivers, manual labourers, truck drivers,
tea vendors, fast food vendors, vegetable, fruit  hawkers, shoe shinner, cobbler and many others.
These people are not protected.
Do they get pension? No. They don't get many such benefits.
Workers in factories are fired without notice
but government jobs offer a lot of security. You have to punch in and punch out.
There is a steady salary, post-retirement benefits, insurance, provident fund, etc.
This is not called the unorganised sector.
Those who's jobs do not provide security are a part of the unorganised sector.
The government has asked these people to apply for the E-Shram card.
Remember this is not for the Deaf.
However Deaf individual who are part of the unorganised sector like househelp, tea vendors, shoeshiner,
clothes presser, etc. can be helped to apply for the card.
Remeber this. Well to do Deaf individuals with government jobs need not apply. Don't get confused.
The registration under the e-SHRAM portal is totally free and the registration is done at Common Service Centres (CSCs).
You will have to attach your Aadhar card, bank acount, etc. Remember the government said its free of cost.
The immediate benefit that an e-Shram cardholder will get
is accident insurance coverage if the worker dies or suffer a permanent disability.
They have to show the card to make the claim of Rs 2 lakh.
Those with minor injuries will be given Rs 1 lakh.
There are many such benefits.
Why was the E-Shram card started?
Remeber during the lockdown, migrant workers had to walk by home to their homes?
That time the government wanted to help but they did not have any data.
How would the government help so many people?
This is why the E-Shram card was started to prepare a database of such people.
Till now 20 crore people have applied and more are expected.

Israel has a bizarre divorce law. The world is shocked to know about this law

Noam Huppert, an Australian, was in love with an Israeli national & married her.

His ex-wife had filed a case in the Israeli court seeking money support for their children.
The court gave a ‘stay of exit’ order to him which means that he cannot leave the country.
The court ordered, Huppert to pay monthly to both of his children until they turn 18.
He must pay 5,000 shekels that is around Rs. 1 lakh 20 thousand a month for each of his two children till they turn 18
As in Israel the laws in favour of women are very strong.

So, Huppert has to pay for both his children. It is shocking for him.
The court order unclear if he can pay the entire sum in advance to lift the stay of exit order, that is why is still stuck there.
The court has extended its order and he is banned from leaving Israel.
You will be shocked to know the date that the court has given him.
It is 31st December. You maybe thinking it will be 2022, or 2030 or 2050
The court order is till 31st December 9999.
Oh my god! Shocking! It isn't 8 years. It is 8000 years.
Shocking, the man has been ordered to not leave Israel for 8000 years.
Huppert is very stressed and told an Australian news agency,

so that the world can take notice of this and maybe help in making the law less stringent and allow the men to go back.

A senior citizen, Peter Myaliparampil had filed a case in the Kerala High Court
stating that he does not agree to PM Modi's image on the 2 vaccine certificates. The reason for this is
that according to Peter he had paid for the vaccines himself.
The certificate also includes his private details like name, Aadhar card number, etc.
He said that Modi's image on the certificates is an invasion of his privacy. This is why he did not agree to it
and filed a complaint.
Justice Kunhikrishnan said, 'Are you ashamed of PM Modi?
What is your problem? He did not elect himself as the PM Modi was elected to power by the people of India.
So what's the harm if his image is on the certificate? Be proud of his hard work.
Advocate Ajit Joy, appearing for the complainant said,
There are Presidents, Prime Ministers, across the world.
They do not put their image on vaccine certificates. Then why is India doing this?
The judge said, "They may not be proud of their PMs, we are proud of our PM.
We may have different political views, but he is still our PM and his image will be there in the certificates.
However the lawyer stressed that the certificate was a "private space" and the image should be removed.
The argument continued. The judge said, "There are more than 100 crore people in India and they haven't complained about the certificates.
Then why have you complained? What's your problem?
Advocate Joy said that to be proud of one's PM was a personal choice.
Its a personal choice to like or dislike the PM.
Also it is not allowed to put the image on the certificate because of the Supreme Court's rules.
For example when politicians create advertisements and campaigns prior to elections for ministerial posts they need to use their personal funds.
They can not use the tax payer's money which the Central Government collects.
As the tax money is to be used for India's development like building roads, bridges, hospitals, schools, etc.
It is not meant for political campaigns.
Similarly, Modi's image on the certificate is inappropriate.
As they can influence people to vote for him in the elections.
The central government opposed the plea saying it was a publicity stunt.
The court said it will examine whether the plea has any merits and if not, it will dispose of the matter.

However, the chopper crashed enroute!
They were travelling in the IAF’s Mi 17 V5 helicopter which has been prone to accidents in the past.
After the shocking crash it was revealed that 13 people had died.
The only survivor is Varun Singh SC with serious injuries is currently under treatment at a military hospital Coonoor.
The pilot Prithvi Singh Chauhan also passed away. Their deaths are extremely saddening.

In Maharashtra's Ahmednagar there is a small village named Shani Shingnapur
where there is famous temple dedicated to God Shani's 5 feet tall idol.
This is a very famous tourist attraction.
Here is an interesting fact. In Shani Shingnapur the shops and homes do not have a door or lock.
There are no locks even inside the house!
There are no lockers for gold jewellery and cash. Everything is completely open. How shocking!
When stores finish business for the day, they don't even close the shutter.
Everything is open. People leave their homes unlocked and anyone can enter.
However, there is not a single case of theft as they strongly believe in Lord Shani's stone idol
who is the God of Saturn which is the sixth planet. Isn't interesting!
Isn't it unbelievale that there isn't a single theft whenever everything is open.
Let me tell you an interesting story.
Legend has it that nearly 400 years ago, a black stone landed on the banks of the Panasnala River when it started overflowing.
This is the same idol of lord Shani.
When a local shepherd saw the stone, he prodded the slab with a sharp rod, ‘blood' started oozing from it.
The shepherd was confused as to how a stone could bleed when it was not human.
He ignored it and went home. Later that night, Lord Shani appeared in his dreams,
and said the stone was his idol. Lord Shani said he wanted to be placed in the village,
so that he can keep a watch on the villagers.
The shepherd agreed and decided to make a beautiful temple for Lord Shani.
However Shani refused and said he wanted to be placed at the centre of the village without any shelter,
so he could look over the village without any hindrances and prevent any mishaps or theft.
Lord Shani said he wanted to be placed at the centre of the village.
He promised to protect the village from any dangers and mishaps.
The next day the shepherd placed the stone in the centre of the village and since then
this belief has prevailed and tourists visit the village.
This is why there isn't a single theft.
If someone dares to steal, they believe they will be punished with a blindness, mental illness, warts, disability, etc.
People believe stealing in the village could lead to 7 years of bad luck.
It could cause many problems such as financial problems, unemployment, etc.
A man who built a door outside his home had an accident the next day.
This is why he removed the door. However some place wood panels to keep dogs and cats out.
However the rest of the door is always open.
Even post offices do not have doors.
After finishing everyone leaves and the office is open.
How shocking! Villagers strongly believe there will be no theft as Lord Shani is watching over them.
People have believed in this for years.
Interestingly, there is a bank called the United Commercial Bank which has a branch in Shani Shingnapur.
All important documents, gold ornaments, etc are left unopened.
Even though it is a bank everything is left open.
It has a glass entrance with a high tech lock that is barely visible. This ensures the bank is safe and also respects the sentiments of the villagers.
However, many villagers now strongly feel that it is time to get rid of the superstition.
So what changed their minds? Until 2010, Shingnapur had not reported any cases of theft
However the next year, gold ornaments worth Rs 70,000 went missing from a home.
People were shocked! That's when people started talking about putting locks.
There have been many other instances of theft and people filed police complaints.
However the police have covered these up because the no-door policy attracts a lot of tourists
which is very good for the local economy. If people knew that the village will have locks,
tourists would not visit as the village would be like any other city and would lose its uniqueness.
To ensure the economy remains unaffected, the superstition continues, even though there are many thefts.

so that necessary arrangements can be made for easy travel.
Don't tell them at the last moment. It is their duty to give accessibility.
Passengers with anxiety issues or blind passengers using service dogs also need to inform the airlines in advance.

Estimates put the population of persons with disabilities in India at 70-100 million.
Yet, it is only a small percentage of the population that has been seen in the mainstream of any aspect of life
Research has shown that the reason for this is the lack of accessibility that stumps development.
Let me tell you the meaning of accessibility.
Whenever a book is published, people enjoy reading it.
However, the Blind can not read it as it is not in Braille. They are excluded and do not receive accessibility.
This is the reason why they can not live a quality life.
The correct form of accessibility for the blind would be books in Braille.
The blind are then at par with other and can navigate through life.
Similarly, even on television new channels, TV serials, etc.
hearing people enjoy listening to the shows but what about the Deaf.
They are unable to understand as the content is not accessible. They are at a disadvantage.
ISL interpretation in such content, will ensure both Deaf and the hearing can understand the video
and lead an equal & quality life.
Similarly even in transport places ramps must be built for people on wheelchair,
ISL notifications in trains regarding cancellations,
braille, and various forms of accessibility must be given so people can live a fair live.
This is done around the world but not in India.
Whenever malls, building, metro, etc. are designed, if you forget people with disability
that means there is no accessibility. This is why the concept of 'Universal Design' must be followed.
Accessibility based on disability will provide fairness for all.
Many architects are completely unaware about Universal Design.
They end up designing projects without thinking it. This is a big problem.
This is why awareness must be created on this.
NCPEDP, in association with Mphasis, instituted an award,
to those who incorporate 'Universal Design'. This is the name of the award and is being awarded since 2010.
The Awards are given under four categories:
CATEGORY A: PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES
CATEGORY B: WORKING PROFESSIONALS
CATEGORY C: COMPANIES/ORGANISATIONS
NCPEDP –Mphasis Javed Abidi Public Policy Awards
We are proud to announce that ISH has won the NCPEDP – Mphasis Universal Design Award in the companies/organisations category!
ISH News has been broadcasting news which can be understood by the Deaf & hearing
as the videos contain subtitles, voice-over and it is 100% accessible and has perfectly applied universal design.
This is why we were given the award. The award was presented to our Founder & CEO Mr Alok Kejriwal.
Our entire team is very grateful to NCPEDP & MPHASIS for the award.
We promise to continue spreading accessibility for all our viewers.

Delhi's NAD - National Association of the Deaf's
President A.S.NARAYANAN has sent an open letter to Prime Minister Modi.
The letter demanded the recognition of Indian Sign Language (ISL) as an official language.
In the letter, NAD praises PM Modi
launching the ISL dictionary which has excited the Deaf Community.
President Narayanan has said that if ISL is not recognised,
Deaf individuals in India would continue to suffer due to lack of accessibility.
They will deprived of their right to information, employment, etc.
They mentioned that the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
mandates that sign language be accorded equal status as other spoken languages.
Also India’s Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016 states
the importance of ISL, stresses that teachers in colleges, schools, universities must use ISL.
It also mandates ISL interpretation on television so that people get clear information.
Inorder to fulfil the above-mentioned mandates, NAD believes ISL needs to be recognised.
If this does not happen there will be no accessibility.
Among the 22 official languages, the association said Dogri language is spoken by 2.3 million people
and Maithili language is spoken by 15 million people in India.
ISL is the mother tongue of 18 million Deaf people in India.
Yet our language remains unrecognized, even when there are so many Deaf individuals in the country.
NAD has written the letter to PM Modi hoping he accepts and makes history.
This would make the Deaf Community very happy.

and click on either the PDF or Word document of the letter sent to PM Modi.

said that data showed the vaccine was successful in preventing Malaria and approved the vaccine.
This is the first Malaria vaccine in the world.

Since June 2021 the Chinese government has strictly rationed the use of electricity in factories, homes, offices, etc.
How shocking!
In some cities the use of ACs and lifts have been banned.
Severe restrictions have been implemented.
You are aware many Indian cities and villages face power cuts for hours.
Now China is experiencing the same with severe electricity rationing.
How shocking! China the world's strongest economy, technology
and gadgets are the cheapest which are exported all over.
So why is such a country rationing its electricity. What is the problem?
Before I tell you something, you will first have to understand
how electricity is made.
Electricity is produced by burning coal in a boiler to produce steam.
The smoke of the coal is released in the open.
The steam produced flows into a turbine, which spins a generator to create electricity
which powers factories, homes, offices, etc.
Watch the video to clearly understand the process.
I hope the video has helped you understand.
Instead of coal China also uses Natural Gas to create electricity.
Natural Gas is an exothermic form of energy which extracted from below the earth's surface
to create electricity in the same process in which coal is used to create electricity.
However the positive is that it is a clean form of energy which does not harm the environment.
Coal on the other hand is extremely harmful to the environment.
However, it is not possible to immediately switch to natural gas.
China currently is heavily dependant on coal and will slowly transition to natural gas.
The largescale mining of coal and extraction of natural gas to generate electricity
is depleting these fossil fuels. This is a huge problem.
Once these resources are gone, there won't be any electricity. Then how will we work?
As these resources reduce, their price will increase.
This is why China is rationing electricity as they are not able to cope with the rising prices.
This is not the case only in China, the same is happening in Europe as well.
China and Europe are worried about the upcoming winters
when heating with the help of electricity will be a necessity.
Which is why the rationing of coals will cause problems.
Here are reasons why the price of coal & natural gas has increased :
1. For more than a year the entire world was on lockdown.
Factories, businesses, etc. were shut and everyone was home. You know about this.
Finally after almost a year and a half the lockdown lifted.
That's when factories ramped up their production leading to rise in need for coal.
That's when the price increases.
2. China is the leader when it comes to manufacturing tech equipment.
They manufacture various gadgets like mobiles, TV, refrigerator, ACs, etc.
They are known to export these items for dirt cheap prices.
These factories run for hours on electricity generated through coals.
It even used natural gas to generate electricity.
Continuous use of coal, will lead to its depletion.
We can not be complacent about this as coal is not formed in day.
It is a natural resource found below the earth's surface and can take hundreds of years to form.
Organic matter will decompose and eventually turn into coal.
Even resources of natural gas are depleting. This is a huge problem.
3. China used to get 90% of their coal from their states.
The remaining 10% was sourced from foreign producers.
However, there is a severe shortage of coal in these states
and they are unable to meet the rising demand as production takes time as coal is a natural resource.
This has caused the electricity crisis.
4. Countries across the world have promised
to reduce missions in their factories to protect the environment and combat climate change.
China has promised to stop the harmful emissions by 2060 and the use of coal.
They are slowly trying to switch to natural gas to achieve their goal.
5. China used to import coal from Australia.
However, they stopped this due to political tensions.
This is another reason for the shortage of coal and electricity crisis.
6. Indonesia and Columbia have been supplying coal to China & Europe.
Heavy rains in these countries affected the production.
In other countries because of the lockdown,
coal mining stopped which is why the production reduced and price increased in China & Europe.
China and Europe’s electricity problem was a blessing to the India.
Earlier a lot of factories in India used to buy coal from foreign countries at cheap rates.
Now that coal prices in foreign countries have increased,
Indian coal producers are being favored by Indian factories, but still the coal stock is limited.
Experts say the price for coal will remain high in the coming months.
Fuel price are increasing in China, Europe and India.
Economies are struggling to handle this.
With the rising prices of coal, governments need to ration their electricity.
If prices continue to rise, factories may shut and the economy will end up in shambles.
This is why the situation needs to be carefully handled.
Lets hope India does not suffer the same fate as China.
Electricity in factories needs to be carefully moderated. So that the economy is safe.

All disability related courses (Hearing Impairment / Visual Impairment VI / Learning Disability etc.)
are managed by Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), New Delhi.
There are many courses like - D.Ed., B.Ed., M.Ed in HI, VI or LD.
There is DTISL - Deaf teacher training course and even Interpreter course.
After doing these courses, the professional is registered with RCI and given a Central Rehabilitation Register (CRR) number.
After which you are permitted to teach.
As per RCI Act, 1992 - RCI registration is mandatory, otherwise there can be punishment / fine.
You all must be knowing that in deaf schools across the country, most teachers are hearing. Why?
This is because many deaf people do not know how to apply and get qualifications to become a RCI certified teacher of deaf.
I will tell you.
You can become RCI certified teacher of deaf in two ways -
For a deaf individual to called a teacher of the deaf, need to complete one of the two RCI approved course.
DTISL is a two year Diploma in Teaching ISL.
After completion of the course, you become a certified teacher.
DTISL course is currently being offered in three institutes in the country :
1. ISLRTC, New Delhi
2. IDBA, Indore
3. HWSPSHI, Panchkula, Haryana
As an ISL Teacher, you can get a job to teach interpreters or to teach deaf students in deaf schools.
PM Modi announced ISL as a language subject,
schools all over the country will now start teaching ISL for which there will be a demand for deaf teachers.
Deaf can study this course and become teachers. So go ahead and apply.
2. If you are interested in teaching various subjects like maths, English, science etc,
then you need to complete a D.Ed. in Special Education (Hearing Impairment)
There are many training institutes in the country which offer D.Ed. in Spl. Ed. (H.I.).
However only hearing people apply as there is no accessibility.
Last year for the first time, in Haryana 25 deaf and 5 hearing people - a total of 30 people applied in a D.Ed. (H.I.) batch.
Teachers knew ISL and interpreters were there for classes where teachers did not know sign language.
After completing D.Ed. in Spl. Ed. (H.I.) one can apply for jobs in deaf schools as teachers from Nursery till Class VIII.
Both courses- DTISL and D.ED / B. Ed (HI) are important.
DTISL helps to you train deaf as well as hearing interpreters.
Whereas B. Ed, D. Ed (HI) helps you to teach subjects such as Science, Maths, English, etc. as bilingual teachers.
Good news, RCI has announced the admission process for 2021,
Deaf who are interested can apply for the teacher training courses.
You need to be 12th pass to apply for these courses.
The cut-off for D.Ed. courses is 50 % in 12th
and the cut off for DTISL course is 45 %.
The admission will start from 31st August and will be till 30 September 2021.
All the information about the course is available on the RCI website.
You can also contact the institutes - ISLRTC, Haryana and IDBA Indore for more guidance and support.

decided to test the quality of all the different brands of honey that are sold in Maharashtra.

In China, a Beijing-based 53 year old veterinarian doctor
was the first person to get infected & die with the Monkey B virus found in Macaques Monkeys.
He got infected because he had dissected two dead Macaques Monkeys for research in early March.

All close contacts of the patient are reported to have tested negative for the virus and are safe from it.
What is the Monkey B virus?
Monkey B virus is a virus that affects only Macaques Monkey's saliva,
brain or spinal cord, urine & feces.
This is how it can be transmitted.
B virus secreted from feces or urine can survive for hours on moist surfaces.
Humans can get infected while a person disects Macaques Monkeys. People must be careful.
A person can get infected if the fluid reaches the eys, nose or mouth.
If such fluids are exposed to broken skin, a person can get infected. Hence, safety must be maintained.
Symptoms may start within one month or could appear in three to seven days.
The first indications of B virus infection are fever and chills,
headaches & muscle ache.
The virus spreads to and causes inflammation of the brain and spinal cord.
It can cause brain damage and damage to the nervous system and death.
Currently, there are no vaccines against B virus infection.
Nuses, doctors & workers exposed to Macaques monkeys are at risk of infection.
Only one case has been documented of an infected person spreading B virus to another person.

There was a woman named Leesamma Joseph in Kerala.
She had a 55% permanent disability. Her form of disability is not known.
Her brother who was working with the Kerala Police, passed away during service.
This is why Joseph was employed in her brother's place on compassionate grounds.
When she wanted to get promoted, Joseph was denied promotion because of her disability.
Unhappy over this, she filed a case in the Kerala High Court.
She alleged discrimination on account of her disability.
The HC then said that Leesamma Joseph is eligible for promotion under the PwD quota.
She must be treated just like any other able bodied employee and should be promoted.
She should not be denied promotion.
The Kerala government, unhappy over the verdict,
filed a case in the Supreme Court of India saying Joseph can not be promoted on account of her disability.
Two judges Justices S.K. Kaul and R. Subhash Reddy presided over the case
and told the Kerala government that:
According to the Persons with Disabilities Act of 1995,
PwD reservation quota is provided in all government jobs.
Under this there are two criterias.
If an able bodies employee in government job
acquires a disability through an accident, he becomes a person with disability
and is eligible for promotion.
Similarly, a government employee born with a disability, is also eligible for promotion.
Such individuals must be treated fairly and can not be denied promotion.
The court also said, merely providing reservation is not enough.
Once PwDs are given reservation in government posts,
there should be career progression through promotion & skilled PwDs should be encouraged.
If individuals are denied promotion on account of their disability,
it can cause breed negativity & demotivation among them.
Watching able bodied persons getting promoted, can lead massive self-esteem issues.
PwDs must be motivated & encouraged.
This is why apex court has said Joseph is eligble for promotion as per the PwD law and there shall be no discrimination.
The court gave Kerala three months to identify posts in which reservation could be given for PwD in promotion.

Level 1 : Cities and districts with 5 percent positivity rate

Level 2 : Cities and areas having 5 percent positivity
and oxygenated bed occupancy between 25 and 40 per cent will come under this category.
Level 3: Cities and areas with positivity between 5 percent and 10 percent,
or oxygenated bed occupancy more than 40 per cent will fall in the category.
Level 4: Areas having positivity between 10 percent and 20 per cent,
or having oxygenated bed occupancy of more than 60 per cent come under this.
Level 5: These are areas having a positivity rate of more than 20 per cent,
or having oxygenated bed occupancy of more than 75 per cent.
This level is the most dangerous.

The Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MEITy)
had issued a new set of guidelines for
social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, etc.
These new guidelines were issued in February 2021.
Social media platforms were given 3 months to comply with these guidelines.
As per the new rules announced by MEITy,
if social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Twiter, etc. have a a user base of more than 50 lakh -
- currently like Facebook other platforms too have crores of users -
then they are required to appoint Indian resident officers as directed by the ministries.
All social media companies have to appoint 3 officers.
Let me tell you about these officers.
1. ‘Compliance Officers’ will monitor the content and remove it if it is objectionable.
2. They will also have to appoint a ‘Grievance Redressal Officer’
who will take care of the complaints and act on them in 15 days.
3. The ‘Nodal Contact Person’ will coordinate with the police over serious matters.
These 3 officers must be Indian residents and will be appointed by the ministries.
When objectionable posts depicting nudity, morphed photos and other vulgar content are shared,
social media platforms will have to track the originator of such posts
if the government or a court asks them to.
Such posts have to be deleted within 24 hours.
Such rules are not only applicable to social media platforms but also to OTT platforms.
The streaming platforms include Netflix, Amazon Prime and others.
MEITy said that social media platforms do not have a code of self-regulation.
Therefore, it wants the government officers to get involved in social media and OTT platform companies to regulate content.
They will also have to set up a committee
that will have the sole power to take actions on complaints of the violation of codes.
The deadline to accept the guidelines set by the government ended on 25th May,
but so far none of the platforms have complied with the new regulations yet.
Platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and WhatsApp have not complied yet.
The Indian version of Twitter, Koo,
is the only social media platform to comply with the new guidelines.
Currently when an objectionable post is circulated,
action is taken against the individual who created the post while the social media platform receives immunity.
Now that the deadline to comply with the guidelines is over,
social media platforms will lose their special immunity status or the platform may be banned.
US-based social media companies had asked for six months time
as they are waiting for a response from the US headquarters.
While the government calls the new rules transparent and stress they are needed to increase accountability,
social media & OTT platforms have resisted the
changes saying the guidelines go against the right to an individual's freedom of speech.
Social media companies & OTT platforms are likely to ask for an extension to discuss the guidelines further.
Lakshdweep Islands are near the coast of Kerala.
There are protests happening in Lakshadweep over the last few days
over a slew of reforms passed by the island's Administrator Praful Khoda Patel.
People from Kerala have supported the protests and have started campaign called 'Save Lakshadweep’.
The protests are to withdraw the new reforms.
Celebrities, politicians, social media users, and many others have supported the campaign.
According to them, the laws implemented should be withdrawn.
Let me tell you about these reforms.
Praful K Patel became administrator of Lakshadweep in December 2020.
After taking charge, the first law he passed was the ‘Goonda Act’.
According to this law, in Lakshadweep any person can be put behind bars.
Under normal circumstances, there is a procedure and court trial to arrest a person.
However, according to the Goonda Act, there is no need for a trial
and the person can be arrested directly.
The people of Lakshadweep are unhappy with his law.
Crimes are a very rare occurence in Lakshadweep
and the prisons are almost empty.
People feel the law was passed undemocratically and hence are unhappy.
Also, the Prevention of Anti-Social Activities Act (PASA), that was passed in January 2021,
gives the government power to detain a person without any public disclosure for a period of up to one year.
LDAR is the Lakshadweep Development Authority Regulation 2021.
This law too was passed by Praful Patel.
For any town planning or any future developmental activity,
this law gives the administrator powers to use the islanders property.
It will gives complete powers to the government to directly interfere with an islander’s right to possess
and use their property in the name of development.
The different districts of Lakshadweep have Panchayats.
Earlier the panchayats had powers to look after Education, health, Fisheries etc.
Patel has curtailed the powers of the district panchayat and vested all the powers with the administrator alone.
The government has said that those with more than 2 children will not be allowed to contest panchayat elections.
Lakshadweep island’s population is around 97 percent Muslim.
The government has banned non vegetarian food in schools.
In lakshadweep sea food is majorly consumed.
The government has also passed the Animal Preservation Regulation, 2021
which will ban beef on the island.
Till now alcohol was never sold on the island.
Now liquor licenses will be given and sale of alcohol will be permitted.
Fishermen sheds were also demolished by the government saying they were illegal.
Earlier, Patel had imposed strict Covid protocols.
If anyone wanted to enter the island they had to strictly quarantine for 14 days.
Only after that they can enter the island.
Patel has also made COVID protocols of Lakshadweep less strict.
Now only a negative RT-PCR certificate is enough to enter Lakshadweep.
People are not happy with this as well because they feel that the earlier rule controlled the spread of the virus.
People of Kerala are unhappy over the laws as they are undemocratic & unconstitutional.
Kerala Rajya Sabha MP Elamaram Kareem wrote to President Ram Nath Kovind,
on 24th May requesting him to urgently remove Patel
as people were not happy with his way of working.
People of the island suspect that
Praful Patel who is a close aide of PM Modi has made these reforms
to establish a Hindutva agenda on the island.
They feel this is why he has imposed a ban on non veg food and beef.

struck down the reservation for the Maratha community in the SEBC Act 2018.

exceptional circumstances within a particular community.

Whenever married couples have a baby, it is a joyous occasion
and is lavishly celebrated by family & loved ones.
Sadly many couples experience miscarriage or still births.
This causes a lot of grief for the couple. Family and well wishers share their grief,
but a mother's pain is the highest. Mothers shatter when they miscarry or have a still birth.
It causes a lot of emotional trauma. This pain is very difficult to comprehend.
Many sympathise with the mothers but they usually fail to understand their pain.
It will be difficult for women to overcome such pain and takes a long time.
When mothers miscarry or have a still birth, they experience severe bleeding,
and the body becomes very weak.
The frail body & bleeding can be treated with medicines,
but the shattered emotions take a while to recover from. A mother's pain is incomparable.
Companies usually give a 6-month maternity leave to mothers.
However, in times of a misscarriage or still birth,
women are given a very short break and have to return to work later.
Companies do not give many leaves to women to help them recover from the trauma.
They have no option but to resume work.
Now the New Zealand parliament has passed a law
that would give couples who suffer a miscarriage or stillbirth three days leave.
The leave would help them recover mentally & physically.
The law passed ensures that it will be a paid leave and salary will not be deducted.
Ginny Andersen, the member of Parliament who drafted the bill said,
Women are emotionally devastated when they miscarry or have a still birth.
They are unable to request a leave from work.
This is why they resume their duties.
I wanted women to have the confidence to be able to request leave which is their right
when they experience such a loss.
This is why we passed such a law for the mental health of mothers.
New Zealand received a lot of praise from around the world.
However, in India we have a stronger law.
Indian women are entitled to paid leave for six weeks following miscarriage or still birth.
Shocking isn't it that India's law is much better. But many are not aware about this
and resume work after the incident. This is because many women are not aware.

Let me tell you about a very strange incident.
In Chandigarh, a 25-year-old girl's case shocked doctors.
This woman had bloody tears falling from her eyes. She had no idea how this happened.
She said that she wasn’t experiencing any pain or discomfort.
Doctors were surprised and wanted to know the reason.
The doctors sent her to an ophthalmologist and for other tests.
All the results came clear.
They were unable to diagnose her condition.
Upon investigating further they found,
the bleeding eyes only occurred when the woman was on her period.
Once her periods stops the tears would stop.
She had experienced the same during her last period.
Since she experienced the same again, doctors were able to find the cause.
It is a rare condition called Ocular Vicarious Menstruation.
Ocular Vicarious Menstruation is a very rare condition.
During a menstrual cycle women bleed inside their uterus.
But OVM causes bleeding in the eyes, nose, mouth, lungs, kidney and stomach.
The girl was suffering from this condition.
Doctors treated her with hormonal medication and contraceptive pills -
which are medicines to prevent pregnancies.
She had to take them for 3 months and will help to treat the condition.
Doctors say this may help treat others around the world suffering from OVM.
Since the 1900s, over a period of 120 years, there have been very few cases of OVM.
For example, since 100 years, there have been many cases of cancers
but comparitively OVM is extremely rare.
In 1913, a doctor in Roswell, New Mexico,
reported a case of a woman who had ulcers on both her knees that would bleed.
The doctor was unable to diagnose her.
These ulcers would bleed during her period and doctors were unable to diagnose her.
According to the report, she had a difficult pregnancy after which the condition disappeared.

On 17th March 2021, the Purnagiri Jan Shatabdi express train

Let me tell you what happened.
The train was on its way to Tanakpur in Uttarakhand from Delhi.
Rajendra Singh, public relation officer, North Eastern railway division said,
Just before the train reached Tanakpur, a cow had died on the track,
which is why the train stopped.
But suddenly the train began going backwards and covered a distance of 20km.
The loco pilot tried his best to stop the train, but his efforts went in vain.
A pressure pipe in the train had burst which caused the brakes to fail.
This is why the train went backwards.
When the passengers in the train realised the train was moving backwards, everyone panicked.
The train covered 20km in this way!
Fortunately, none of the passengers were injured.
Since they were unable to stop the train, Singh said,
“Railway crossings were shut to allow the train to pass.

to ascertain the cause of the incident. Strict action would be taken against culprits.

In Odisha's Ganjam district there is a beach called 'Pati Sonepur'.
At the beach, the fishermen had thrown their net in the sea.
When they pulled the net out, they were stunned to find a huge Whale Shark.
The Whale was 15-feet long and weighed 1,500 kg.
The Whale was alive! The Local fishermen, villagers & forest department decided
to take the whale from the Pati Sonepur beach & released it deep into the Bay of Bengal.
Since the Whale was alive, they decided to release it.
If they release it near the beach, the whale would be risk of getting stuck in the nets.
Hence, they released it into the deep sea so that it can move around safely.
Officials said they released the whale into the sea because,
Whale Sharks swim close to the water surface and are a slow moving fish.
This is because it feeds 'Plankton' which are found near the surface of the water.
If it is released near the coast, it can get stuck in the nets.
Officials said, this is why it was released into the deep sea so it can feed.
Whale Sharks come near the Pati Sonepur beach generally from February to May every year.
Forest personnel have been posted on the beach to ensure the whale does not come back to the shore.
Sometimes if a whale dies, it can be washed ashore.
This is why personnel have been posted to keep a watch.
Whale sharks are protected under the Wildlife Protection Act.
This is because they are an endangered species.
To make sure they do not become extinct, the laws were created to protect the whale.
According to forrest officials 2020
in Odisha, along the coastline of the Ganjam district,
at Gopalpur, Pati Sonepur and Kantiagada 4 whales had died.
To ensure this doesn't happen again, measures have been taken to protect the endangered species.

to protects humans, nature and the wildlife.
They used nets to help villagers easily collect the Mahua flowers.

He was able to find her all because she was taught Sign language and writting.

You are aware that the COVID vaccination drive has started in India.
The 1st Phase focussed on vaccinating frontline workers.
Now the 2nd Phase has started
in which people above the age of 60 and those above 45 will be vaccinated
starting from 1st March.
Individuals above the age of 45 will be vaccinated only if they have comorbidities.
I am sure that many of you are confused on how to register for the vaccines and which App to use.
Journalist Faye D’Souza has clearly explained the entire registration process.
Let me tell you about it.
To avail the COVID vaccine, you will have to register on the Co-WIN website only and not the App.
Now let me tell you how to register.
Open the Google search engine and then go to the Co-WIN
and this is where you can register for the vaccine.
Click on the yellow Registration tab.
A new window will open up where you have to enter your mobile number
and then click to receive an OTP. Once you receive it, enter that in as well.
Some users may face problems with OTP. If you have trouble, click on resend OTP.
Once you receive it, you can proceed.
OTP related issued should be solved by the government soon.
Now you will directed to a page where you have to select a Photo ID Proof.
There are options such as Aadhar Card, PAN Card, driving license,
Voter ID, Pension Passbook & NPR Smart Card. You can choose any one.
For example if you select an Aadhar card,
carefully enter Aadhar card number.
Once you enter your ID details,
you will have to carry the same ID to the vaccination centre.
For example, if you have entered your Aadhar card details, but forget to take it along,
another ID will not be accepted. So make sure you carry the same ID you have entered.
Then enter your name as per the ID mentioned. There should be no difference in the name.
Then put in your gender. Male, Female or Others.
Now you will have to enter your year of birth.
Those above the age of 60, i.e born before 1961, can enter their birth years.
Those above the age of 45, i.e born prior to 1976, can enter their birth year.
A red text will pop up. Asking if you have any cormobities. Click on 'Yes' or 'No'.
Such individuals will have to carry a doctors certificate along with them at the time of vaccination.
If you are above the age of 45 without any comorbidities, then you are not eligible for the vaccine.
Now you have completed the registration.
You may want to register for your older brother, mother, any of your senior relatives
or those suffering with comorbidities. You can add such persons and register for them.
Again these individuals must be above the age of 60 or 45 with comorbidities.
Keep in mind that on one mobile number, only 4 individuals can register.
After completing registration, you can now proceed to schedule an appointment for vaccination.
First enter the state you are living in,
next enter the city you live in, Block & then your pin code.
You will then be shown a list of COVID Vaccination centres close to you.
It will include both government & private hospitals close to you.
Some people have had trouble finding a centre close to their place.
Hopefully the government solves this in the next few weeks.
Select the centre you want.
If you choose a government hospital,
remember you do not have to pay for the vaccine.
It will be administered in 2 doses.
If you go to a private hospital,
each dose costs Rs 250. So in total you have to pay Rs 500.
You will have to pay for vaccines in private hospitals, whereas in government hospitals it will be free.
Once you select the centre name you have the option of date.
As of now, the timings are from 9am to 6pm
and per day they vaccinate only 50 people per centre.
If slots are available go ahead and book.
If there is no availability, then you click to check slots for next week.
If availability is there, proceed to book and then confirm your appointment.
Once this is done, you will get a receipt with your name, reference number, etc.
Download and print this document.
You also receive a confirmation SMS.
Those above the age of 45 need to carry this receipt, Photo ID Proof that they mentioned earlier,
and doctors certificate regarding their cormobidities,
at the time of going to the vaccination centre.
Those above 60, must carry the receipt, their photo ID proof
and if they have any illness, they can carry a doctors certificate at the time of vaccination.
Currently there are only 2 vaccines in the market.
There is Covishield by Serum Institute of India
and Covaxin by Bharat Biotech.
Think carefully before scheduling an appointment at any vaccination centre.
Supposing you schedule the appoinment and go to the centre and prefer a certain vaccine.
At the centre you won't have the choice to choose a vaccine,
you will have to take what they give because it is ordered in bulk by the hospital.
If you prefer a particular vaccine,
contact the centre close to you beforehand and check what they have.
Once you are satisfied with what they have, you can book the appoinment.
Otherwise contact another centre and fix the appointment accordingly.

In India, there are many families that grieve when a daughter is born.
According to many, a daughter has no furture and has to be married off.
For the rest of her life, she will tend to her children and can do no other work.
Many people have such a mentality.
In Laxmipur village of Siwan district in Bihar,

that a daughter can do anything in the future. She has her own goals in life.

under the guidance of their geography teacher and coach, Sanjay Pathak.

The girls have achieved multiple accomplishments in the last 10 years
in football, handball, javelin throw, high jump, athletics, and other sports,
at National & International tournaments and have also secured 70 medals.
Sanjay is not a formal coach. He was a normal teacher.
He began coaching because of his passion to train talent in his region.
Let me tell you how he came up with this idea.
Pathak was posted at the Adarsh government middle school.
Two girls from the village named Tara and Putul, wanted to participate in the local sports tournament.
Initially Sanjay too did not agree but then he agreed to register them.
To his surprise, the girls won a gold medal in athletics.
Pathak was awestruck at their talent.
After this incident Sanjay thought, “Like these girls there must be many such others in the village.

This did not stop him and he went ahead to help the girls hone their skills.

represented India in Nepal, Tajikistan, Beirut, Lebanon and other national sports competitions.

On TV there are many advertisements about air conditioners, mobiles,
gadgets, toothpaste, shampoo, soap, etc. Many well known celebrities are part of such ads.
There are many influencers on social media platforms such as YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, etc.
where they post various forms of content.
These posts are highly viewed and such individuals have a large following.
They have millions of followers.
These influencers promote various products including shampoos.
They even promote mobiles, gadgets, clothing, makeup, etc.
It is common knowledge that celebrities are paid to appear on TV advertisements.
You may think that influencers are not paid for their content. But that's not the case.
Such influencers with a large following are usually paid by brands to promote their products.
For example influencers who promote a soap are usually paid to do it.
People think only TV ads are paid but even the social media ads are paid.
People are usually unaware about this.
Earlier, there weren't many regulations for social media influencers.
Television adverts were properly regulated, but social media was not.
People were free to collaborate with brands and post content.
This is why the Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI)
has issued a set of draft guidelines that will be finalized by March 31.
It will be applicable to all influencers who want to post content on social media platforms.
These draft guidelines will apply to posts published on or after April 15.
Let me tell you about these guidelines.
On social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram,  YouTube, Snapchat, Pinterest, etc.
when influencers post images, stories, LIVE, videos, etc.
if they have been paid by brands, then the influencer must ensure the post is labelled tags such as
#ad, #collab, #sponsored, and #partnership.
This will help people realise that the video was a paid advertisement.
As per the ASCI these labels must be visible on all devices like mobile, computer, iPad, laptop etc.
When an influencer posts any form of paid content on social media,
it must be mentioned in the video in any form for people to understand its a paid collaboration.
There is another rule. Let me give you an example.
Say a brand has a cream that promises to brighten the skin in 7 days.
When they ask influencers to promote the skin cream,
the influencers must not do so blindly.
It is the influencer’s responsibility to check its performance claims.
Influencers shouldn't use filters that exaggerate the brand's claims, to mislead viewers.
They must post authenticate images or videos.

This is the Sign for Transgender Men & Women.
Transpersons want to showcase to the world that they can be empowered and independently live their lives.
There is one such story of Urooz Hussain from Bihar.
She is  27-years-old and set up her cafe named 'Street Temptation' in Uttar Pradesh's Noida.
Urooz said that she wanted to show the world that a transwoman can setup her own business.
Urooz was harassed and mocked at her workplace.
She then decided to resign and independently set up her business.
Urooz said that she was born a boy.
Between the age of 13-18, she always felt that she was a girl and not a boy.
Because of her feminine behaviour, her male relatives would bully her a lot.
Her father was strict and forced her to behave like a boy.
However, she always liked to interact with girls more than boys.
Urooz would use makeup, paint her nails, wear feminine clothes and related strongly with women.
She loved playing with dolls, cooking and was interested in feminine things.
Since she was always bullied, in 2013 she left her hometown and moved to Delhi,
where she began her transition as a transwoman.
She added, "People always think all transgenders just beg, clap and are sex workers.
But this is not true. Transperson are all natural beings and must be respected.”
Hussain further explained that she was harassed and bullied for being a transwoman.
But she never gave up and was determined to proudly stand by her identity,
to create awareness that transgender people can setup businesses. She worked to do this.
She added that due to the financial difficulties during lockdown
she even thought about selling the restaurant.
Urooz had some savings which she had given to doctors for her gender reassignment surgery,
she was in two minds about whether to sell her restaurant or proceed with the surgery.
She requested the doctor to give her the money back and postponed the surgery
so that her business could carry on.
She further added, "Any job-seeking transperson could approach to work at her restaurant
as we are all the same and understand each other.
Transpersons can work here without any discrimination.
In 2020, Jharkhand had recorded 3,366 road accidents and 2,294 deaths.
The state government approved a proposal
& announced a reward for those who carry a victim to the hospital.
The Jharkhand government approved the 'Good Samaritan Policy'.
The victim must be rescued within 1-hr of the accident to eligible for the reward.
If victims are taken to any doctor, hospital, etc. within an hour they will be paid Rs 2,000.
₹2,000 each will be provided to two persons, who help carry the victim for medical treatment.
If more than two persons help the victims,
they would be entitled to a reward of ₹5,000 which will be distributed amongst them.
Earlier onlookers avoided helping as they feared interrogation and hassles of the court-room.
The policy is to encourage people to rescue victims through the cash prize.
The identity of the 'Samaritan' will not be disclosed but they will be paid.
The ones cooperating with the police investigation will also be felicitated with a cash reward.
Earlier samaritans had to take part in continuous court proceedings.
Now as per the new policy, if they are a witness to the accident then they will be called for the hearing only once.
The state government said this move would motivate people to step up and help save lives.

NASA's Spacecraft was at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, USA.
The spacecraft contained the Perseverance rover.
It took off from earth on 30 july 2020 and after a six-month journey, the spacecraft reached Mars' orbit.
The spacecraft then began its descent into Mars's atmosphere with a parachute.
Once it was close to the surface, the rover was lowered to the ground using cables.
The rover successfully landed on Mars on 19th Feb 2021 at 2.25 am IST.
Having the rover land on Mars was not an easy feat.
This is because the land on mars is uneven and the crater was 47-km wide.
Despite all challenges they were dertermined and successfully completed the mission.
Before the rover landed it faced many challenges.
Americans at NASA were extremely anxious and did not know if the rover reached in one piece.
You would think they would be able to track the rover in real time.
However that's not the case. In our day to day lives say we travel to Goa from Mumbai.
On reaching Goa, we can immediately update our families in real time.
This was not the case with the rover.
The distance between Mars and Earth is 206.02 million km.
Any information captured by the rover takes 11 minutes to travel from Mars to Earth.
This is why it took long for the America to realise the rover landed safely.
Upon receiving information, people at NASA were overjoyed and began applauding.
The spacecraft was travelling at a speed of 20,000 km/h.
Indian-American Dr Swati Mohan was part of the team of scientists that worked on this project.
It was being controlled by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, USA.
The entire project cost $ 2.7 billion.
The successful landing of the rover can be seen using this link:
The Perseverance rover will remain on Mars for one Martian year which equals 687 days on Earth.
US President Joe Biden was overjoyed & congratulated the team that worked on the rover
and said that this is Proof that with the power of science and American ingenuity nothing is impossible.
Till now NASA has sent 4 rovers to Mars. Perseverance is the 5th.
The aim of the rover is to stay on mars and try to find
signs of life in the form of plants, bacteria, virus
and ascertain whether Martian atomosphere is suitable for human beings.

Nidhi gave all her personal data, bank passbook and other documents in these 8 months.

Later she was interviewed online for 1 and half hour.

as she was moving to Harvard University, USA to teach.

stating her online classes would commence from September 2020.

A Deaf man named Virender Singh, known as ‘Goonga Pehelwan’,
is a three-time Deaflympics gold medallist.
He has now been awarded with the Padma Shri.
Virender Singh is a strong Deaf wrestler and has shown the world that
there is no difference between the Deaf & hearing.
He is a role model for all Deaf individuals.
Virender is from Sasroli village in Haryana’s Jhajjar District.
Since the age of 8, he was interested in wrestling.
He was inspired to take up wrestling by his father and uncle, who were wrestlers too.
At the age of 8, Virender's father suffered a road accident,
and badly damaged his left leg.
This is why Virendra was moved to Delhi and continued wrestling there.
His uncle personally started coaching Virender.
Virender then started training at famous wrestling akharas of Delhi.
At the National Rounds of the World Cadet Wrestling Championships in 2002,
Virender a Deaf individual competed along with other hearing wrestlers.
He qualified to the finals and won a gold medal.
The silver was won by a hearing person. Virender automatically qualified for the international games.
However, the Indian government disqualified him, citing his deafness as the reason
and chose the silver medalist for the international games.
Virender was heartbroken and then returned to dangals to earn his livelihood.
Like hearing individuals participate in the Olympics,
the Deaflympics are for Deaf individuals.
In 2005, the Deaflympics were held in Melbourne, Australia.
When his father & uncle came to know about the Deaflympics,
they worked very hard and saved Rs 70,000 for Virender to travel to Melbourne.
Virender went there and won the Gold medal in wrestling.
Since then Virender continued winning medals.
Again, at the 2013 Summer Deaflympics in Bulgaria he won a gold medal
and he also won a Gold medal at the 2017 Summer Deaflympics in Turkey.
Now he has been awarded with the Padma Shri.
He is the first from his community of Deaf athletes to achieve this feat.
The government has bestowed upon him 4 awards.
He has received The Rajiv Gandhi State Sports Award & National Disability Award.
Virender was awarded the Arjuna Award for his stellar contribution to Indian Sports.
Even though Virender achieved so many medals, he received no recognition or monetary support.
Virender continued to participate in dangals while he juggled his tournaments.
He is the first from the Deaf community to achieve this feat.
Virender Singh spoke to the Times of India newspaper through his friend who helped interpret.
He said:
If I’ll continue to win medals for India,
people will see a Deaf man's capability. The recognition & respect will automatically follow.
Deaf wrestlers are as good as able-bodied athletes.
No one should think that just because we are Deaf, we are weak.
We are equally strong.
Just like I am a Deaf wrestler and I have achieved medals,
similarly other Deaf athletes can achieve success as well.
Now my dream is to achieve the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award.
I hope to give my best at the future Deaflympics and World Championship to achieve this dream.

The Central Government has prepared a bill to amend the Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products Act 2003.
This would become the Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products Amendment Act, 2020.
This bill proposes to raise the age for allowing sale of cigarettes & tobacco products to 21 years from the current 18 years.
Under the amendments proposed in the bill,
If cigarettes or tabacco products are sold to people below the age of 21,
they can be jailed for a year and fined Rs 50,000.
A second convinction for the same offence could lead to a 2 year jail term
and a Rs 1 lakh fine. This has been proposed in the bill.

The penalty for smoking at restricted areas is being increased from Rs 200 to Rs 2,000.
Cigarettes must be produced in compliance with the Government's quality control guidelines.
They must also print the advisory images of the dangers of smoking on the packs.
Violation of these guidelines, will lead to 2 years jail and a fine of Rs 1 lakh.
Earlier vendors would sell lose cigarettes.
Now only the entire packet can be sold.
The packet must be properly manufactured and sealed.
Packets of 10, 12 or 20 cigarettes must be in compliance with government rules.
A first time conviction would lead to 2 year prison term or a fine of Rs 1 lakh.
A second conviction would lead to 5 year prison term or 5 lakh.
These are the amendments are proposed by the Central government.

The 'Impeachment Process' is where the House of Representatives -
which is like the Indian Lok Sabha - a President is charged for his alleged misconduct.
Once the members vote, if majority votes are against the President, then
the President will be removed from office by the United States Senate
similar to the Rajya Sabha in India.
This is called Impeachment.
Last week Trump supporters stormed the US Capitol which led to a lot of violence.
5 people were dead because of this.
Because of this the US House of representatives on 13th January decided
to vote and decided whether US President Trump provoked his supporters in his speech.
The House of Representatives voted at 1:30am IST.
Both Democrats and Republicans - Trump belongs to Republican party - voted.
The members voted 232-197 & charged Trump responsible for inciting violence at the capitol.
10 were republicans from his own party, voted against him.
However, the Senate will not hold the trial immediately.
The trial will be held after Joe Biden assumes presidency.
If the Senate decides that Trump is guilty of provoking violence,
then he will not be allowed to take part in elections in 2024.
This is the second time Trump has been impeached.
He was impeached earlier when he tried to dig up dirt on Joe Biden
to beat him in the elections.
Now again he has been impeached.
Trump is the 1st US President to be impeached twice.

Karnataka’s BJP government on 9th December 2020,

As per this law, the slaughter of “cow, the calf of a cow, bull, bullock and he or she buffalo” is banned.
Offenders will receive stringent punishments.
The Opposition Congress and JDS were shocked that the bill was tabled and approved out of the blue.

When the BJP was in power in Karnataka in 2010,
they had passed a strict law that did not allow cattle slaughter.

with certain restrictions and the punishments were less severe.

Under the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Bill, 2020,
the slaughter of “cow, the calf of a cow and bull, bullock and he or she buffalo” is banned.
Buffaloes will be allowed to slaughter only if they are above the age of 13 years
for medical research, if the cattle is very sick, or if the cattle has an infectious disease
and prevention has to be taken to prevent the infection from spreading.
However, a competent authority needs to certify the slaughter.
If a cow is killed in Karnataka, then arrests can be carried out without an arrest warrant.
The punishment for slaughtering cows
is seven years of jail or fines ranging from Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh or both.
The new Bill also prescribes new punishments
for the transport of cattle, sale of meat, and purchase or taking cattle for slaughter
- a prison term of three to five years and a fine of Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh.
