The current regulations have around 18 parameters that honey must comply with.
If all the 18 parameters are passed, only then the honey can be labelled as ‘pure honey.’
CSE food researchers selected 13 Indian honey brands including Dabur, Patanjali, Baidyanath and Zandu.
The brands met all the parameters and passed those tests.
The brands were then put through a special test, called NMR.
This is a German test. All the brands were tested. Shockingly,
only three brands passed this test: Saffola, Markfed Sohna and Nature’s Nectar.
The rest failed.
The NMR test is not required by Indian law for honey that is being marketed locally but is needed for export.
Dabur Honey in a statement denied that its honey was adulterated with sugar syrup.
The company furnished a July 20 report from a German company, Bruker.
The report said there was no evidence of sugar syrup.
The CSE investigation said Indian companies were importing synthetic sugar syrups from China to adulterate honey.
Sunita Narain, Director General, CSE said,
“We are consuming honey, it to fight the pandemic and strenghten immunity.
But honey adulterated with sugar will not make us well.”
Bee-keepers work very hard to make natural honey. This increases cost of the product.
Since companies sell adulterated honey, people buy that instead.
Because of this Bee-keepers are suffering a loss.

RTGS is a type of transfer to transfer money from one bank to any other bank.
RTGS transactions have no amount cap.
The minimum amount through RTGS is Rs 2 lakh. It is used for large transactions.
Earlier, RTGS was available from 7.00 am to 6.00 pm on all working days of a week,
except second and fourth Saturdays of every month.
Now RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das announced
that RTGS will be available round-the-clock i.e 24x7x365 from 1st December 2020.
This was to encourage business payments with flexible timings.
The decision was taken to make India one of the few countries in the world with 24x7 RTGS service.
In December 2019, the RBI had made the NEFT system available on a 24x7x365 basis.
Earlier when people transferred money through NEFT or RTGS, banks would add extra charges.
But in July 2019 RBI stopped those charges, the aim was to promote digital transactions.
The Reserve Bank of India has mentioned that there will be 11 bank holidays in the month of December
However, the bank holidays will not be observed by all the banking companies.
Banking holidays also depend on the festivals being observed in specific states.
25th December, Christmas is a holiday during which all the banks across the country will remain closed.
With the banks having holidays for about 11 days in December,
removing the time limit for RTGS transactions will help promote digital transactions in the country.

WhatsApp has introduced a ‘Disappearing Message’ feature that deletes unread messages after seven days.

Personal chats include important conversations and some are not that important.
If you feel a particular text is not important and receive many unneccessary texts,
then tap on the contact’s name, click on disappearing messages, and then click on ‘On’.
The messages on these chats will disappear after 7 days.
The chats in which you kept the disappearing messages 'off', will remain as is.
In group chats, only the group admin will be able to do enable disappearing messages.
If disappearing messages are enables, media sent in the chat will disappear,
and it won't save on your phone as well.
However, if auto-download is on,
the images will automatically save on your phone but get deleted from chat after 7 days.
WhatsApp said for now disappearing message feature will delete messages after 7 days.
If successful, they tweak the number of days later.
WhatsApp said the update was made because people are flooded with messages daily.
If unopened, the chats remain in the inbox for a long time.
It becomes troublesome to go throught these chats.
Disappearing Messages helps to screen chats and the messages vanish in 7 days.
Important chats if turned off, will remain as is.
All important conversations say about banking, addresses, shopping lists, etc will remain easy to find.

Let me explain what are OTT platform.
On Television networks there are News channels, audio, movie, serial and other services that you can watch.
There are movies that you watch in theatres as well. But OTT platform is different from this.
OTT platform consist of digital content that you can watch on mobile phones, laptops or through Apps
of companies such as Hotstar, Amazon Prime, Netflix, Zee5, etc. These are part of OTT platform.
People have started watching content on OTT platforms very recently.
Between 2018 - 2019 towards the end of March, OTT platforms made a business of Rs 500 crore.
According to projections, OTT platforms make earn upto Rs 4,000 crore upto 2025.
Television, radio, newspapers, magazine, movies, etc have been issued guideline by the government.
The guideline include regulations such as certification for movies, censorship of sensitive content, etc.
OTT platform do not have to follow these rules. There are free to broadcast any form of content online.
These companies are free to decide the stories be it related to politics, vulgar content, etc.
They do not have to mention any form of certification for the videos.
They are free to decide their subscription fees as well. They do not have to follow government guidelines.
Many complained that OTT platforms must be regulated because their vulgar content can influence the youth.
Now President Ram Nath Kovind
signed an order amending the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961.
As per this, all OTT platforms will now be regulated by the Information and Broadcasting Ministry.
OTT platforms will not be happy with following the government's guidelines.
Because many online platforms create movies, web series, etc on politics and other sensitive topics.
They may not be happy as they will have to be censored by the government.

Last year the IPL had started a new initiative,
where the 8 IPL teams like the Mumbai Indias, Rajasthan Royals, Kings IX Punjab,
Kolkata Knight Riders, Chennai Super Kings, etc. with eleven players
each can transfer players such as bowlers, batsmen and wicketkeeper on loan to other teams.
This was started last year and is known as ‘Mid-Season Transfer Window’.
The transfer window has started after each of the 8 teams have played 7 matches each.
The IPL 2020 started on 19th September and ends on 10th November.
Since half of the season is over the transfer window will start from 13th October 2020
and teams will have a 5 days window to complete the transfer.
Compared to last year's limited rules, this year the IPL has released new rules.
Teams can give any player on loan - both Indian and overseas – during this window.
However, the IPL Governing Council will have to be notified of all transfers.
1. Which players are eligible for transfers?
Let me tell you. Lets take Mumbai Indians (MI) and Chennai Super Kings (CSK) as an example.
If CSK wants a particular player from MI, then as per the rules
only the player who has played upto two matches will be allowed to transfer.
A player who has played more than 2 matches in the IPL will not be eligible.
During the 5 day window, once the teams complete their discussions and registeration,
50% of the amount will be paid  “within 7 days of registration”.That means CSK has to pay MI in 7 days.
The remaining amount will be paid “within 7 days of the final match of the season” on 10th November.
2. Will the loanee player have any game restrictions to play against their parent team?
When a player from MI transfer to Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR),
that player can play with KKR against any other team except MI.
This is because MI is the player's parent team. Hence, he can't play against them.
3. Is this a permanent transfer?
No. Let me give you an example,
If ace batsmen Chris Gayle of Kings XI Punjab
transfers to Chennai Super Kings in the current IPL season,
then in 2021 IPL Gayle will come back to KXIP.
This is a good opportunity for talented players who did not get the chance to participate in the matches.
The transfer window is a good opportunity for the players to improve their skills.
Let me give examples of Possible transfers:
Ace bowler Imran Tahir of CSK may be wanted by the Delhi Capitals.
Because the leg-spinner had 26 wickets in the previous IPL season
but is yet to get a game this season.
DC lost bowler Amit Mishra due to a finger injury
and now they might be interested in a good replacement bowler for their team.
Ajinkya Rahane of the Delhi Capitals is an amazing batsmen with a total of more than 3,800 runs.
CSK may want him for their team.
Because according to Dhoni, CSK has been struggling with their batting this year.
This is why they may consider getting Rahane on board.
The concept of the transfer window is not new.
This has been going on between football teams for a while now.
BCCI's idea to implement the same in Indian cricket is commendable.
However many say that the transfer window idea will not be success here.
Here are 3 reasons why people think the transfer window idea will not work:
1. Players from various teams during any IPL season, travel together across the country for any match,
the team practices and trains together and share a strong camaraderie with one another.
They are always together.
Similary while travelling together to Dubai, Abu Dabi and Sharjah they train and spend time together.
A player that has been with a team for a long time, will face discomfort on the sudden transfer.
If a team from CSK transfers to KKR may not be happy.
Even if the player has not played a match thus far would still be emotionally attached to the team
and a sudden change would feel unnatural. This is human.
Hence many feel the transfer window is not a good idea.
Unlike in football, where the transfer fees are so high that the player usually falls for it.
However cricket is very different and there is a strong bond between teams.
2. A player who has been staying with the team and being a part of team discussions,
when transfered, can easily go to the other camp and spill the beans. This is unfair.
This is why the idea will not succeed.
There is no long-term planning behind this and hence the chances of it succeeding are less.
For example, CSK is a strong team with strong players.
Transfers will cause the team to weaken. This will eventually lead to weaker matches.
These are the reason why people feel the concept may not work.

Sheetal Bhanushali was a 32 year old housewife .
On 3rd October at about 7.00 pm, Sheetal fell into a manhole.
Heavy rains and water logging caused, the manhole cover had come off.
This is how Sheetal fell into the open manhole and her body was found on 5th October.
Why did it take two days for her body to be found?
Well after falling in the manhole, her body travelled a long distance.
Sheetal had fallen in a manhole in Ghatkopar East,
and her body was found 30 KM away in Haji Ali by some workers.
On finding the body, the workers informed the closest police station which was the Tardeo Police.
Officials are surprised how her body was found 30 km away from Ghatkopar.
They are shocked and are unable to understand this.
Sheetal's relative Mahendra Bhanushali said,
on 3rd October around 7 pm Sheetal with her son Yash went to buy craft items.
She dropped him home.
Sheetal then went to collect flour from a flour mill.
It was raining heavily and there was severe waterlogging.
A manhole cover had opened automatically due to the water logging.
Sheetal while walking could not see the open manhole and fell into it.
When she did not return her family looked for her.
People told them she fell into the manhole.
They then registered a missing complaint with the Ghatkopar police.
Mahendra Bhanushali added,
Putting covers on manholes is the BMC's responsibility.
The BMC had put a low-quality manhole lid which was light in weight.
So due to water logging it floated away and sheetal fell into it.
Only the BMC is responsible for Sheetal's death.
The police should register an offense of low quality work and negligence and against the BMC.”
The Ghatkopar police had first registered a missing complaint about Sheetal
and then when her body was found,
they converted it into an Accidental Death Report (ADR)
This means since, she died accidentally by falling into a manhole, it was not a natural death.
In the postmortem report,
the cause of death was drowning and shockingly she was found to be COVID positive.
Sheetal is survived by her husband Jitesh, who has a garments business,
and two children, son Yash age 8, and daughter Dhvani age 2.
Assistant Commissioner of BMC Manish Valanju of L ward said,
“It is shocking how Sheetal's body moved so far.
We will investigate.”
BMC has asked for a detailed report of Bhanushali's death.

In homes across India, people watch a variety of TV channels like Sony, Zee TV, Colours,
star plus, news channels, sports channels, etc.
People watch these channels in multiple languages such as Gujarati, Telugu, Punjabi, etc.
People watch movies and TV series.
TRP tells us which TV Channel and show are viewed the most.
TRP stands for Television Rating Points.
The Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC), gives TRP rating to TV channels in India.
They do this by installing a device called ‘Barometers’ in thousands of houses.
BARC gave a confidential contract to a company called Hansa Research
to install these barometers in various houses.
30,000 barometers were installed across India of which 2,000 were installed in Mumbai.
The device checks which channels and shows are viewed the most in these houses.
Hansa Research had filed a case with the Mumbai Police
saying that some of Hansa Research's former employees
had sold the data of these houses, which are kept extremely confidential, to TV Channels.
The Mumbai police 8th October began investigating TV channels.
The Mumbai Police said that its Crime Branch
has busted a TRP manipulation racket which was being done by TV channels.
Three channels Fakt Marathi, Box Cinema and Republic TV are being investigated.
According to the Mumbai Police,
these TV channels bribed Hansa Research former employees for data.
Once they received the data, channels located the house where the barometers were installed.
The channels would bribe the house to keep the TV on the full day even if they weren’t at home.
They did this to increase their TRP ratings.
In India there are household that talk in Marathi, Hindi, Telugu, Malyalam, Punjabi, Gujarati, etc.
They all do not watch Hindi news channels but watch channels in their respective languages.
English news channels bribed non-English speaking homes, and told them to keep English news channels on.
This was again done to increase their TRP ratings.
Owners of Fakt Marathi and Box Cinema were arrested for TRP fraud.
Mumbai Police Commissioner Param Bir Singh told reporters at a press conference
that the well known Arnab Goswami owner of Republic TV
will soon be questioned about his exponential increase in TRP rating.
Generally TRP ratings fluctuate but Republic TV's TRP has remained for a long time now.
The Police suspect a foul play in their TRPs and have promised a thorough investigation.
Arnab Goswami is famous for his loud debates and his coverage about Sushant Singh Rajput's death.
According to the police, securing high TRP ratings helps TV channels
charge the advertisers more money to display their adverts on the channels.
The three TV channels charged a large amount for such advertisements.
The police have promised a thorough investigation.
In a statement, Arnab Goswami strongly responded by saying
the Mumbai Police commissioner Param Bir Singh were completely false.
Arnab said he had earlier questioned the commissioner on the Sushant Singh Rajput death case.
The commissioner took offence at the questions and is now making false charges against me.
He said he will file a criminal defamation case against Param Bir Singh
and asked him to be ready in court.

which sells healthy home-cooked food. The food is prepared by an elderly couple.
They earn very little money.
With their meagre earnings they then buy groceries for the next day’s menu.
The elderly couple struggling to make ends meet with their limited earnings.
They have struggled for the last 30 years.
On 7th October a food blogger Gaurav Wasan, visited the food stall
and met the 80-year-old Kanta Prasad and his wife Badami Devi.
Wasan recorded a video of them both.
The couple spoke about their struggle to sell food and make ends meet during the lockdown.
The couple shared their story and the video went viral.
In the video, Prasad said he and his wife Badami Devi start cooking large quantities of food at 6.30 am
and are ready with the food by 9.30 am.
Dal, curry, parathas, and rice were ready to serve for around Rs. 30-50 a plate.
When Vasan asked Kanta Prasad how much he has earned today,
Prasad broke down and showed a Rs. 10 note in a box.
With tears in his eyes he said that due to the lockdown no one is eating at his stall.
In four hours he could earn only about Rs. 50.
A tearful Prasad said they never made huge profits.
The couple gets no help from their children - two sons and a daughter.
When Wasan's video went viral, on social media
and he encouraged people to visit the stall because the couple make home cooked meals.
The video was shared by many.
Many have offered to help the couple financially
and others announced plans for lunch at Baba Ka Dhaba to support their business.
Many celebrities and sports persons shared posts on social media to support them.
The next day there was a huge crowd of customers at the dhaba.
The couple were very happy. Have a look.
Kanta Prasad said, “We are very happy with the number of customers coming now.
All my stress went away when I saw so many customers.

His wife added, “The lockdown was a very bad time. For months we could not sell anything.

Cinema halls across India have been shut since March as a part of coronavirus-linked restrictions.

On 6th October 2020, Union Minister Prakash Javadekar
released rules and procedures for theatres.
Here are more details.
In cinema halls, only 50% occupancy will be allowed.
For example a theatre with a capacity of 100, can only allow 50 customers.
Similarly theatres across India can only function at 50% capacity.
Back to back shows are not allowed.
After every show they must reserve time thorough sanitisation.
Once that is done, they can allow coustomers inside for the next show at 50% capacity.
Thermal screening, masks, hand sanitizers, social distancing are mandatory.
Seating arrangements must be according to social distancing norms and unoccupied seats must be marked.
This is the responsibility of the theatres.
After the movie, customers must exit in a line keeping safe distance to prevent crowds.
Cinema halls must note down customers phone numbers.
This is because, if someone who watched the movie gets infected,
theatres can use the contact numbers and inform customers to self isolate at home.
This will help control the spread of the virus.
Unpacked foods such as popcorn, samosa, sweet corn, etc will not be allowed.
Only packed food and beverages will be permitted.
Delivery inside the auditorium won't be allowed during intervals.
Customers have to follow self service.
The government stressed that people must wear their mask correctly, practise social distancing,
follow respiratory etiquettes of sneezing & coughing in one's elbow
or tissues and disposing them properly. Spitting is prohibited.
The temperature of ACs must remain in the 24-30°C range.
Digital no-contact transactions for tickets will be preferred.
Even for food & beverages, only digital no-contact transactions will be accepted.
All patrons have to install the Aarogya Setu app on their phones.
Strict action must be taken against those violating the rules.
Theatres will not open in containment zones. They will only open in non-containment zones.

The USA's NAD and 5 Deaf Americans had filed a lawsuit

to provide ASL interpreters for all its COVID-19 briefings.
The Judge wrote a 25-page opinion
and the NAD has successfully shown that the White House has violated laws by not providing ASL interpreters.
The Judge supported NAD and said that Deaf people are suffering
because they do not have access to information about personal safety, public health and the economy.
There is no ASL interpretation for the spoken press briefings. Hence, interpreters must be provided.
All the 50 states in the USA and local cities provide in-frame ASL interpreters
but the White House does not.
The White House had said that they provide accessibility by giving
subtitles and transcripts in all their videos.
The White House is not violating any laws.
But the Judge did not agree with them.
The Judge agreed with NAD’s argument that there are Deaf people who understand very little english.
There are many Deaf individuals who rely on ASL.
The Judge has said the White House and NAD must discuss the details of how to provide interpreters.
The judge said it has made the order but is allowing time for the enforcement till the specifics are cleared out.

number of downloads, the number of years its been on the market, etc. then download.

people download these apps as they are free and think it is quick and cheap.

On 29th July 2020, the New Education Policy was approved by the Union Cabinet.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the policy was a much awaited reform in the education sector
and it will transform millions of lives in the times to come.
PM Modi said that the New Education Policy is based on "access, equity, affordability and accountability".
According to modi this will bring in an era of transformation and knowledge.
Modi said, "Respecting the spirit of 'Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat' they would promote Indian languages, including Sanskrit.
Many foreign languages will also be offered at secondary level.
Indian Sign Language (ISL) will be standardized across the country.
Highlights of National Education Policy 2020.
1. The mother tongue/ local/ regional language is to be the medium of instruction in all schools
up to Class 5 or preferably till Class 8 and beyond.
Sanskrit will be offered at all levels and foreign languages from the secondary school level.
However no language will be imposed on any student, they are free to chose what they want.
2. NIOS will develop high-quality modules to teach Indian Sign Language.
They will also teach Deaf children other basic subjects using ISL.
3.The 10+2 structure will be replaced with 5+3+3+4.
It will consist of 12 years of school and three years of preschool.
A foundational stage for ages three to eight,
pre-primary for ages eight to eleven,
a preparatory stage for ages 11 to 14
and a secondary stage for ages 14 to 18.
4. As per the new policy exams will not be held every year.
School students will sit only for three exams in Classes 3, 5 and 8.
Assessment in other years will be more competency based which will test their concepts, understandings and development.
5. Board exams will continue to be held for Classes 10 and 12
but these will be re-designed with holistic development as the aim.
6. The government has said that the policy aims at reducing the load of studies on students
and allowing them to become more "multi-disciplinary".
Education was always considered more important than extra curricular activities like sports, dance, signing, etc
Now it will all be included in education as it is very important.
There will be inclusion of arts subjects for students studying science subjects and vice versa.
Multi-lingualism will be encouraged.
7. The government proposed higher education institutions like the IITs to aim for holistic education by 2040.
There will be inclusion of arts subjects for students studying science subjects and vice versa.
8. The NEP 2020 proposed a four year undergraduate programme.
Students leaving after 1 year will get a certificate.
Students exiting after two years will get a diploma.
A bachelor's degree will be awarded after completing four years of study.
9. A HECI will be set up to regulate 3,000 higher education institutions.
The HECI will not have jurisdiction on law and medical colleges.

NGO Swabhiman and the NCPEDP conducted two surveys.
90% of the students who participated were from Odisha,
and 10% from Jammu and Kashmir, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.
It included 2,178 students from classes I to XII,
1,041 parents, 303 teachers and 104 adults with disabilities.
The disability categories included orthopedic impairment, Blind, Deaf, intellectual challenges and multiple disorders.
On 18th July the report, titled ‘Digital Education in India: Will students with disabilities miss the bus?’ was released.
In the survey majority of the students with disabilities said that online learning was a big hurdle for them.
About 56.5% of students with disabilities said
that they were struggling but they are still irregularly attending classes.
Around 77% of students said they will not be able to cope and would fall behind in learning.
The report said that 90% parents of the students with disabilities said
teachers were not giving them attention.
86% said they did not know how to use technology.
81% teachers said they did not have accessible educational material for online learning.
The teachers said that 64% of students did not have smartphones or computers at home.
The surveys also found that 67% of students
expressed the need for laptops, smartphones or tablets for educational purposes.
Around 74% of them said they needed data/Wifi support.
77% asked for study material in formats suitable for children with disabilities.
61% needed scribes and attendants.
44% students said that no Sign Language interpreters were present in the webinars.
The report has recommended educational material in alternative formats to suit specific needs of individuals.
All children with disabilities cannot be merged into one group as they are persons with different needs.

On 20th July the Director General of Health Services (DGHS) Ministry of Health wrote a letter
to state authorities stating that the public is using the N95 masks inappropriately.
DGHS Rajiv Garg in the letter said,
Use of valved N95 masks are not safe and can spread coronavirus
I will tell you about the N95 Masks:
N95 respirator is used to protect the person from airborne particles
and from liquid contaminants.
N-95 masks filter 95% of airborne particles.
The edges of the respirator form a seal around the nose and mouth and are mainly designed for health care workers.
They are also used at construction sites to protect the person from dust particles.
But there are some types of N95 masks that are not as beneficial.
There are some N95 masks that have a 'One-way Valve'.
One-way valve do not filter the water droplets coming out of your mouth and risk spread of infection.
This is not safe.
A perfect face mask should prevent you from catching a respiratory illness and should also protect others.
A N95 mask that has a two-way valve can filter out particles during both inhaling and exhaling.
However, these are mostly used by health professionals as they are more exposed to infected patients.
The government issued an advisory in April saying
while coming out people can use homemade masks.
The advisory said that any used cotton cloth can be cut into a face cover.
The colour of the cloth is not important
but it is important that cloth is washed in salted boiling water for five minutes
and dried well before making the face cover.
The mask should fit the face well and there should be no gaps on the sides.
It advised people to wash their hands thoroughly before wearing the face cover.
When the face cover gets damp or humid, it should be changed and a fresh mask should be used.
Or if you want to reuse the mask you can wash it and then use it.
Cloth masks without cleaning should never be reused.
Never share the face cover with anyone. Every member in a family should have a separate face cover.

and some rely totally on Sign Language.

she found it very difficult to communicate with her colleagues.

the Deaf Community has been demanding governments to officially recognise Sign Language

The petition against the Government College of Arts Chandigarh.

The college has a general qualifying standard of 40% in the aptitude test.
But the SC/ST candidates are given a relaxation to 35%.
However, people with disability have the same qualifying criteria as the general candidates.
But SC/ST candidate are given relaxation.
People from SC/ST castes have been oppressed and face barriers in the society. Hence, they are given reservations.
However, people with disabilities have faced the same problems,
but still they were being included in general category. This is why Aryan filed the petition.
A three judge Bench of the Supreme Court announced their decision about this case on 8th July 2020
and said, "A similar case was filed in the Delhi High Court in 2012
by Anmol Bhandari against the Delhi Technological University.
The case was about people with disabilities being included in the general category and treated differently from SC/ST.
In the Anmol Bhandari case, the High Court has correctly said that people suffering from disabilities
have also been socially oppressed. Hence they should be given the reservations.
Even the people with disabilities have faced the same barriers. Their lives were never equal to others.
They never had accessibility. Including them in the general criteria would be wrong.
They said that People with Disabilities would be entitled to the same benefits as SC/ST.
The Supreme Court supported the Delhi High Court's decision.
The Supreme Court rejected the Government College of Arts Chandigarh’s decision,
and said that from now all persons suffering from disabilities will be entitled to the same benefits as SC/ST candidates.
If SC/ST students require a minimum 35% to seek admission,
then the same shall apply for people with disabilities in future.”
The Supreme Court allowed Aryan Raj to apply for a fresh the year.
From the High Court Order, the Supreme Court quoted,
We cannot lose sight of the fact there are multiple types of intellectual/mental disabilities
and there are different types of physical disabilities. These two categories of disabilities are very different.
People with intellectual & mental disabilities have certain limitations.
Their courses must be made according to their specific needs and must not be generalised.
The course work must be designed keeping mind slow learners, people with cerebral palsy and other mental disabilities.
Please remember people with physical disablities are different.
They must also try to increase the number of seats to include students with disabilities.
Advocate Rajan Mani, who was also the High Court’s adviser in the Anamol Bhandari case
and also advised for Mr. Aryan Raj’s case in the Supreme Court.
He said that the Supreme Court's endorsement of the High Court judgment
and quoting its orginal order, was a huge fillip to disabled persons’ rights.
Mr. Mani said, “Till now candidates with disabilities were not able to get benefit of reservation in education and employment
because they were treated by general standards.
Now public sector employers and colleges/universities
will have to allow the same relaxations to them as to SC / ST candidates.”

After COVID-19, the world may now have to be worried about the Bubonic Plague.
On 7th June, China confirmed a case of Bubonic Plague
in Bayannur which is in the Inner Mongolia of China.
Bubonic Plague is not a new disease but it has no treatment.
In the 14th century, it killed around 50 million people in Europe.
It has caused the most dangerous pandemics in history.
A case has been discovered in the city of Bayannur which is now on high alert.
By 6th June the local authorities had issued a warning, which will last a year.
The warning issued for the plague is a level 3 warning.
Level 1 signifies a dangerous outbeak. The severity of the infection reduces with each level.
Level 4 being the mildest.
The Level 3 warning denotes a moderate risk and will applicable for the rest of the year.
The patient is isolated and treated in hospital and is stable.
It is a very infectious disease and is transmitted through flea bites and infected rats.
If treated early, the patient can be saved.
If not treated on time, the infection can spread causing pneumonia and difficulty breathing.
The Symptoms of Bubonic Plague are,
Swollen Lymph Nodes, fever, Chills, Headache, Fatigue and Muscle Ache.
Bayannur health authorities are urging people to take extra precautions
to minimize the risk of human-to-human transmission.
Marmots are large ground squirrels that are eaten in some parts of China and Mongolia.
Marmots have caused plague outbreaks in the region.
Authorities have also warned the public to stay away and inform them of any dead or sick Marmots.
In 1911 in northeast China,
the consumption of Marmots, caused the Pneumonic Plague epidemic which killed 63,000 people.
Marmots were hunted for its fur, which was popular among international traders.
Due to the trade, the fur came in contact with many and spread the virus.
The 1911 epidemic was controlled within a year.
But marmot-related plague infections have persisted decades later.
In Mongolia last week,
two cases of Bubonic Plague were confirmed in Mongolia in brothers
who had both eaten marmot meat. Thus their infection was confirmed.
Last May a couple in Mongolia
due to their cultural beliefs ate the raw kidney of a marmot.
They believed it is a remedy for good health.
However the couple died.
WHO has said they are monitoring the situation in China.

On 6th June an open letter by 239 scientists from 32 countries
was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases Journal.
It was directed towards the medical community and National & International organisations such as WHO, ICMR, etc.
It said COVID-19 could be airborne.
The letter showed evidence that
microdroplets released by COVID infected patients, during coughing, sneezing or talking,
remain in the air and can infect people at up to 2 metres distance.
The WHO had earlier said that COVID-19 is not airborne
and only spreads through small water droplets from nose or mouth, which come out while coughing or sneezing.
After the release of the letter,
Benedetta Allegranzi, the WHO's technical lead for infection prevention and control,
said at a virtual press conference,
Particles of COVID-19 virus can float in the air in crowded areas, closed, poorly ventilated areas
and infect individuals.
Evidence still needs to be collected and properly understood. After which an announcement will be made.
So far, WHO as well as various other medical associations
have encouraged people to regularly wash hands, maintain social distance, and
precautions against coming in contact with droplets.
If it is confirmed that the virus can spread through air,
then countries across the world will have to make changes to their safety guidelines.

From 2011 to 2018, researchers took 30,000 nasal swabs from pigs.

They were used to study flu,

Blood tests found that 10.4% of swine workers had already been infected.

Sachin got himself screened by a doctor and procured a health certificate as well.
He presented the certificate to the Mulund police and requested them to allow him to go back to Ambajogai.

He kept taking breaks at various districts.

He kept talking breaks. But he struggled a lot.
Despite getting blisters on his feet, he continued to walk.
The skin between his toes began to chafe.
Pradeep kept calling to make sure he was okay but Sachin kept walking.

The truck was halted at a police check-point 10 km from Ahmednagar.

RGIA airport in Hyderabad announced an innovative digital solution.
They will introduce contactless terminal entry for air travelers.
In its press note GMR Hyderabad International Airport Limited said
they have come up with a very effective new rule.
Earlier when there was no coronavirus, the air passengers showed their ticket and photo ID to CISF personnel for verification .
On verification, passengers were allowed to enter.
Now the process has changed as they have installed high-definition cameras.
Now the passengers will display the documents in front these cameras
and a CISF Personnel who will be sitting far away from the passenger will verify the document on a computer monitor.
Then the passenger will be allowed to enter the terminal. There will be no contact whatsoever.
Earlier boarding pass and baggage tags were handed to passengers.
Now all counters have been fitted with acrylic shields.
Earlier, at the check-in counters once the staff approves the boarding pass, it will not be given by hand.
When the passenger approaches the counters fitted with glass shields,
the printing machine will face the passenger. Once the staff approves the pass the passenger can collect it.
The passengers have to themselves collect baggage tags as well.
Before take off, passengers will not be individually screened for high temperatures.
As it could lead to the spread of the virus.
There will be thermal cameras to measure the temperature of every passenger.
Passengers will be screened through computers.
If anyone is found with a high fever, they will be stopped.
They will not be allowed to board the flight.
Health officials will be alerted about this.
Such digital solutions will be used to provide a contactless travel.

Gabi Cirlig is a cybersecurity researcher that studies data hacking on various devices.
While using the Xiaomi's Redmi Note 8, he found that,
the phone was recording all the activities performed on it.
Generally while browsing through webpages like google, one can view the search history even after the page is closed.
The incognito mode allows you to browse webpages without saving your search histrory.
Cirlig found that, the phone recorded the search history in incognito mode as well.
Accessing folders, images, Apps, shopping and any form of activity performed on the phone was being recorded.
He was shocked to find this.
Cirlig said, recorded data was sent to servers of a Chinese company, Alibaba, which were rented by Xiaomi.
Cirlig also tested 3 Xiaomi devices –  Xiaomi Mi 10, Xiaomi Redmi K20 and Xiaomi Mi MIX 3
and found that they are also recording user data.
Xiaomi’s USP is cheap devices that have many same qualities as higher-end smartphones.
But for customers, that low cost could come with a hefty price: their privacy.
In reply to the Cirlig's research, Xiaomi said,
“The research claims are untrue. Xiaomi's top concern is security. We do not record user data.
We have followed all the laws and regulations.
But they said that their mobiles record data for analysis.
All data is recorded after receiving permission from the user.
If the user does not give permission, it does not record the data.
On May 3, Xiaomi announced that in its next update, customers will have the option to stop their visited websites being recorded.

Edgard Ziebat, a 40-year-old German national
landed at the Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA) in Delhi from Vietnam on March 18th.
He had a connecting flight to Istanbul, Turkey from Delhi airport.
However his connecting flight to Turkey was canceled due to the COVID-19 crisis.
After announcement Edgard was stuck.
Then India canceled all international flights from 22nd March 2020 due to the COVID-19 outbreak.
Because of this announcement Edgard was stuck in the Delhi Airport.
One of the officers at the airport said,
“Since the flights were cancelled, Edgard stayed in the transit along with other stranded passengers from other countries.
Embassies of all the other nationals were informed.
The Indian immigration officers informed German embassy that Edgard is stuck in Delhi Airport.
German embassy informed the Indian immigration officers that Edgard is a wanted criminal in Germany.
Now Edgard was found in Delhi, India.
German embassy informed that Edgard has many cases against him.
But since he was on foreign land, they would not be able to take his custody.
Edgard was not given an Indian visa as he was merely supposed to catch his transit flight to Turkey from India.
Now since he is stranded in India, the officials refused to give him a visa due to his criminal record.
For the last 54 days, he has been staying in the transit area of the airport.
He reads magazines, talks to his friends and family on the phone
he talks to the housekeeping and security staff and eats at the airport’s fast food outlets.
He sleeps anywhere in the transit area, on benches, floors as he is all alone in the transit area.
Edgard has told the officials that he can manage his expenses.
Indian authorities had tried to send Edgard to Turkey a few days ago on a relief flight.
Indian authorities requested the Turkish authorities, to include Edgard on the flight.
Turkish authorities refused and said that the flight was for Turkish nationals only.
He is still stranded at the airport.
Airport authorities have given him recliner, mosquito net, food and basic essential items.
The authorities regularly visit Edgard to check his health.
They have found that he has visas of many countries.
He is ready to buy a ticket and leave the airport. This will be possible only when the international flights start.
But it is not sure when. All he can do is wait.

Let me tell you the three categories.
For Mild/ Very Mild/ Pre-symptomatic Cases admission is necessary.
If 10 days after the start of the symptoms, they do not have a fever for 3 days,
then without testing they can be discharged.
As the guidelines, after discharge the patients have to follow home isolation for seven days.
If their oxygen levels are above 95% then they are healthy.
If the patient’s oxygen level drops below 95 %, then the patient will be shifted to COVID Health Center.
If the oxygen levels fall below 90%, patients may have lethargy, confusion, or mental disruption.
For patients admitted having moderate cases.
If after ten days of the start of symptoms,
there is no fever for three days
and the oxygen level is above 95% for the four days without oxygen support then will be discharged.
They also will be discharged without testing.
They will also be advised for home isolation for seven days.
If the moderate case’s fever does not solve, they will need oxygen support.
Once they are better and oxygen levels are normal,
after three days they will discharged.
If their levels are still low, they will be monitored and then they will be discharged after 3 days.
Severe cases of COVID-19 patients who already have HIV or those who have undergone transplant surgery like Kidney.
Such patients have a very weak immune system.
Mild and moderate cases can be discharged.
For severe cases they need to be moderated by the doctor.
Once their symptoms go away they will not be discharged but
they will have to do the RT-PCR test.

23 Deaf people from Madhya Pradesh were working in Private companies at Delhi and Haryana.
Once the lockdown due to COVID-19 was imposed, they were unable to go back to MP.
They had to stay put as no mode of transportation was available.
On 29th April 2020, they had sent messages with photos saying “Help me, I cannot hear or speak.”
After that Mr. Gyanendra Purohit Director of NGO Anand Survey Society and his wife Monika Purohit,
saw these messages and got in touch with the 23 Deaf individuals.
They had become restless due to the three lockdowns and wanted to go back to their home towns.
They wanted to go home as they were suffering to make ends meet.
Mr Purohit and his wife got in touch with the Haryana Police,
Delhi Police and the Madhya Pradesh government. They discussed a plan to send the Deaf individuals back home.
Mr Purohit and his wife planned the rescue by communicating with them in sign language and through emails.
Communication was a huge challenge and had to be done through video calls.
It was fortunate that they had smartphones and so video calls and GPS could be used.
A police officer from MP staying in Delhi also helped.
With his help, the Deaf from different parts of Delhi and Haryana
were transported to one meeting place. From there they would start their journey to MP.
Accomplishing this was a huge challenge.
Three of the Deaf individuals were from containment zones and buses were not allowed to enter the area.
They were unable to make calls also due to internet issues.
Since buses weren't allowed in containment areas it became extremely difficult.
On 4th May Mr. Purohit and his wife took the responsibility
of waking them up to make sure they reached on time.
One of them stayed far away from the meeting point,
so he started walking at 2 am to reach the destination.
Everyone was picked up from 6 spots and they safely reached Gwalior, MP.
All the Deaf persons safely went back to their homes in their own vehicles.
Technology such as social media, messaging and video-calling apps have proved to be a boon.
Without it, it not have been possible help the Deaf reached safely.

One such new treatment which is being tried is Plasma Therapy.
Plasma is a yellowish fluid present in the blood.
So what is Plasma Therapy?
In this treatment, plasma from a COVID-19 patient who has recovered from the disease,
is transfused into a coronavirus patient who is in critical condition.
The Plasma transfusion helps strengthen the immunity of the second patient to fight the Coronavirus.
The ICMR has recently allowed states to start clinical trials of plasma therapy.
Nearly 100 institutes are researching if plasma therapy is safe and efficient in treating COVID-19 patients.
A doctor in Kerala said that the transfusion process is not as easy.
Separation of plasma from blood required the help of quality machines.
To test a person's immunity for the plasma transfusion also requires different machines.
These machines need to be of high quality and they are not available in India.
They have to be imported from Germany.
In India Kerala, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Punjab have already started testing Plasma Therapy.
Plasma Therapy was also used to treat Spanish Flu in 1918
and to treat H1N1 infection in 2009.
In 2014, the World Health Organization (WHO) had recommended Plasma Therapy to treat Ebola virus.
The plasma from one recovered person can help two people.
China, UK and the USA have also started testing Plasma Therapy to cure COVID-19.
A 49 year old person suffering from COVID-19 in Delhi Max Hospital,
was the first patient who was administered plasma therapy.
Hope the Plasma therapy proves successful in treating COVID-19.

Viruses and the disease that cause them have different names.
People often know the name of a disease, but not the name of the virus that causes it.
For example everyone knows about the dangerous disease AIDS.
Which virus causes it? It is HIV.
Currently the disease that has spread all over the world is the Coronavirus.
When the disease first spread it was called the ‘2019 Novel Coronavirus’
On 11 February 2020, the WHO Chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus announced,
the new name of this disease. ‘COVID-19’
He said that, in COVID-19 'co' stands for corona,
'vi' stands for the word virus,
'd' for disease,
while '19' signifies the year of its initial identification, meaning 2019. Hence the name COVID-19.
But why was the name changed? According to International rules
when a new disease immerges it can not be named after any place such as India,USA, UK, Japan, China etc.
It can not be named in reference to any religion or animal.
For example Swine Flu, which was named after Pigs that cause it, spread all over.
This affected the pork bussiness due to the stigmatisation of the disease.
Similarly even the disease Ebola was named after a place in Africa where it originated.
This is why WHO adopted the name ‘COVID-19’ so that there is no connection to any religion, place or animal.
The name of the Virus that spreads COVID-19 was not randomly selected.
When the virus immerged it was properly studied. Its genetic features, mode of transmission and other factors were understood.
After this the WHO announced 'SARS-CoV-2’ to be the name of the virus.
The name SARS-CoV-2 was given because the genetic structure of the virus was similar to the SARS virus that spread in China in 2003.
So now you won’t get confused as the Coronavirus was renamed COVID-19 but the meaning is the same.

Over the last few months, there have been many rumours
about telecom companies like Bharti Airtel, Vodafone, Idea, etc shutting down.
Why so? Well there is a big battle between the Central Government & telecom companies.
This is because telecom companies owe money to the Central Government.
Which they haven't paid yet leading to a big problem.
The Telecom companies have to pay the government AGR.
What does this mean? Well in simple words,
it means that the telecom companies have to pay the government license fees, tax, spectrum fees, etc.
Spectrum fees means when telecom companies are set up, tower are erected
for creating signals using air waves to provide communication services.
For this they need to pay the Central Government.
Now the issue is that the Central Government has its own method of calculating the AGR,
which the telecom companies do not agree with.
Telecom companies have complained against this many times.
Now finally, the Supreme Court has announced their verdict.
The judges ordered the telecom companies to pay all the money they owed to the government as soon as possible.
This amount that the companies have to pay is enormous.
The telecom companies have to pay the governement a sum of Rs 1.5 lakh crore.
Now the major trouble is that these companies do not have the money and going through massive losses.
Vodafone has to pay Rs 55,000 crore to the central government.
This includes penalties, interest, etc.
Vodafone’s lawyers have clearly said that,
in order to repay the Rs 55,000 crore they would have sell all their assets.
Their lawyer has said clealry that if Vodafone does this they will have to shut down.
Bharti Airtel has to pay a total of Rs 35,000 crore.
They have already paid Rs 10,000 crore.
They will pay the balance Rs 25,000 crore after an internal financial assessment of the company.
If companies are forced to pay, they may all have to shut down.
Just imagine what happens if big companies like Vodafone shut down?
Earlier there were so many telecom companies competing against each other by offering cheap data services.
If companies are forced to pay, only 1 or 2 companies will remain in the market.
Then the prices will shoot up.
If telecom companies shut down, many would lose their jobs.
Even if telecom companies shut down, they will not stop using the service because communication is a necessity.
If the only two companies hike their prices, people will have no choice but to pay.
Currently it is pretty evident that the Indian economy is in shambles.
If such big huge companies begin to shut down, it can dangerously affect the economy.
There is no clear answer about what will happen now.
Companies are hoping that the government will come to some agreement.
The next Supreme Court hearing is on 17th March we all have to wait to see what the future is for these companies.
Did you see the video of the girl playing the violin during a brain surgery?
Do you think she was bored and wanted to play the violin keep herself busy.
No I am joking.
Let me tell you why she was playing the violin during the surgery.
The woman’s name is Dagmar Turner and she is 53 years old.
She had a tumor in her right frontal lobe which is this portion of the brain. It was very dangerous.
We all have our own skills that we are good at be in dance, singing, sports, etc.
When you participate in a dance competition and perform,
where does the skill come from? This ability is stored in the brain.
Similar the ability to sing and other abilities are stored in the mind.
The brain stores various skills.
Similarly, Turner ability to play the Violin is stored in her brain.
Right next to that place, the tumour has grown.
The distance between them is their distance from the tumour was as narrow as a credit card. This is very dangerous & difficult surgery.
Turner was very afraid.
This is because, if during the surgery the part of her brain responsible for violin playing gets damaged, she would lose her ability forever.
She was worried because, she has been playing the violin since the age of 10.
If she lost the ability now, she would be heartbroken.
She did not want to lose her ability to play the violin.
Dr. Keyoumars Ashkan, in the last one year, has successfully performed 400 tumour removals.
Before the surgery, once the tumour is found then the operation is performed.
However during the surgery after regular intervals the person is roused asked questions such as their name, age. Once they confirm
the surgery resumes. They are again woken up and asked if they remember to sing.
This is because if the patient is not roused and after the surgery
the patient may wake up and lose their abilities. They want to avoid this.
This is why before the procedure Turner's tumour was located and her brain was mapped.
She was made to play the violin, to figure out which areas of her brain were active when she played the violin.
Two hours later, the operation began and Turner was conscious unlike other patients,
she was made to play the violin.
She continued playing the violin during the surgery.
If she stopped playing, it would mean the portion with that ability was compromised.
If she continue playing, it means all is well.
The doctors successfully remove over 90% of the tumour
and she was still playing the violin. This meant her memory was intact.
She went home to her husband and son three days after the procedure.
Turner hopes to be back with her orchestra very soon and start playing the violin.

which was headed by Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray in Mumbai.

All over India Hearing as well as Deaf people hate waiting in traffic.

Day by day honking is increasing and everyone is fed up.
Am I right?
Mumbai is the most noisiest city in the world due to so much honking.
Because in Mumbai if the signal is red for 60 seconds, still people honk hoping to clear the path for themselves.
All of this, when the signal isn't even green yet.
The Traffic Police were tired of people honking despite the Red signal.
They were fed up of all the noise pollution.
In Mumbai due to the metro construction, the roads are narrower leading to traffic
leading to continuous honks to move ahead.
Similarly even the BMC keeps digging up roads to fix pipes or any other work.
Due to narrow roads people still honks.

But one problem of traffic and honking is enormous and the Traffic Police really wanted to do something to put an end to it.
They then came up with an unique idea to slove it. Look at the video!
Did you saw the video? Did you understand? I am sure some of you haven't, so let me explain.
Let me tell you, the traffic Police's unique idea to solve the honking problem.
When cars stop at the signal, once the timer which is set for 60 is up, the traffic starts moving.
Similarly cars stopped at the signal where a timer was attached.
Next to it a Decibel meter was attached.
Just like we have units of measurements such as Kilo Meter to measure distance,
milimeter to measure the width of a mobile
and many others, there is a machine that measure Decibel.
When the Decibel meter is at 0 and the timer is ticking away, vehicles at the red light
have no patience. They keep honking as they are in a hurry.
People start shouting and yelling. All of this noise is measure by the machine.
While the timer is ticking, the decibel meter starts increasing.
It continues to measure all the sound. When the meter goes about 85 DB.
Then when the Timer hits 0 seconds it resets to 90.
As the meter measures the noise, the timer will keep reseting.
People were very confused.
Once the timer is up, the cars must move so why is it reseting and signal turning red?
People started to look around at each other with a confused look.
Some people were even laughing looking at the timer reseting.
People failed to understand but eventually they realised they did
when they saw a sign that read "Honk More, Wait More".
This meant the timer will keep reseting if people continued to honk.
So it's better to stop honking, have patience and wait for the timer to hit zero.
Then they move ahead and the timer won't reset.
Everyone understood because of the sign.
They then waited for the timer to hit zero and go ahead.
When everyone understood this, two traffic policemen high-fived each other for finding a solution.
Video of this has gone viral all over social media.

Last year, Pune's famous tea shop, Yewale Amruttulya in Maharashtra
attracted many customers & earned a whopping Rs 12 lakhs a month.

The FDA is a government organisation which is the Food & Drug Administration.
The FDA collected tea samples from the shop.
The samples were sent to a government run food lab in Mysuru, Karnataka.
After testing they found the samples were adulterated with a dye to darken the colour of the tea powder.
The name of the dye used in the tea powder is tartrazine.
It is harmful to one's health and is banned. However they are still selling it in their tea.
FDA has caught the famous Pune tea selling their adulterated tea.
There are some colours which are permitted to be used in products like sweets and fruit juices.
These are non-toxic and can be used. However the Tartrazine is extremely toxic & bad for health.
This is not the first time, earlier in September 2019,
the Yewale Food Products factory in Katraj was given a stop work notice.
The FDA found products like sugar, tea masala, tea powder which were being sold.

Dhruvi Gohil was a 16-year-old student from Borivali, Mumbai.
She was extremely smart and was a very good student.
This young girl died on the day of her 16th Birthday.
Let me tell you about it.
Dhruvi was preparing for her exams till late night.
The next day she went to have a bath around 6.45 am.
Her parents said that she wanted to wash her hair. You all know women take a long time to wash their hair.
She went inside in the bathroom at 6:45 for a shower
while her parents were busy with their chores.
It had been a while but then her parents realised she was washing her hair so there was no problem.
However from 6:45am it was now 8:00am. It had been too long and they became worried.
They started knocking on the door of the bathroom but there was no response.
Her parents then broke open the door and found Dhruvi was found unconscious,
The right side of her body burnt due to hot water.
They immediately took her to the hospital.
According to Dr Vivek Chaurasia, Dhruvi was then taken to the hospital and she was unconscious.
The doctors then put her on a ventilator.
The next day her brain started swelling, she got convulsions and then she died.
The Doctors who were treating her were neurologists.
According to the doctors, Dhruvi died because of the heaters.
Let me explain.
Gas geysers consume oxygen to generate heat for warming water.
Since it has become cold in Mumbai, the family had completely closed the windows in the bathroom.
The girl just like all human was breathing in oxygen and exhaling Carbon Dioxide.
However in the bathroom, since there was no ventilation, the geyser consumed all the oxygen in the bathroom.
The girl was exhaling carbon dioxide. This gas is not at all good for the body.
There was no source of oxygen because all the windows were shut due to the cold and the increasing Carbon Dioxide is very bad for health.
The geyser continued to consume the oxygen and levels of oxygen kept decreasing.
She continuously exhaling and inhaling the same carbon dioxide which is extremely bad for health.
Doctors say the dangerous carbon dioxide caused her to faint.
After she fainted she remained there from 6:45 to 8:00am.
She was unconscious for around 1 hr 15 mins almost 75 minutes.
She was also getting convulsions and then she died.
Doctors say that Senior citizens and people with respiratory illness are more prone to suffer.
if there is no ventilation in the bathroom.
Doctors have said it is better to crack the window open so that fresh oxygen can circulate in the bathroom.

There has been a lot of confusion about the meaning of the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).
There are some completely in favour of the Act.
Whereas some are completely against it & there are many arguments.
Many Deaf individuals have contacted us for an objective explanation of the CAB & NRC.
Let me tell you about it.
The Citizenship Act was passed in 1955.
Amit Shah presented the Citizenship Amendment Bill (CAB) in the Lok Sabha were it was passed by majority votes.
It was then presented in the Rajya Sabha, where it was again passed by majority votes.
This was then presented to the President Ram Nath Kovind who approved it.
This means it is now the Citizenship Amendment Act.
You may be confused because I signed CAB earlier and now I am saying CAA. What is the difference between the two.
The Citizenship Amendment Bill was being discussed to be passed in both the houses.
When the President approved it, then it became the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA).
Let me explain you in detail about CAA.
The CAA focuses on three countries, which are Pakistan, Bangladesh & Afghanistan.
All those who have entered India before 31st December 2014, will be given Indian Citizenship.
Citizenship will be given to people of 6 religions.
Hindu, Parsi, Sikh, Jain, Christian & Buddhist immigrants will be given citizenship.
The Government will give them fast track Indian citizenship in six years.
The CAA focuses on these 6 religions because,
People of these religions face a lot of persecution in those three countries.
This is why the immigrants will be allowed to stay in India.
From the three countries, if an immigrant is being oppressed or has any other problem and has come to India,
and if that person is a Muslim, he will not be given Indian Citizenship.
Only the 6 religions will be supported.
What is the NRC? Let me explain.
This is the full form of NRC.
The NRC was implemented under the Citizenship Act 1955
It was only for the state of Assam and not for the entire country.
It was implemented during 2013–2014, to identify illegal immigrants.
This was by the order of the Supreme Court.
There are many illegal immigrants staying in Assam.
This is why the number of Assamese people is reducing and illegal immigrants is increasing.
The main aim of the NRC in Assam was to identify the number of illegal immigrants in Assam
to make sure Assam’s culture is protected.
In Assam people had to prove that they are Indian citizens by showing various documents.
On 31st August, the Indian government created and released the list of NRC which contained all the legal citizens of Assam.
However there were 19 lakh people which included immigrants and residents of Assam without proper documentation.
These people were not included in the list.
These people could lose their citizenship.
Since these 19 lakh immigrants could lose their citizenship, they can appeal to the court.
After going through all the documentation, if the court is still not satisfied, they will not be given Citizenship.
These immigrants will then be sent to India's first detention centres in Goalpara, Assam.
This detention centre is the size of 7 football fields.
The people without Indian Citizenship will be sent to these detention centres.
The government will care for their food and other amenities but they aren't allowed to leave.
Earlier the NRC was only for Assam, right?
However on 19th November 2019, Amit Shah announced in the Rajya Sabha that the NRC will be implemented all over India.
This means that, people all over India will have to prove their citizenship by showing various documents.
If people do not have clear documentation about their citizenship, they will be sent to the detention centres or will be deported.
The construction of detention centres in Maharashtra has already started.
However the Indian Government has not announced the process and implementation of the NRC.
The list of documents needed such as PAN, Aadhar, etc have not been clearly announced & it is very vague.
But they have already started constructing detention centres.
On 22nd December while addressing a gathering at the Ram Leela Maidan, PM Modi said that
there was no discussion of implementing NRC all over India.
It was implemented in Assam only as per the Supreme Courts orders.
PM Modi said this but Amit Shah had said that the NRC will be implemented all over India. How contradictory!

The next video we will release is about the connection between the NRC & the CAA and why people are protesting all over India.

On 13th December 2019, Friday the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly has passed two Bills,
to expedite the procedure of work in cases of sexual crimes.
It is called Andhra Pradesh Disha Bill.
A severe punishment will be given within 21 days.
The death penalty or severe punishment will be given within 21 days.
As we all know in Telengana, a veterinerian doctor was raped and burnt her body.
To keep the girl’s identity private her name was then changed to Disha.
This is why the Bill was called the Disha Bill.
Disha Bill states that rape,
acid attacks,
social media harassment,
stalking,
voyeuristic act such as a person gaining sexual pleasure by watching a rape or by looking at someone bathing through a camera,
and many such offences will be covered under the Disha Bill.
Sexual crimes against children that are covered by the POCSO Act will also be under the Disha Bill.
The Bill says that, investigation of the rape must be completed within seven working days,
the court trial must take 14 days and judgement must be announced within 21 days.
If a person rapes or performs any sexual crimes against children, they can be given life imprisonment.
If a woman is harassed or her images are circulated on social media,
They will be jailed for 2 years.
The second bill that was passed says that 13 special courts will be set in various districts of Andhra Pradesh.
These will focus on rapes and various sexual crimes.
The Bill has been sent to India's President Ram Nath Kovind and waiting for his approval.

Vodafone, Airtel, Idea, Jio all suffered huge losses.
This is why, Jio announced to everyone that,
if a Jio user places a call to any other network even if no one answers,
the customer will have to pay the IUC charges.
If a jio user places a call to any network such as Vodafone or any other network,
and if the call is answered voice call charges according to your plan will be deducted.

will help in the strong development of the bones.
It also helps to maintain a healthy heart.
Eating well will make sure you have healthy muscles.
A healthy diet will ensure healthy nerve signalling.
Why is Calcium and Vitamin-D important for healthy bones?
Your bones contain 99.5% calcium and this is very important for your life.
You all may think focusing on calcium rich foods will keep your bones strong.
However that is not the case.
If you eat both Calcium and Vitamin D your bones will remain strong.
When you consume Calcium and Vitamin D,
the Vitamin D helps bones absorb the Calcium.
Now let me tell you the food sources of Calcium and Vitamin-D.
The sources of Calcium are milk, cheese, curd,
beans, tofu, Chia seeds have calcium,
fish, green vegetables, almonds, etc. all are rich in calcium.
If you eat these, you will remain healthy.
The recommended daily intake of Calcium is 1,000 mg per day for most adults.
When you have a meal that is rich in Calcium you may think that you have consumed 1,000 mg of calcium for the day.
This is not the case. Some foods may have 300mg, some 200 and some may have 100 mg of calcium. The quantity will vary.
You have to make sure you meet the 1,000 mg limit and not go over or below.
Women aged above 50 and everyone over 70 should get 1,200 mg per day.
Children aged between 4-18 years are advised to take 1,300 mg of Calcium per day.
Vitamin D recieved from the sun and absorbed by the body helps to keep the bones strong.
Between 11:00 am to 2:00 pm you must exercise or walk inorder to absorbs the sun's rays.
If you have a Vitamin D defeciency your bones will face many problems in the future.
I know everyone is busy with work but you must to remove time and absorb the sun rays.
Food sources of Vitamin D include fish, eggs, mushrooms, soy milk, orange juice, cereal, and oatmeal.
These are sources of Vitamin D and will ensure you remain healthy.
Apart from following a healthy diet rich in Vitamin D and Calcium
follow these simple tips to improve your bone strength:
1. Exercise on a regular basis
2. Avoid bad posture and make sure you stand straight.
3. Do not eat in excess. Try to control your portions.
4. Avoid excess caffeine and alcohol
5. Reduce your daily salt intake
6. Quit smoking.

Kulbhushan Sudhir Jadhav is an Indian national.
He was a retired naval officer and was not working with the military at all.
On 3rd March 2016 the Pakistan government arrested him in Balochistan, Pakistan.
They arrested him on charges of terrorism and spying for India.
On 23rd March 2016 Pakistan arrested the man but did not inform India immediately.
They informed India very late on 25th March 2016.
This is completely wrong.
There is an international law called the Vienna Convention.
The law has to be followed by all the countries in the world.
It states that if a person is arrested his country must be informed immediately.
The person must not be mistreated and should be respected.
Many such rules were not followed by Pakistan.
They did not follow the Vienna Convention.
They ignored and broke many rules.
Similarly when they arrested Kulbhushan, they informed India late on 25th March.
Secondly Kulbhushan was not allowed to meet with any Indian officials as well.
The case was not carried out in a civilian court but in Pakistan’s Military Court.
When Kulbhushan wanted to choose his lawyer, he was denied that as well.
On 10 April 2017, Pakistan’s Military court sentenced him to death.
Then on 18th May 2017 when India heard about this they appealed
to the ICJ which is the International Court of Justice.
They told them to stop his execution.
India continued to fight and finally stopped it.
India argued with Pakistan and said that they had not followed International rules and it was an extreme injustice.
Yesterday on 17th July 2019 ICJ in Hague, Netherlands
the ICJ suspend Kulbhushan's execution. They finally decided to do this.
They have ordered Pakistan to allow Kulbhushan to meet to Indian government officials.

In Extremely cold temperatures between  -40°C to -70°C can anybody survive?

Just like a block of concrete.
It becomes very hard.
The Jawans said that once they remove the packet, even a hammer can not break it. It is very difficult.
It becomes rock hard in the freezing -40°C to -70°C temperatures.
How do the Jawans survive then?
What do they do with the juice?
They have to boil it in water first. Once it melts,
they can not keep it in a glass. They have to immediately drink it.
This is how they suffer.
The Jawans said that,
it is very easy for people to wake up in the morning and make an omlette
or boil an egg. It is very easy isn't it?

The eggs are like rocks that you can hit someone with.
They say that even a hammer fails to crack the egg.
No matter how hard they hit it, they fail to crack it.
Even after banging the egg on the table it just bounces off without any signs of a crack.
They really suffer a lot.
They said that vegatables like Potatoes, Tomatoes, etc.
all freeze and turn into rocks.

First, they have to boil them. Once it softens they cook and eat them.

people all over India were very shocked.

The legal limit for an abortion in Maharashtra is 4-5 months or 20-weeks of the pregnancy.
The Bombay High Court (HC) on 3rd April 2019 declared that,
a doctor can perform an abortion if the woman's pregnancy exceeds 20-weeks.
If there is a danger to the mother's physical and mental health,
then the pregnancy can be terminated.
If the foetus has any abnormalities, such as a heart defect or any extremely serious condition,
then the pregnancy can be terminated.
The Bombay High Court said that, if the mother wants to have an abortion,
she can only do so after taking the courts permission.
Since there are many cases of such requests,
the Bombay HC has ordered the State Government
to solve these cases.
The High Court also told the state government
to create guidelines for the medical board to follow.
The HC has given them 3 months
to set up such medical boards in every district in Maharashtra.
There are many cases where in an abortion post 20-weeks,
the child is born alive.
In such cases the HC said that the hospital or clinic will have to take responsibility
for the child's medical treatment.
If in an abortion post 20-weeks, the child is born alive
and the parents are not in a position to take responsibility of the child,
then the government will step in and care for the child.
The Bombay HC has told the state government to make sure their new policies
protect the mother as well as the baby.

They said that movie-ticketing platforms should only charge the price of the ticket,
and not the extra fees.

movie-ticketing companies must charge customers only the price of the ticket.

also charge extra fees.
The Railway Police Force (RPF) received a tip-off
that, from Kalyan station a ticket was purchased with a fake disability certificate.
On 20th March 2019, the RPF were waiting in the train.
The passengers were all sitting in the train.
When the Ticket Conductor arrived he starting checking everyone's tickets.
When he asked for one of the passengers disability certificate,
the RPF immediately caught the passenger.
The person's name was Ashok Mahajan aged 47 years and his son Rajdhar Mahajan aged 22 years.
They were both arrested.
During the interrogation, the man said he owned a store in Ulhasnagar.
When he was questioned regarding the fake certificates,
he told the entire story.
Ashok Mahajan said that in his store in Ulhasnagar one of his regular customers
named Wadhwa asked Ashok if he wanted a disability certificate.
Wadhwa said the certificate had many benefits.
The certificates would provide concessions, confirmed berth in the railways
and many such benefits.
When he asked Ashok if he wanted it, Ashok agreed.
Ashok said even his son wanted it.
Wadhwa then told Ashok to pay Rs 5,000.
From the Rs 5,000 Wadhwa kept Rs 500 for himself
and paid the agents Rs 4,500 who would procure the certificates.
When the police inspected the certificate,
they found that it was from Thane Civil Hospital
and the signature was of an Orthopaedic surgeon.
When they went to the Thane Civil Hospital and show them the certificate,
a doctor named Dr Kailash said that, an Orthopaedic surgeon can not authorise the certificate.
People with disabilites such as Blind, Deaf, Handicap,etc,
have to be examined by different doctors before they are issued the certificate.

The West Nile Fever, is caused by West Nile Virus (WNV).

swollen lymph glands and skin rash.
When the virus enters the brain it becomes fatal.
WNV should be treated when the initial symptoms manifest.

Kerala's Health Minister KK Shailaja and the Union Health Ministry
are in constant touch. The WHO which is the World Health Organisation's
protocols are being followed as well.
She said when detected with WNV, one must seek medical help at the earliest.
In time, it can be cured.
If there is fever or other symptoms, one must get treated immediately.
The Kerala government is working hard to spread awareness regarding this disease.
They have even carried out various innitiatives to control mosquitoes in the state.
WNV's first case was detected in Uganda's West Nile district in 1937.
WNV has occurred in Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia and Northern America.
Last year in the U.S, many people were detected with this virus.
Union Minister for Finance Shri Piyush Goyal presented the Budget on 1st February 2019.
This Budget provides farmers, labourers & middle class
direct tax benefits and/or tax concessions.
Annual income of upto Rs 5,00,000/- lakh will not be taxable.
If taxpayers have annual gross income upto Rs. 6,50,000/- Lakh,
and they invest Rs 1,50,000/- lakh from this in provident funds, insurance, shares, etc
they will not have to pay tax.
Standard Tax Deduction is applicable for salaried persons.
The amount deducted once a year was Rs 40,000/- now it has been increased to Rs 50,000/-.
If a person has made investments in Post Offices & Banks
the interest earned above Rs 10,000/- was taxable.
This was the old rule.
Now the rule has changed. Interest of upto Rs 40,000/- has been made tax free.
If the rent paid by non-individuals such as corporates,
was upto Rs 1,80,000/- per year, TDS would not be deducted.
If the rent were above Rs 1,80,000/- TDS would be deducted.
Now the rule has changed.
If the annual rent is upto Rs 2,40,000/- TDS will not be deducted.
If the rent were above Rs 2,40,000/- TDS will be deducted.
Earlier Tax returns would take a long time to process.
Similarly, refunds would take a long time to process as well.

Deaf Festival" was organised by the DAI.

Today is the Chinese New Year! Let me tell you about it.
According to English calendar 1st January is the 'New Year'.
According to Hindu calendar Diwali comes in October or November.
Similarly, every year Chinese New Year falls between 21st January and 20th February of the English Calendar.
Every year they celebrate New Year with a fun and floric.
This day is considered as the ending of the winters and the beginning of the spring season in Chinese culture.
Chinese families believe in gathering for the annual reunion dinner. In Diwali we Indians keep our houses clean, go to each others house etc
Similarly it is also a tradition in China to clean their houses, have dinner with family, go to friends or families house and enjoy.
People decorate their houses, windows and doors beautifully with paper-cuts and they also light firecrackers.
It is their belief to use red colours on New Year. They lit red firecrackers, stick red paper-cutsouts and even give money in red envelopes, etc.
There is a very interesting story behind this tradition.
Long ago there was a mythical beast called The Nian that lived under the sea or in the mountains.
Nian would eat villagers, especially children, break houses etc in the middle of the night .
The beast would come only once a year during the days surrounding the New Year.
Once, in order to protect themselves, all the villagers decided to hide from the beast.
An old man appeared before the villagers went into hiding and said that he would stay there at night.
The old man hanged red lanterns, put red papers cutouts and set off firecrackers.
Nian came that night again but the brave old man was sitting there.
Next morning when adults & children came back to their village, they saw that no house was destroyed and neither Nian ate anyone.
The villagers assumed  the old man to be a deity who had come to save them.
The villagers then understood that Nian the beast was afraid of the colour red and loud noises.
After that Nian never came back to the villag and it is believed that he was eventually captured by the Chinese monk deity Hongjun Laozu.
Hence, the Chinese started following the day as their New Year and started hanging red lantern, and red spring scrolls and lighting firecrackers on New Year.

Remember to keep your tray in the over while it is pre-heating
then we're going to prepare our tomato sauce
slice each tomato into 4 parts and remove the parts with the seeds
then put them in the mixer and make a puree

10 mins after cooking the puree, add 15 chopped basil leaves

then switch off the gas and 3/4 tsp rock salt
