roll out each part into a chapati

then make holes in the chapati with a fork like this

Before plating the pizza, there's just one last component left to make

In a huge revelation, a person has revealed that rupees notes worth ₹88,032.5 crores are missing.
Activist Manoranjan Roy filed an RTI application.
It is mandatory for the government to disclose information asked in the RTI.
You all know that RBI is the apex bank of India.
Also India has three units where currency notes are printed.
Our currency notes are printed only in these places under the orders of the RBI.
Once the notes were printed they were then handed over to the RBI who then distribute it to all the banks.
There are rules for all this.
Now this is what happened. The total of the supplied notes from the three mints came to 8,810.65 million pieces. This is the number of notes and not their value.
However, the RBI has received only 7260 million pieces of the ₹500 notes.
These 500 rupees notes were worth ₹88,032.5 crores are missing.
Roy recieved this response to this RTI application.
These notes were supplied to the RBI when Raghuram Rajan was the governor. The governor's signature is on the notes.
Roy then told the CEIB and the ED in order to investigate this discrepancy.
Now the RBI announced that none of the notes are missing.
The RBI said, "These reports are based on erroneous interpretations of information collected from the printing presses.
Notes are not missing. All notes are accounted for.
Members of the public are, therefore, requested to rely on the information published by RBI as we share accurate information."

Every time we get our salary, some money is deducted because of tax.
Why is the tax eating my money and for what?
Every time anyone buys essential items like soap or groceries
or if they go to a restuarant, on the bill you see that there is some tax levied.
When you buy something, you have to pay tax.
For buying anything, we have to keep on paying taxes.
Even when you pay for petrol, the bill includes tax.
We pay so much of tax, what happens to all the tax money?
But in the first place, why do we have to pay tax?
Whenever we pay tax, the money goes to the government.
Government collects the tax money from everyone.
When you get your salary, you plan and budget your expenses
like food, electricity bill, rent, etc. and the balance remains.
All of us do money management and hence save money for the future.
Similarly, the Government also plans things with the tax that is collected.
The money is used for building roads, schools, hospitals, and other infrastructural developments.
This money is also used to support setting up of small businesses.
The government collects the tax money and even uses it to help farmers.
Managing the tax money is not easy and has to be done every year.
The amount of money spent on different things changes from year to year.
For example, during the 2 years of the coronavirus pandemic,
very little budget was set for farmers or for setting up small businesses.
rather the money was used for hospitals, vaccines, etc which the government provided free to people.
It was used for research and treatment of Covid-19.
The budget does not remain the same always and varies according to the situation.
66% of India's population is poor
which means 2 out 3 people are so poor that they do not have enough money to buy essential items.
They can surely not pay tax. This group constitutes 66% of the population!
Only 1% of Indian population pays income tax which is the same as 1 in 100 people.
The remaining 99 people are unable to pay income tax as their salary gets over in paying for innumberable things
or their salary is too low to afford highly priced things.
Government is aware about this and make it affordable by giving subsidy in transportation,
free schooling, subsidy in school fees,
free medical services in hospitals etc. All this is provided from the money collected as tax.
A part of the tax money is used to provide free services like education, medical etc.
What about the remaining money?
India has taken a loan from the United Nation owned World Bank which is situated in USA.
World Bank gives these loans to help countries grow.
India too has taken a loan. It is similar to how we take loans for buying a house, mobile or vehicle.
We too repay the loan in installments and with interest.
Same ways, India has to repay the World Bank loan in installments and with interest.
India owes 600 billion dollars to World Bank. Whoa! Thats a huge amount to be paid back.
10% of the tax money is used on defence.
This includes purchase of high-ended military equipments, fighter planes etc.
It also includes the salary of the military staff.
They have to be paid well as they are the ones who at the time of attack on India,
will help protect the people of India and ensure peace.
Remember, you must pay your tax as the money is used to pay for others things that help the country develop.

Many people do not achieve 7-9 hours of uninterrupted sleep.
This affects their health.
With the current hustle culture, heavy workload, work pressure, and many other factors
people do not think of sleep as a priority.
Inadequate sleep has harmful consequences. Here are some of the effects of sleep deprivation.
Sleep deficiency can easily increase the risk of
heart attacks, stroke, and other cardiovascular problems.
Many researchers have said while we are sleeping, a part of the brain controls the circulatory system.
If you do not sleep well, it can disrupt the parts of the brain that control the circulatory system.
This is one issue. Sleep deprivation also increases blood pressure,
higher heart rate, inflammation, etc.
If you have an interrupted sleep, your decision making and perception is affected.
You become mentally exhausted.
Your efficiency towards work and other skills will reduce throughout the day.
It may even cause driving accidents.
Uninterrupted sleep for 7 - 9 hours keeps you mentally healthy.
You will be able to make proper decisions and judgments. Hence, sleep is important.
While you go to sleep, your immune system produces substances like antibodies
which protect your body from bacteria and viruses.
It is important to sleep for 7-9 hours in order to protect yourself from illnesses.
So, when you do not sleep enough, your immune system gets affected and you may fall sick.
It is believed that adequate sleep can make your memory sharper.
In a 2009 study, American and French researchers said that,
when we learn words, sentences, mathematics etc.
it goes to the brain and when you sleep well,
this information is transferred to the long term memory.

Everyone is aware that packaged water bottles have been used by people since many years.
People consider packaged drinking water as a healthy and clean option as there can be a problem with tap water.
Nowadays drinking from a packaged water bottle has a significant problem
A study was conducted by Columbia University, United States of America.
It studied 25 bottles of water from each of three popular bottled water brands, whose names were not disclosed in the study.
It found nanoplastic particles, which are very tiny and not visible to the naked eye and unknowingly people have been drinking this water.
One of Columbia's biophysicists and study co-author Wei Min said,
"In each 1 litre of bottle, the study detected 1,10,000 to 4,00,000 nanoplastic particles.
How Dangerous!
Out of the various types of nanoplastic particles found, the most common one was the polyethylene terephthalate (PET),
which is the predominant plastic used in the bottled beverage industry like water, soft drinks and juices.
Minute particles of PET likely enter the water through repetitive screwing and unscrewing of the bottle cap
or during bottle compression while drinking from it.
Other commonly found particle was nylon which might have originated from water purification filters.
Similarly, these nanoplastic particles can get collected in our vital organs
heart, kidney and even the bodies of unborn babies by crossing through their placenta.
The entry of dangerous chemicals used in plastic production causes a significant health risk
such as inflammation, respiratory issues & cancer of important organs like kidneys, liver, heart, etc.
It also causes problems in the reproductive system and the nervous system.
Earlier it was better but nowadays plastic is very harmful.
I would advise you to avoid buying packaged water bottle and instead it is better to carry water from home.

The police on 16th September found bodies of four people in Gairigaun area of Tinkune in Kathmandu, Nepal.
The bodies were found in Shree Dibya Sawmill.
Police were shocked to see the gruesome murders. Let me tell you how the police came to know about the incident.

The man worked as a security guard at the sawmill. The fourth victim was 20 year old Nabin Rai.
Police wondered about the reason for the murders.
A 28-year-old man named Dipendra Rai, who lived in the same house, found the bodies.
He immediately rushed to the police station and informed them of the murders.
However, the police arrested him after noticing blood on his clothes.
Rai was released after police found that he had no involvement in the killing.
On the same day on 16th September 2023, the police teams reached the site for investigation.
After returning to the police station, they checked the CCTV footage of 15th September 2023 of the area.
In the footage of 15th September midnight, they found a suspicious man roaming around with a bag.
In the footage, he was even seen running on the footpath next to road. The police was suspicious about him.
Police found that he was in the Pepsico area and launched a search operation.
He was finally found and arrested. While questioning the police found that the man is Deaf.
The accused has been identified as Sindhupalchok resident, Sanjay Bhandari.
Police questioned him about what he was doing in the Pepsico area.
He wrote in English, “I Killed Four People” on a piece of paper.

Look at these codes.
These international numbers are only leaving missed calls. Strange.

This can have 2 explanations:
1. The numbers shown seem to originate from some countries, which may have no strict rules like identity proof check or something for taking a new sim card.
2. It is possible that the scamster is from India, and has identified these countries and is having new numbers on an on-going basis.
These are the two ways in which people are being hoodwinked.
These fraudsters give missed calls. Once the person calls back they are sweet-talked by offering jobs, they send emails, and hack their accounts.
They send viruses, etc to hack.
Isn't WhatsApp strictly monitoring their App?
Why are accounts being hacked. User privacy needs to be mainted.
Karan Saini, Security Technologist at the Centre for Internet Society - which is a non-profit -
actually messaged one of the numbers he got a call from to see what would happen.
He immediately got a response from a Bot asking whether he would like some "part-time" work

Look at the whatsapp conversation.

This is the story of a village in India and I will tell you all about it.
This village is the richest village in India.
Rich means not in terms of money, or luxuries.

It is in Maharashtra. It is Hiware Bazar in Ahmednagar district. This is India's first richest village.
The roads, houses, hospitals,  supply of water, farming, standard of living, etc. are all of the best quality.
Shocking! Like you even I wasn't aware.
About 30 years back, this village was in a terrible condition.
Due to drought the land was barren, there was no proper road, there were no crops and there was hardly any water.
Hiware Bazar was a exteremly impoverished. People were addicted to alcohol, gambling and crime was rampant.
People were extremely destitute.
Hospitals and chemists were far away. People defecated in the open and the village was extremely unsanitary.
They were hardly educated till the 3rd or 4th standard. No one studied till the 10th.
Teachers were not willing to teach. The village registered less than a 30% literacy rate.
Teachers from the cities refused to teach in this village due to the bad reputation.
To make a living, villagers started manufacturing and selling illegal alcohol.
To make ends meet, they resorted to all kinds of illegal work.
Most youngsters would leave Hiware at the age of 15 to work in neighboring cities.
However one person changed the face of the village. Indians were stunned by his work.
Do you know who is this person? Let me tell you.
His name is Popatrao Baguji Pawar. H decided to return to Hiware and improve the status of the village.
He was 26 years old when he completed his postgraduation and decided to return to the village in 1984.
He had decided that he would improve the status of his village.
Pawar won the 1990 panchayat elections and was selected as the sarpanch.
Pawar noticed that there were only two hand pumps in Hiware and that too was broken.
The women of the village had to travel up to 3 km every day to fetch water.
Pawar noticed this and approached the taluka panchayat samiti and got 2 new hand pumps installed.

He began educating them about right ways to earn money, farming, healthy ligestyle, etc.

Pawar realised that lifestyle changes were good but villagers desperately needed to earn their livelihood.
That's why Pawar told them to start farming.
But this seemed impossible because Hiware is a drought-prone area and receives less than 15 inches of rainfall a year.
He thought of a way to conserve water.
He did trench farming, where narrow trenches are dug alongside the slopes of hilly farmlands to capture water when it flows downhill and keep it around crops.
He gave this idea and led the villagers to farming.
A lot of the rainwater was not being saved. This is why in 1992,
a land area was created that channels rainfall to nearby waterbodies.
The villagers used this water for farming and would get a good yeild.
This resulted in a better life for the villagers and they stopped resorting to malpractises.
The village has 294 water wells. Earlier there were none.
It was surprising to see the various water conservation projects.
Now villagers are happy because they have sufficient water for farming and their quality of life has improved.
By 1993, Pawar had expanded the local school up to class 10.
As a result, villagers who left Hiware earlier to become laborers in cities returned for better life opportunities.
Due to Pawar's work in the education sector, the village now has a more than 69% literacy rate.
Many students pursue careers in engineering, medicine, tc.

168 of 182 families were classified as poor but today there are only 3. Everyone is financially strong.

They all well to do and have no money problems. All because Mr Pawar who encourage them to get a better life.

The infrastructure of the village has drastically improved. Villagers are fully satisfied.
Earlier people would defecate in the open and it was very unhygenic.
Now there toilets inside each home. The village is extremely clean now.
All thanks to Pawar for improving the village.

It is regarded as the ‘green model village’ and people uplifted from their poverty stricken lives.

Hu guys! Welcome to this lecture on Salad receipes.
We have already discussed the fundamentals of building a salad in our previous lecture.
I am going to share with you 5 delicious salads.
The 5 salads are split up into 2 lectures. 3 in this one and 2 in the next one.
So, just a little recap, salad is the main meal that you are replacing with your lunch or dinner.
Salad pyramid looks something like this. It shows the propostions of food stuff that should make up the salad.
At the of the salad are raw vegetables.
These could be any. Ranging from spinach, coriander, cabbage, lettuce, arugula, kale,
to like, I don't know - bell peppers, carrots, cucumbers, tomatoes, broccoli, peas.
So you want to use these abundantly.
Next up on the salad are healthy fats such as coconuts or avacado.
Use these moderately. Make sure you use whatever you using is seasonal and regional.
Last on top are dressings or nuts and seeds
These are there just to add some fun and texture to your salad.
Use this sparingly and in very limited amounts.
Why? Because they are harder to digest.
If you can then skip them altogether specially in the curing stage.
The whole point of having a salad is to have something light and give your stomach time to digest the previous meal.
That is the reason we don't add grains like chickpeas or lentils or kidney beans to our salad.
No point of having the salad if your are adding toomuch of the stuff into it. It's not really a salad then!
Focus on the alkaline stuff, the greens, the vegetables, food that is light and detoxifying
Not on the aesthetic stuff. Okay, now lets get started with the salads.
The salad that we are going to start with is the Classic Ayunature Salad.
For this you will need 1 large cucumber, 2 carrots, 4 tomatoes, 1 small green capsicum, 1 cup coriander,
2 big pieces of coconut and 1 Tbsp of black sesame seeds
Dice the cucumber, carrot, tomatoes and capsicum into pieces.
Then add them all to a mixing bowl.
Chop the coriander and toss it with the rest of the ingredients.
Grate your coconut into your salad and sprinkle some sesame seeds from above.
Yes I do know that this one is very very simple salad. Out of all 6 this is probably the cleanest and the healthiest kind of salad
and that is why it is called the Classic Ayunature Salad.
We delibrately don't add any dressing or salt, lemon or nuts to it.
Remember if you are in the curing stage, you should avoid nuts and seeds as much as possible.
And ideally salad should be eaten without combing with lemon and salt.
I am saying this again and again because it is important for you to know.
Yet the coconut and coriander give it a delicious fresh flavour.
Remember you can and in fact you should tweak the ingredients according to your season and region.
The next salad that we are going to be making is the Beet Rocket Salad.
The ingredients that you will need are a handful of spinach leaves, a handful of rocket leaves, 1 small beetroot,
a piece of fresh coconut and 3 - 4 soaked walnuts.
First chop all your spinach, rocket leaves and peeled beetroot.
Next we are going to cook the beetroot. So go ahead and place it in a saucepan with some water and let it cook for 10-15 mins.
or until it's soft.
Once cooked, toss the beetroot along with spinach and rocket leaves in a mixing bowl.
Now it's time for the dressing. The dressing we are making with this salad is called the Middle Eastern Dressing.
To prepare this take a blender and add to it half a cucumber, 1/4 cup coriander, 4 soaked dates,
1/4 tsp cumin and 1/4 Tbsp lemon juice.
Blend until smooth.
Combine this dressing with other ingredients. Grate the coconut from top and add in the crushed walnuts.
Mix it all together and there you have it - Beet Rocket Salad.
I absolutely love this salad. The sweetness from the dates balances the peppery taste of the rocket leaves so well.
The third salad we are going to prepare is the Rainbow Salad.
You will need, 1/2 red cabbage, 1 carrot, 1 yellow bell pepper, 1 beetroot and 1 cup of boiled peas.
Simply chop the carrot, cabbage, bell pepper, beetroot and add them all t o a mixing bowl.
The dressing we are using in this salad is called Almond Chilli Dressing.
You will need 1/4 cup soaked almonds, 2 tsp lemon juice, 1/8 small green chilli, 1 coin ginger,
1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 cup water.
Go ahead and blend all of these ingredients together.
Combine the almond chilli dressing with the other ingredients.
And your Rainbow Salad is ready to be served.
Super easy! Okay, so I hope you liked the first three.

You have an Aadhar card, right? I have one as well, like everyone else.
Aadhar Card is used for many things like banking, obtaining a SIM card, staying at hotels etc. Aadhar card is the most powerful identity proof.
The process to obtain Aadhar card involves biometric verfication as well.
Biometric and other data is recorded by the government.
Many a times people wonder how the money from their bank account is getting deducted?
The banks haven't deducted any money and neither has the person transferred any money. Then how did was the money deducted?
This possible through aadhar card scams. What is it exactly? Is the government's fault? No!
Deceitful hackers are responsible for such scams.
There is Aadhaar-enabled Payment System (AePS) used for various banking-related payments.
While opening a bank account, you scan your biometrics.
These crooks steal your biometrics and use for transactions and it does not require an OTP.
While staying at a hotel, they usually ask for the Aadhar card, scan it, and then sometimes even request fingerprints for verification.
Scammers might stalk the victims and get hold of their fingerprints from office biometric scanners, or atm machines, etc.
They then use this to transfer money from your account and you will be left shocked.
The Aadhar card is used and protected by the government, but it's still hacked by hackers.
However, don't worry.
There is a way to safeguard yourself. To protect yourself from such scams - 'Lock Aadhar biometrics.'
Through the settings, once you lock your biometrics, hackers will not be able to use it for any transaction. You will be safe.
Let me tell you the process.
Go to UIDAI site or mAadhaar mobile app and type your Aadhar card number.
Click on Profile.
Tap on the menu button.
Then Click on Biometric Settings.
Tick on the 'Enable Biometric Lock' option and tap Ok.
Enter the OTP that you receive on the registered moile number and your biometric details will immediately get locked.
No one will be able to hack them and you will be safe.
What a relief!
if you wish to open a bank account or get a new sim card, and require your biometrics, it will not work
as you have locked your biometrics. You will have to unlock the biometetrics in the same way as you locked it.
To unlock the biometrics, click on unlock and submit the OTP. Once unlocked, give your fingerprints at the bank etc
and immediately lock the biometrics again. For your safety, you need to lock and unlock as and when needed.
That's a relief, isn't it?
Today I told you about locking your biometrics on the Aadhar card website.
There are various other safety measures like showing the entire Aadhar card number or mask Aadhar
which means only a few digits of the Aadhar card will be visible. These changes can be done through the settings.
We will share more such features in our upcoming videos. So, keep watching!

This is State Level Association of the Deaf (SLAD) which advocates its support and demands accessibility and other rights for the Deaf community.
The focus on Deaf right in Maharashtra.

What is the protest about?

You can have a look at the previous videos and the protest now is related to it.
Earlier the government had promised to fulfil the demands, however, nothing was ever done.

SLAD have put across 7 demands that are necessary for the Deaf community.
Here are the 7 demands.
1. Various government jobs vacancies available in Maharashtra are advertised in the newspapers.
Under the 3% disability reservation, vacancies for Deaf are advertised, however, these are higher education jobs like graduates, B.E etc.
But the Deaf education system in Maharashtra is very poor and most of the Deaf are only SSC or HSC passed.
There are hardly any highly educated Deaf. A high percentage of Deaf are not very well educated.
The government must change its policy.
Government must change its policy and make job vacancies suitable to the Deaf who are not highly educated as currently there are no colleges for them.
This is the demand.
2. Maharashtra government has already passed a GR in 2007, however, they neither implemented it nor announced it.
Shocking! The person who found the GR is Shaikh Mujahed from Parbhani.
He is Deaf and this is his sign name.
He brought this GR to the notice of the SLAD members who were shcoked reading it.
It was related to the jobs for the Deaf in Maharashtra government.
For example: When applications for a post are received from Deaf candidates, their audiogram too is attached,
which may vary from 40-50% to 100% profound Deaf.
During selection priority must be given in descending order starting from profound Deaf who have 100%, 90%, 80% hearing loss.
Deaf with 70%, 60% 40% deafness should be kept lower in the prioroity list.
Priority should be Deaf with higher hearing loss. This was mentioned in the 2007 GR but was never implemented.
Then why have so many people with mild hearing loss or hard of hearing selected for government jobs?
The demand is to change this.
3. When government of Maharashtra announce job vacancies for the Deaf,
these include Group A job which are higher officer level jobs. Then is Group B which are different,
then is Group C which include clerical posts and then there is Group D which include the peon level jobs.
These are 4 different categories and written exams including GK are held for selection in all the groups.

While there should be examination for selection in Group A and B officer posts,
there should not be a written exam for Group C and D posts. Selection should be based only on an interview.

These can be for emergency services like police, court, fire brigade etc.
SLAD demands accessibility!

This is because till date many have been selected by showing fake disability certificates

Hence all disability certificates should be re-assessed and those found fake, should be punished.
SLAD demands that the vacancies available after dismissing people with fake certificates, should be fillled up with suitable Deaf.
6. This is the next demand.
In Maharashtra there are a lot of residential Deaf schools which have separate accomodation for boys and girls.
There are hostel wardens as well.

SLAD demands that the male wardens of girls hostels to be removed and replaced with female wardens.
They demanded male teachers in girls school be replaced by female teachers as there is a possibility of male teachers exploiting the female students.
7. This is the seventh demand.
Section 66 of the RPWD Act 2016 states that
all government committees should have representation by person with disability including blind, locomotor disability and Deaf.
Till date no one had been selected. Finally, 3 years back Mr Manoj Patwari and Mr Aniket Selgoankar were selected on the advisory board.
However, after the change in the Maharashtra government, new members where selected by the government.
SLAD demands to reinstate both the Deaf leaders in the advisory board.

Today 23rd September is the 3rd day of the International Week of the Deaf.
IWD has been celebrated by the Deaf community for years in the last week of September since 1958.
Today 23rd Septemeber is International Day of Sign languages (IDSL).
IWD is a celebration by the Deaf Community and IDSL is celebrated to create awareness.
The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on 17th December 2017, recognised that
every year 23 September would be celebrated as the International Day of Sign Languages.
On 23rd September Sign Languages such as ASL, BSL, ISL, etc from around the world will be celebrated.
Similarly in India has languages such as Hindi, Marathi in Maharashtra and each state has their own language.
At workplaces, colleges, universities, schools, etc. students are taught in their respective languages,
Similarly colleagues communicate in their own languages.
Hindi day is celebrated on 14th September 2020
and people celebrate it by hosting Hindi elocution, stories, essay, singing and other competitions.
On this awareness is raised about preserving the culture of the Hindi language.
Similarly Marathi Diwas is celebrated on 27th February
Marathi Diwas is celebrated by hosting essay writting, jokes and conversing in Marathi
to preserve the Marathi language. Such celebrations are held across India.
On 23rd September IDSL we celebrate the National Sign Language of India which is Indian Sign Language.
People use sign language to share stories, jokes, there are competitions and many activities.
Hearing individuals are taught to create awareness. These are done across the world.
This year’s theme for IDSL is ‘Sign Languages are for Everyone!”
By everyone it means families, hearing individuals, colleagues, children, childhood friends,
everyone can use and learn Sign Language and remain united.
According to the WFD, there are approximately 70 million Deaf people in the world
and they use more than 200 different Sign Languages.
These Sign Languages are the native languages of the Deaf Community.
On 23rd Septemeber when IDSL is celebrated by teaching hearing individuals, hosting competitions, etc.
it will emphasize the importance of Sign Language to the Deaf Community.
It will automatically lead to the understanding that it is a Deaf person's Human Right.
Indian Sign Language has its own beautiful grammar just like spoken languages like Hindi, English, German, French, etc.
On this day we take pride in our culture and work to preserve Sign Language by creating awareness.
On this day lets celebrate with families, by using Sign Language
teach Sign Language in colleges, schools to your friends and celebrate IDSL.
However, remember when you teach Sign Langugae to hearing individuals,
do not teach them finger spelling.
Finger spelling is not complete Sign Language. They are tools
to aide communication when the sign for certain words are not known.
Through Sign Language have complete conversations like "Hello', "What's your name?", "I stay far away.", etc.
Share stories and jokes in Sign Language, then hearing individuals will understand.
I hope you understand. Enjoy celebrating the day of Sign Languages.

Human Rights, are rights of all individuals. Men, women, Deaf, people with disabilities, Blind,
are all entitled to Human Rights.
Human rights are a set inalienable rights given to all humans around the world.
All human beings have the right to use their human rights without discrimination.
This is very important.
Deaf individuals are naturally Deaf.
Their language of communication is Sign Language.
It is their right.
Human Rights give rights such as Right to Life.
Right to life is where every human has the right to live and should not be killed by any entity.
Right to Live will ensures all human lives are protected by the law.
Right to Equality, is where all individuals for jobs and in all sectors
must not be discriminated on the basis of their gender, religion, skin colour, etc.
All humans must be treated equally for jobs.
The same goes for Right to Education. Every individual has the right to be educated in their native tongue.
Regardless of gender or caste everyone has the human right to be treated equally.
All the human rights are interlinked. If one is not given, people are deprived of the others.

When people are not treated equally as per their Human Rights, they are not able to avail right to education.
If as per our Human Rights, Deaf people are given access to education in Sign Language, they are able to learn
and achieve goals. This ensures they are qualified have the right to secure jobs without being discriminated.
A job ensures they earn well and able to be a part of society.
If one right is not given, they are deprived of all rights.
This leads to the Deaf Community becoming isolated and they do not receive equal status.
Hence, it is important Deaf indiviudals advocate for Sign Language as their Human Right.
Once access to Sign Language is given, the other rights will automatically be achieved.
The wants of the Deaf can be fulfilled when the government recognises Sign Language
and provides interpreters in society.
Deaf individuals will have access to education, news and all forms of content.
Hence, Human Rights are very important.

If our father, grandfather, grandmother or anyone else passes away,
it is natural for us to cry. We feel heavy-hearted for losing the relative.
After a person passes away, his last procession takes place.
But only men participate in the last procession and not the women. Why?
During the last procession, women return back midway and men continue with the procession.
I fail to understand the reason.
Hinduism has its own rule, traditions and culture.
But I want to understand these customs in detail and not just know them as a rule.
We are just told that Hindu women are forbidden from entering the crematoriums.
You all know that in June 2021, actress Mandira Bedi's husband died at a verty young age.
Mandira had carried a clay pot in one hand and held the bier with the other and even lit the pyre.
The news made headlines with some praising her and some criticized her for breaking the customs.
But let me tell you honestly,
None of the Hindu scriptures mention banning women from visiting a crematorium or performing the last rites.
If there is nothing in the scriptures, where did this custom come from?
Hold on! This Hindu custom has a scientific reason.
You would be surprised to know that there is a scientific reason for not allowing women.
Over the years, these customs were transformed and imposed as rules.
But there are scientific reasons behind these customs. Let me tell you two of them.
The first is scientific and psychological reason.
If a woman's father, brother or mother passes away she is emotionally distraught and heartbroken. It is not easy for her.
If the women accompany men to the crematorium, they tend to get highly emotional on seeing the last rites.
Men are known to be less emotional than the women and are able to control their emotions.
Women are known to be more emotional on seeing their loved ones' last rites.
Sometimes the corpse cramps up due to heat and this can be more disturbing to the women.
Sometimes, due to an illness or someother reasons, the corpse jerks up and fall down.
Humans cannot lift the body and put it back as it will be too hot, hence, the corpse needs to be beaten back into the pyre using bamboo sticks.
Watching these disturbing scenes can negatively affect the mental health of the grieving women as they are more emotional.
That is the reason why women do not go to crematoriums.
Therefore, in earlier times, the elders of the household asked women to stay behind.
Women only helped changing the clothes on the dead body and preparing for the last rites.
Only emotionally stronger men were preferred to go to the crematorium and not the women.
This is the psychological reason.
Here's what the second scientific reason says.
Hindus have common crematoriums. While we use one pyre for our relative, other pyres are used by others.
There is a high probability that someone being cremated alongside, may have died due to an infectious disease.
Therefore, there is always a chance of the virus and bacteria getting transferred to other people.
That is why to remove the virus, after the cremation, we wash our hands and feet before entering the house and then bathe.
People misunderstand that not bathing after peforming the last rites bring back the soul.
After the last rites, some people even use salt to ward off the spirit of the deceased.
I always failed to understand why do I need to ward off the soul of my loved ones by bathing or using salt.
This was not the reason!
Scientifically, viruses from the crematorium could get transferred to other people and harm them.
That is why we need to bathe and not to ward off the soul. But to keep ourself clean.
These viruses can live in the hair for up to 2 weeks and that is another reason why women don't go to crematorium.
Men of the family, shave off their head after performing the last rites while the women do not and they have long hair.
Women are more closer to the children and if they go for the last rites, the virus in their hair may also affect the children.
That was the reason why the elders forbidded women from going to the crematoriums.
Over a period of time, they simply converted these into rules and the scientific reasons were never told.
I hope you all have understood the reason now.
You all understood the 2 scientific reasons.
Times have changed now and people have become broad-minded.
If a couple have only daughter or daughters and no son? What will they do?

Before we move on, we'd like to quickly remind you of the 4 principles of Satvic food, which we follow in all our recipes
And that is LWPW
L means living, which means we only use ingredients that are living, full of life
Nothing that comes from a packet, bottle, tin or box
W means wholesome, which means we only use ingredients in the form Mother Nature gave them to us
So we use brown rice instead of white rice. Instead of sugar, we use dates or jaggery. Instead of oil, use coconut kernel
And instead of refined flour, we use whole wheat flour
Next is P for plant-based,
which means all our ingredients come from plants, not from animals
Meat, fish and eggs are out of the question
And we use coconut or almond milk instead of milk
And finally W for water-rich, which means we use ingredients that are as water-rich as possible
which are full of water
because any food that is water-rich can be digested very easily
Even in the Bhagvad Gita, the first identification of Satvic food given by Lord Krishna is that they should be juicy

As you all know winter season is for 4 months and is my favorite season!
We wear stylish hats, gloves, jackets, etc.
During the winters, we enjoy sleeping in thick cozy blankets.
We hate to get out of bed and want to keep sleeping.
We all want to keep sleeping and waking up becomes very difficult. You all know this.
But there is one thing I don't like about winters.
And that is severe acid reflux and heartburn.
Why does this happen?
I will explain improtant points to prevent acid reflux.
Over eating adds extra pressure on your digestive system which then leads to acidity.
And then you feel the acid reflux,
causing that uncomfortable burning sensation in our chest, sour taste in our mouth, coughing, etc.
Everyone finds it difficult.
Also, consistent acid reflux can result in a serious condition called GERD,
which causes the esophagus to become inflamed and can even create holes.
It is very dangerous.
Many of you are unaware about how to prevent this.
Mistakes during winters cause these problems. So remember and avoid them.
Every winter, remember to watch this video and share it with your friends to learn.
Here are the points.
In winter, we often enjoy spending time tucked into bed for hours.
We don't go out but sit for hours. Also on during weekends,
we are on our phone, watch TV, and keep eating. We do not do any type of activity.
This can weaken the stomach's digestion power leading to acid reflux.
2. Outdoor Activites
On winter days, we don't go out as we feel cold and tired to walk with all the heavy winter clothes.
However, the food we eat may be difficult for the stomach to digest.
Physical activities helps to balance our system, aiding in the digestion and absorbtion of food and maintain a balance.
Being lazy and only eating during the winter cause the digestion problem.
Digestion becomes weak leading to acid reflux.
Also some people exercise immediately after eating, which is not safe for digestion and leads to more acidity.
Wait for 45 minutes to 1 hour after eating and then exercise, so that the stomach can digest properly.
As you all know, sun is an important source of vitamin D for our body.
But during winter, the sun exposure is low.
The whole day, there is fog, and we can only catch glimpses of the sun for a few minutes. You all know that.
Then how to get sun exposure?
As soon as you see the sun, try to get some sunlight yourself.
Is it beneficial if the sunlight is less and it id foggy?
Yes, it is.
Without exposure to the sun, your body will lack Vitamin D.
As you eat, the food passes through the esophagus and into the stomach.
The stomach will absorb the food, digest and pushes it to the intestine.
The muscle between the esophagus and stomach, called the sphincter muscle, becomes weak,
causing food to flow back and leading to acid reflux. This is due to weak sphincter muscles caused by vitamin D deficiency.
Hey, instead of sunlight, can we take vitamin D pills?
You should not do it yourself.
Before taking any medicines you should consult your doctor and remember to follow the prescription.
4. Food cravings
During winter, everyone craves to eat cheesy, creamy and fatty junk food.
But digestion of these food is slow and it takes a longer time.
This creates gastric pressure on sphincter muscle and it forces the stomach acid go up into the esophagus causing heartburn.
Try to limit the consumption of fatty foods.
5. Indulging more into alcohol during winter
During winter, consumption of whiskey, rum, wine and other alcoholic drink increases.
But let me inform you that all alcoholic drinks contain acid.
And remember, consuming more and more alcohol will create more acid
making the sphincter muscle to become weak which in turn forces the stomach acid to flow back to the esophagus and cause heartburn.
So, try to limit alcohol intake.
6. Tight clothing
Wearing tight shirts, tight jeans, tight belts, tight jackets,
can put pressure on your abdomen, pushing stomach acid into the esophagus.
Hence, to avoid acid refulx, you must wear loose clothes.
Hope you have understood and would remember the points to avoid during winter that can cause acid reflux.

2. Chewing on a pinch of Ajwain.
3. Consuming rock salt and gulping it down with a glass of warm water may also be beneficial.

Chief Justice Chandrachud agreed readily.

The satellite will match the GPS coordinates of the vehicle from the number plate.

The Deaf and the hearing community dream and wish to add Indian Sign Language as the 23rd official language in India.

to recognize Indian sign language as the 23rd official language of India.

Varughese Mathews, the principal of Kozhikode’s St Xavier’s College of Arts & Science said that
India has 22 official languages and ISL should be added as the 23rd language
as lakhs of Deaf in India use ISL for for fluent and smooth communication. Hence it should be added as an official language.

Once ISL becomes an official language, hearing police officers, government officials, etc will have to learn sign language and communication will be better.
Mathews said that in north India, Hindi is spoken more while in southern India, state wise Telugu, Malayalam etc is spoken.
If a person from north India visits south India, they will face communication barrier.
However, ISL is same all over the country and the Deaf from any part of India easily communicate with each other.
That is why he wants ISL to be made an official language.
Mathews had earlier filed a petition to include ISL as 23rd  official language of India.
Oh! Mathews supports the Deaf community.
State Disability Commissioner, Panchapakesan's memorandum was based on the earlier petition submitted by Mathews.

PAN stands for Permanent Account Number.
PAN is issued in a laminated plastic card by the Income Tax Department.
PAN enables the Income Tax department to identify salary payments,
you need a PAN as proof for loans,
investments in shares, Mutual funds,
it helps the IT department keep track of this.
Your PAN also needs to be linked inorder to avail TDS refunds and other services.
Here are other reasons why PAN number is required:
and even proffesionals like lawyers, doctors, engineers, etc need PAN cards.
Every person if his total income during the year exceeds a certain amount needs to pay tax and requires a PAN card for that.
2.Every company, shop, organisationm, etc who's annual turnover exceeds a certain amount requires a PAN card.
Every person who intends to enter into specified financial transactions require PAN card.
Any financial transaction would require PAN card.
Sale or purchase of a motor vehicle also requires a PAN card.
Opening an account with a bank including a demat account for shares and for issue of a credit or debit card, requires a PAN card.
3. Payment in cash of an amount exceeding Rs. 50,000 to buy a mobile, or for any purchase requires you to show your PAN as proof.
You require to mention the PAN card number while depositing Rs 25,000 or Rs 50,000 cash in the bank.
Only then you can deposit the cash.
Your PAN number is needed for this.
PAN number is not a random set of numbers.
Here is how PAN numbers are generated.
Every PAN contains 10 digits.
The first 5 characters are always alphabets,
followed by 4 numeric digits and ending again with an alphabet.
Out of the first five characters, the first three characters
represent the alphabetic series running from AAA to ZZZ.
It goes in a series according to the applications.
Now what does the fourth character of PAN represents. Let me explain.
"P" stands for Individual
"G" stands for Government Agency
"C" stands for Company
"T" stands for Trust
Have a look at this list. This is the fourth character.
Fifth character of PAN represents
the first character of the PAN holder's last name or surname in case of an individual. My last name is Shah so the character would be S.
So these were the 5 characters.
Next four characters are sequential numbers running from 0001 to 9999
Last character i.e. the 10 character is an alphabetic check digit which is based on a formula which takes into account the first nine digits.
Every PAN contains 10 digits in a fixed combination.

On 1st Febrauray 2024, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced the Union interim budget 2024-25.
Why an interim budget?
We have general elections scheduled between April to May 2024,
therefore the government has announced an interim budget until the new elected government presents its annual budget.
Now let me tell you some key points of the interim budget announced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.
1. Through the Pradhan Mantri Suryodaya Yojana, in 1 crore households in India,
solar panels on the rooftops will be installed. 1 crore households will be made solar powered.
Under this scheme, 300 Units Of free electricity will be provided to these 1 crore households every month.
The households are expected to save ₹15,000 to ₹18,000 on electricity bill per year.
2. FM announced a new Rural Housing Scheme that will allow those living in rented houses, slums, chawls, etc.
to buy or build their own house in the next 5 years.
Government will also build 2 crore new houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) to meet the high demand of the growing population.
3. More medical colleges will be set up using the existing infrastructure.
4. Finance Minister Sitharaman announced that Healthcare cover under Ayushman Bharat scheme
earlier was not given to Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) helpers.
However now the Ayushman Bharat healthcare scheme has been extended to all ASHA workers as well.
5. The Lakhpati Didi scheme is focused on women.
The target of the Lakhpati Didi scheme has been increased from 2 crore women to 3 crore women.
The aim of this scheme is to encourage women to establish micro-enterprises and earn a minimum annual income of ₹1 lakh.
The scheme trains women in LED bulb making, drone operation, tailoring, weaving, etc.
The women can then set up a micro-enterprises conprising of 11 - 12 people.
6. Last year ₹5.94 lakh crores were allocated to defense.
This year funds allocated to defense have been increased by 4.5% to ₹6.21 lakh crores.
7. Policies and schemes focusing education, skill development, support for startups,
and sports achievements have been promised.
8. Finance Minsiter announced that a corpus of ₹1 lakh crore has been kept,
that would be available on loan at minimal or nil interest rates for 50 years.
This is to encourage research & development in ‘sunrise domains' which are new but fast growing and expected to become important in the future.
There will be nil interest on this loan and ₹1 lakh crore corpus has been kept.
9. 40,000 railway coaches are promised to be converted to Vande Bharat standard.
Metro Rail to be expanded to other cities as well.
10. The new ‘UDAN’ scheme has been introduced.
There are Tier-1, Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
Tier 1 are metro cities such as Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru etc which have good air connectivity.
Tier - 2 cities are cities which have 50,000 to 100,000 population.
and Tier - 3 cities are the ones that have 20,000 to 50,000 population.
Under the UDAN scheme 517 new routes will be introduced to connect tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
Upgradation and expansion of the existing airports will also be taken up.
11. Green energy reduces air pollution and protects the environment.
Green energy such as biogas, CNG, electric cars will be a major investment in the future.
12. The Central Government has funds
for states to developed infrastructure, branding, marketing to increase tourism etc.
Central government will provide long-term interest-free loans to states for their infrascructure development, tourism etc.
The aim is to encourage all the states to develop.
13. Government has plans to increase farmers' income
and will promote private investment as one of the post-harvest activities.
14. Has the Income Tax slab rates, GST rates, other taxes & import duty changed?
Finance Minister announced that there has been no change in these.
15. Capital expenditure has been increased by 11.1% to ₹11.11 lakh crore
for infrastructural development and increase port connectivity on all Indian islands including Lakshadweep,
Andaman and Nicobar, etc. This plan has been announced to boost tourism on all the islands.
16. Developmental assistance aid fund for Maldives last year was ₹770.90 crore.
This year it has been reduced to ₹600 crore.
The budget of 2024-25 is an interim budget.
Now we have to wait for the final budget until the new government is formed.

India got independence in 1947 and will complete 100 years in 2047.

While most of you would know about the Public Provident Fund (PPF) scheme, some of you might not know.
Let me tell you about the scheme. It is an important investment with good returns.
Nowadays a days youngsters spend off the money that they earn, which is acceptable,
but at the same time you should save a little. When you get a good return on it in the future,
you will not regret. You will not have to depend on loans.
PPF is one of the best schemes.
PPF is a long term savings scheme. It is not where you can withdraw money in a few months or couple of years.
When at the end of the long period you get a good retrun, you can then invest this money in different investment schemes like FD etc.
The PPF scheme was launched in 1968 by the Finance Ministry
with the main objective to help individuals make small savings and provide good returns on the savings.
I will now give you the details of deposit, interest and other rules.
The first question is, who can open a PPF account? Let me tell you.
1. An person who has an Indian citizenship can open a PPF account.
Nationals of other countries can like UK, Australia etc can't apply.
The Indian citizen also has to be above 18 years of age.
2. A guardian or parents on behalf of a minor can open a PPF account.
However, the account will be in the name of the minor under guardianship of the adult.
3. Only one account can be opened by one person all across the country
The next question is where can you open a PPF account?
You can open a PPF account in any bank or post office.
The third question is about the deposit at the time of opening an account.
he PPF account opening charges are just Rs. 100.
The minimum amount that you can deposit is Rs 500 and maximum is Rs 1.5 lakh.
You can deposit any amount for a maximum of 12 times during a given financial year.
I very well know that from the salary you receive, you will be able to deposit at least Rs 500 every month.
Instead of spending the entire amount, deposit at least Rs 500, it would be good if you can deposit Rs 1000 or above
So, in a year you will be able to save every month.
The next question is, in what are the ways in which you can deposit in the PPF account?
There are multiple ways like cash, cheque, cash, and online transfers.
These days due to the advanced technology, you need not go to the bank, online transfer is a more convenient option.
The next question - How long do I have to deposit money in the PPF account?
The answer is - The lock-in period for PPF is 15 years. You will get the return after 15 years.
The tenure can be extended by 5 years at the end of the period.
The sixth question is, Can you withdraw before maturity?
Yes, you can withdraw. Partial withdrawals ie. 50% is permitted from the 7th year onwards.
Withdrawals can be made only once in a financial year.
Can you get a loan on a PPF account?
The answer is Yes!
However, you can take loan on the PPF account between the 3rd and 6th year.
The loan amount will depend on the total deposits that you have made.
If you want a second loan, it can be taken after the first loan is refunded.
My next question is will tax be deducted?
If your income falls into the taxable slab, every year tax is deducted.
But, the money invested in PPF in a financial year gets exempted from an individual’s taxable income under Section 80C.
Also, the interest earned on PPF deposits along with the accumulated amount is tax free. Wonderful! How beneficial!
The next question is, What is the interest rate?
Interest is paid on 31st March every year. Current interest is 7.1%
Though the interest percentage is not fixed, government usually announces it in the same range. However, every year the interest is paid on 31st March.
Isn't it wonderful? Now that I have informed you the benefits, trying saving a little in PPF from the salary you receive.
At the end of 15 years, along with the interest you would have accumalated a good amount
which can be used for your children's education or marriage or for buying a house
or you can even put it in Fixed deposit etc. So, start saving from your younger days. Minimum amount is just Rs 500.
Since long you would have been spending money, so now try saving it. PPF is really beneficial. Don't waste time now and start depositing.

Did you know that you can create your own 100% plant-based butters
without using any oil or milk in your own kitchen?
Sounds nuts right?
In this video, we'll show you how to prepare 3 homemade nut butters
that you can easily prepare within 15 mins
First we're going to learn how to prepare delicious peanut butter, then almond butter,
and finally, coconut butter
In the first part of this video, we'll show you a step-by-step guide to prepare all these butters
And in the second part, we'll show you how you can use these butters
and the delicious dishes you can prepare using them
including smoothie bowls, laddoos, and brownies

You can use them as toppings for smoothies
or dip your cut dates with them to create a tasty dessert
There are endless ways to enjoy this butter
First let's learn how to prepare peanut butter
Pour 1 cup (100 gm) peanuts into a cooking pot and spread them out like this
Now roast them on a low flame for at least 4-5 mins
By roasting them, the natural oils of the peanuts will be released easily
After roasting them, transfer the peanuts into a bowl and allow them to cool for a while
When they have cooled down, you can transfer them to your blender or food processor
and blend them for 5-6 mins
Ensure that you only blend for 15-20 seconds at a time. Otherwise, your blender will overheat
In this video, we're using a high-speed blender
But you can use any blender that you have at home
Just take a break for a few seconds. If the mixture is sticking to the side of the walls,
you can scrape it down properly with a spatula or a spoon and blend it again
First, your peanuts will turn into a powder. And you'll wonder - "how will this turn into butter?"
Just be patient. As you continue to blend the mixture, the powder will release its oil
And slowly, this powder will turn into creamy butter
Remember one thing - never add water to it.
If you add any liquid to it, you won't be able to make butter properly
and will spoil easily
There we go. Our delicious creamy peanut butter is ready!
If you want to make your peanut butter more flavourful, you can add a pinch of rock salt
or some jaggery while blending as per your taste
Then you can pour the butter into a jar and store it in your fridge
How long can you store it for?
We recommend that the fresher you consume it, the better it is for you
Don't store it for more than 5-6 days
Did you ever imagine that making nut butters could be so simple?
On that note, let's move onto our next nut butter - and that is almond butter
To prepare almond butter, take 1 cup (100 gm) almonds
and pour them into a large cooking pot spreading them out like this
Now roast them on a low flame for at least 5 mins
After roasting them, allow the almonds to cool down for a while
Now you have to follow the same process as before
Just pour your roasted almonds into the blender and turn it on
First, your almonds will turn into powder. And slowly, the powder will turn into butter
If the mixture is sticking to the side of the walls, switch off the blender first
Now take a spatula or spoon to scrape the mixture properly and blend it again
Remember, never allow your blender to overheat. If it is overheating, allow it to cool
There you go! Our second delicious, dairy-free, creamy almond nut butter is ready
Come, let's move onto our final nut butter - and that is coconut butter
To prepare coconut butter, you need 1 dry coconut butter (gola)
You can't prepare it with the hairy coconut
First, scrape off the external brown layers and cut it into small pieces like this
To prepare coconut butter, we don't need to roast the coconut at all
Transfer these pieces into a high-speed blender
Now we'll blend them for at least 5-7 mins until it turns into a soft and buttery mixture
Remember - don't leave your blender running continuously for a long time
First, it'll turn into powder and then butter. Looks like your creamy butter is ready too
Transfer the butter into a jar as well and don't store it for more than 5-7 days
That wraps up all 3 of our nut butters - peanut, almond, and coconut

Look at this. This the UDID card.
I am sure you all know about it, would have applied for it and would have even got the card.
It is an identity card for persons included in all the 21 categories of Disabilities all over India.
The UDID Project was launched in 2016
by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities which is under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Govt. of India.
The project was implemented for creating a National Database which can help getting a statistical data on the 21 categories of persons with disabilities.
The UDID card acts as an identification and verification proof for persons with disabilities.
Earlier PwDs had to carry multiple documents for proof like Railway Concession, Disability certificate etc.
The UDID captures all the necessary detail in a single card. It is also linked to the Aadhar card
as while registering, you put in your Aadhar card details.
A single card can be used as it has all the details.
The UDID card has your name, your year of birth, type of disability and whether the disability is Permanent.
It also mentions the percentage of Disability.
For example: People having less than 40% disability would have a white stripe on the left side of the UDID card.
Those having 40% to 80% disability would have a yellow stripe on the left side of the UDID card.
Those having above 80% disability have a blue stripe on the disability card.
It would be easy to identify the extent of a person’s disability.
A unique UDID number starts with the state identification charachters like MH or TS or KL etc.
The next digits are the district codes which fall within the particular state.
Next digits are the disability code.
In all it is a 18 digit unique number including the State code.
This number give you all the information about the person and is very useful & benficial.
The UDID card lets persons with disabilities to avail of a number of benefits depending upon their disability type and extent.
Have a look here at the benefits.
1. Government provides scholarship schemes for students with disabilities which can be availed using the UDID card.
2. To avail reduction in income tax for persons with disabilities.
3. Concession on Railway fare. You may be surprised as you may be having a separate Railway Concession Certificate.
This is due to the lack of communication between the MSJE and Railway Ministry.
UDID can be used to avail railway concession as well but Railway insists on having a separate certificate which mentions the percentage of disability.
Hope both the ministry are able to come to a consensus and follow only a single card.
4. UDID can be used to avail loan facilities from the government for starting a new business.
5. To avail assistive devices like hearing aids, prosthetics, wheelchairs etc at subsidized rates, UDID card can be submitted.
6. Unemployment allowance for educated persons with disability can be availed using UDID card.
7. It can also be used while applying for government jobs under the Pwd category.
8. UDID card can be used to avail Group insurance which is applicable for government employees with disabilities.
9. To avail free travel facility in state transport, UDID is to be sumitted as proof.
It is very useful.
The DEPwD announced that from 1st April 2023, UDID is mandatory to avail benefits of government schemes for persons with disabilities.
So, everyone apply for the UDID card!
The government said those who do not have a UDID card would not be able to avail the schemes.
However, if the person has already applied for the UDID card, then they will have to provide the UDID enrollment number
along with the disability certificate.
However, in case of availability of a valid UDID number, physical copy of disability certificate is not required.
Only of the UDID number is not available, the disability certifiate is too be submitted.
The DEPwD said the aim of making UDID mandatory bring transparency in the process.
and to reduce fake certification which were easy to get bybribing etc.
In the future, government would treat UDID card as a single proof for Persons with Disabilities.
Now communication technology is getting advance. We use text messages, touchscreen smart phones, email etc.
For all these communication we use the Keyboard. Keyboard is also install on mobiles as well which help us work faster.

people used typewriters.
Then came computers, and now we have touchscreen devices. Right?
Let us go back to the time when even the typewrites did not exist. More than 200 years back people wrote with ink and feather pens.
Invitations, letters, and everything else were written manually which was time consuming and tiring.
Then people thought of ways to send message and inventedtypewriters and then later mobiles.
All this would not have been possible without one of the greatest inventions in history.
But this one idea solved the problem for generations to come.
This was invention of the QWERTY Keyboard. It is found on the uppermost alphabet row of the keyboard.
The top most row of the keyboard has function keys such as F1 F2 etc.
Below that row, is the number row which has number from 1 to 0 and the
Next 3 rows are the alphabets rows which have punctuation marks at the sides
It would be difficult to type if the alphabets in the 3 rows are arranged alphabetically.
People thought of different methods
and came up with the idea of QWERTY method which made typing easy. The method become successful and is still being used.
Let me tell you it's history.
From writing manually, people changed their method in 1829 when a very famous American scientist William Austin Burt invented new method.
He invented a very unique machine called Typographer had a watch like circle and a lever that had to be rotated.
Years ago, it did not have keys like typewriter but had levers for alphabets that were arranged alphabetically and had to be pressed.
Later the invention underwent a lot of modifications and then we had the typewriter.
But the problem remaind the same and the levers got stuck because of the arrangement of keys.
Over the next 4 decades, many other advanced & successful typewriters created by these famous American inventors.
The inventors were forced to rethink the alphabet arrangement of the keys. But the problem persisted.
That’s when American inventor Christopher Latham Sholes stepped in as the problem solver.
Sholes concluded that the best alphabetical layout with the least key-jamming was the QWERTY keyboard.
Sholes experimented with multiple alphabetical layouts and placed the vowels and in different row. This method was successful.
He got this success in the year 1873.
Later, Sholes sold the QWERTY layout to the American Remington Corporation.
By 1877 the company started selling typewriters with QWERTY layout and they were successful.
Since then, very minor changes have been made like the numbers 0 and 1 were added.
The letter ‘M’ was shifted from the end of the middle row to the end of the last row.
and the position of the letters ‘X’ & ‘C’ was swapped.
These minor changes fixed all the problems that caused the levers of the typewriter to get jammed and typing became easier.
The QWERTY keyboard is the keyboard that we use today.
We have chaged from writing with feather pens, to the huge Typographer whose levers got jammed, to the current keyboard.
Without Sholes idea which solved the lever jamming problem, we would not have had the computer, mobile etc keyboards.
It is all thanks to the QWERTY arrangement of the keyboard.
Sholes idea 200 back changed the entire future scenerio.
How smart and god gifted these invventors are! All thanks to Sholes!

People get very excited when they see someone expressing themselves romantically.
Such expressions are made through the eyes, and many other ways.
Do only humans the only one who express their emotions?
You must have never heard of animals expressing their affection, right?
No! Even animals express their affection in different ways.
There are so many animals that are able to show their affection in different ways.
You will be stunned to know that they are very different to humans.
They are very cute creatures.
They are very different from human beings.
A Swan falls in love and finds a partner. They are always together.
99% of swans are faithful to their partners. No matter what happens they do not separate.
99% always remain faithful to their partners.
They swim with their long necks entwined with each other. This is their way of showing affection.
They have a strong bond.
If one partner dies the other can even die due to heartbreak.
Whoa! The other dies soon after the partner passes away. Swans share a strong bond with their partner.
See this? They are called Sea Otters and are they are very interesting creatures.
Sea Otters are known to be very social animals just like humans.
They prefer staying together in the water and are very happy.
They have a strong bond with their partners and always remain together.
Here is something unique about them.
They sleep floating in the water on their backs.
It risks them drifting away and someone else taking their partner.
Therefore, Sea Otters hold hands while sleeping to avoid losing members of their group.
They hold hands so that everyone stays together. Isn't that interesting!
Humans don't do this but sea otters are such cute animals.
Isn't that a cute piece of information.
Now this is very exciting!
When penguins fall in love, they have a unique way of proposing to their partner,
Generally men kneel down and propose with a ring.
Some propose with a cake, chocolate, etc. and surprise their partners.
Penguins do something similar. They express their emotions in a very unique way.
When a male penguin falls in love with a female penguin, to express his love
the penguin will go on a search to find the smoothest pebble of the beach
And, when he finds one he carries it in his beak
and offers it to his potential partner by placing it at her feet. He then awaits the female's response.
If the female penguin likes the pebble, she will accept the male’s proposal by adding the pebble to her nest.
The two will then continue to build the nest together and grow their family.
Seahorses. They have a deep bond with their partners.
Humans show by being close, hugging, dancing, etc. but they do this for a limited time.
However Seahorses are very different. They continuously display affection. Here is how.
Seahorses share a strong bond with their partners.
The Seahorse couple is often seen swimming in pairs for hours with their tails linked together.
They are monogamous and mate for life.
They engage in a couple dance which includes spinning around. They enjoy being together and immensely love their partners.
While dancing they also change colors. Isn't that amazing!
You know there are reality dance shows, where couples perform and compete.
Wouldn't it be funny if there were dance reality shows for Seahorses too?
Cats are dearly loved. Humans and cats share a close bond with one another.
But how do you identify a cat's affection for you.
Humans voice out their feelings which is how we know. But what does a cat do?
They have a unique way.
Cat give out a high-pitch repetitive sound.
This means they love you.
This is a sign of a cat's affection.
Whenever a cat emits such a sound it means they love you.
Cats blink slowly with half closed eyes.
The slow blinking of a cat is known as the ‘cat kiss.’ This is their cute way of showing affection.
Red Foxes. Here is something interesting about them.
Like the swans, foxes too are monogamous but there is one thing that is different about them.
Red Foxes too are monogamous but only the male.
If the female fox dies, the male fox refuses to take another partner and remains single for life.
The male never takes a partner and always remembers the female.
However, if the male fox dies,
then the female fox will look for a new partner almost immediately.
The male and female are very different from each other. Isn't that interesting.
Here were the different animals and the ways in which they display their affection. How surprising!
It's not only humans who show affection. Even animals do!

if you see that the details are not matching with those on the app,
the driver may tell you that the car mentioned in the app has gone for repair and the other car also belongs to him.
While that may be true,
it is safer to not ride in that cab and book another one.
2. Child Lock
It is located in the door frame panel of both the rear doors of most of the cars.
The control of the lock is with the driver.
Child lock is to ensure the saftey children and prevent them from opening the car door.
The control of the lock is with the driver of the car. We all know that.
But when you are travelling in a cab, you have to ensure the child lock is deactivated.
When activated, the rear doors can only be opened from the outside and a stranger may enter and try to kidnap you.
Therefore, when you sit in the back seat of the cab, ensure that the child lock is off.
3. Map and Route
The moment the driver submits the Pin,
the cab shows a route. Follow the same route.
Some cab drivers take you from a different route, stating that it is shorter and less congested or charge will be less.
But never accept it and tell the driver to follow the given route.
It might not be safe to travel on unfamiliar routes as there might be isolated and empty.
Instead request the driver to follow to the route shown on the app.
4. Check the driver's profile
Before starting your trip, always check if the driver’s name and photo matches with the driver of your cab or not.
If you have doubts that the driver information on the app is not matching with the driver who arrived,
as a passenger you have a right to check the driver’s license to ensure your saftey.
In some cases the driver may tell you that the picture used in the app is an old one or a wrong picture has been uploaded by the cab company.
Therefore, if you have any doubts or feel even slightly suspicious of the driver, don’t get into the cab.
5. Safety App
Always have the ‘112 India’ app installed in your phones.
It sends emergency alerts to different concerned authorities.
These authorities include police, fire department, medical services like ambulances, etc.
So, you must have this App on the phone so that  you can be contacted in case of an issue.
But there is a problem.
As per ISH Team's discussion, the 112 India app is useful.
A lot of Deaf uses app like Ola, Uber etc to book cabs.
If Deaf are stuck in an emergency and contact 112 India, it will be hard for them to communicate.
Now that I have explained the points, I hope the Deaf Associations, with the voiceover and subtitles in this video,
will contact the local 112 India helpline authorities and inform them that the app is not accessible to the Deaf.
Ask them for a solution as the safety of the Deaf using the fleet cabs, too should be ensured.
So, Deaf associations, remember to contact the local authorities.
Now that you know the 5 tips to ensure safe cab rides,
you have to ensure your saftey by wearing seat belt.
Don't be engrossed playing games on your phone or surfing Instagram. Ensure that the driver is driving on the given route.
Keep your mobile fully charged in case of any emergency.
When you book a cab, share the details with your family, friends, office colleague, etc for your saftey.
These cabs are beneficial but also sometimes risky. So, remember the 5 points for your saftey.

Everyone knows that 31st December is here and the year will end. We will be into the new year.
All bring in the New Year with a lot of festivities.
But there is also a cultural aspect involved. Let me explain.
For example, Diwali in India spans five days a special occassion each day which holds a significant cultural aspect.
Similarly, as the New Year approaches, various cultural traditions are observed to welcome the New Year.
We may not see anything unique in India but many countries follow their own new year tradition, making it unique from one another.
Let me tell you about these interesting traditions.
1. Brazil: The people of Brazil on 31st December midnight, just before the start of the New Year,
wear white clothes and enter the sea.
Brazilians believe in the tradition of making seven wishes.
For every wish they make, they jump at the time of the wave.
The same way, they make 7 wishes while jumping 7 waves. It is their cultural belief.
The tradition is to honour Yemanja, their goddess of water, and requesting her to fulfill their seven wishes.
2. Spain - In a unique ritual, at midnight of 31st December, Spanish families come together and
eat 12 grapes, one for each month, to bring good luck and ward off evil for every month of the year.
3. Japan - According to Japanese tradition, on 31st December midnight,
people visit the Buddhist temples and ring their bells 108 times
to dispel the 108 evil desires in everyone and to cleanse the sins of the past year.
Once the bell is rung 108 times, all the sins of the past are cleansed and they start fresh in the new year.
This tradition is known as Joyanokane.
In another traditional, the Japanese eat Soba noodles at midnight.
4. Finland - The Finnish traditionally believe that the events of the midnight of 31st December, determine if their new year would be good or not.
But how?
For example, a soft drink can is made of a metal called tin.
Finnish cast molten tin into a container of water and then interpret the shape it forms after hardening.
A heart or ring means a wedding coming up, a ship predicts travel,
a pig-shaped object means there will be plenty of food which means having a prosperous life!
There are interpretations of many other shapes. Finnish believe in this tradition and do it on the midnight of new year eve.
Interesting!
5. Denmark - The new year tradition involves throwing old plates & glasses against the main doors of the houses of friends and families
This is done to banish bad spirits and wish for good luck for them.
People of Denmark also stand on chairs and jump together at midnight to ‘leap’ into new year with good luck.
6. Philippines - The families in the Philippines serve 12 ‘round fruits’
as they believe that the coin like shape of the fruits increases prosperity.
The 12 fruits, with each fruit representing one month of the new year, are eaten on 31st December midnight.
7. Greece - People hang bundles of onions on their front doors after the first church prayer of the new year’sday
as a symbol of banishing the evil and a rebirth in the new year.
8. Colombia, South America - Colombians place three potatoes under the bed of each family member.
One potato is peeled, one unpeeled, and the third one partially peeled.
At midnight, each person tries to grab one of the potatoes with closed eyes,
It's believed that depending on the potato they grab, they can expect a year of either good fortune,financial struggle, or a mix of both.
What a unique way to know what the future holds.
9. Italy - It is customary for men and women in Italy to wear red underwear on 31st December.
The red color is associated with fertility and good luck. So, people wear red underwear with the hopes of being able to conceive in the new year.
10. Russia - The Russians follow the tradition of writing their wishes for the new year on paper.
They then burn the paper with a candle. Once burnt, they collect the ash and keep it aside.
At midnight, they add the ashes to the glass of champagne and drink it. They believe their wishes will come true.
11. Estonia, Europe - On New Year's Day, Estoniansbelieve in a unique tradition.
Usually most of us have 4 meals in a day.
But on new year, they eat 7, 9, or 12 meals throughout the day.
These numbers are considered lucky in their culture and believe more they eat the more plentiful food will come in the new year.
What a unique tradition of eating more for prosperity! Wonderful!
12. Chile, South America - They have their own cultural belief. Usually the New Year's mass is held in the church.
In Chile, new year’s masses are held in cemeteries rather than at churches.
People decorate tombs and sit around the graves of their deceased friends & families to include them in the new year festivities and prayers.
They believe that the deceased being a part of the celebration brings good luck.
The 12 unique traditions were different from each other and were interesting, isn't it?
If you follow such unique culture in your country or in India, let us know in the comments.
