We all have food in the morning, afternoon and night in our daily lives.
What do we do with the leftovers? Do we throw them away?
No. We store them in containers inside the refrigerator to eat the next day.
This way there is no wastage. You all know this.
When buy lots of vegetables from the market, we put it all in the refrigerator to keep it fresh for a long time.
If that's what you think right then no. Some items can be stored in the fridge but some can not.
Since people are not aware they put everything in the fridge and then the taste, colour, all changes.
Some food items like butter must be kept in the fridge & some must not be stored.
There are so many different items. How confusing.
Wait! Now you will be surprised to learn items that can be stored outside and remain fresh.
Here are the points.
We all love to eat bread with butter and it tastes delicious.
But remember, once you buy bread from the market and open the packet,
if you store the leftover in the fridge, it becomes tasteless.
How? You might say that keeping it out will also make it tasteless.
If you keep the leftover bread outside for many days at a stretch,
mold forms on the bread & it starts to smell. You throw it away and its wasted.
This is why you refrigerate it but no. It will spoil the taste. Thefridge might prevent molding but it makes the bread dry & bland.
Here's a suggestion. See how much bread your family needs - maybe its half a packet - and finish it the same day.
It will taste fresh. Buy for a few days is enough.
Remember, do not keep it outside for many days.
Buy how much you need and finish it off so it tastes fresh.
Herbs like basil, thyme & others lose flavour & become dry when stored in the fridge.
Instead, buy in small quantities. Place them on the kitchen platform and use it while cooking. They will taste fresh.
But keep it away from direct sunlight or in a glass with the stems submerged in water.
Don't keep it in the fridge.
3. Coffee Powder
Coffee powder must not be stored in air tight containers in the fridge as it causes mold & its flavour gets ruined.
Store your coffee in an airtight container, at room temperature anywhere in your kitchen.
While using the coffee use a clean & dry spoon to keep it fresh for a longer time
4. Honey
Keeping honey in the fridge will cause it to harden and alter its taste.
It should be stored at room temperature, away from direct sunlight
Honey will crystallize over a period of time.
It is better to plan your purchase. Once you finish it, you can buy it again.
Bananas when kept at room temperature, help the fruit to ripen & taste better.
You all know that Bananas are not kept in the fridge.
Once your Bananas become brown, do not throw them away.
Instead keep them in the freezer. With these frozen bananas you can make different types of desserts like milkshakes, frozen youghurt, etc.
Remember, over ripe Bananas kept near fruits like Grapes, Apples, Papaya, etc. can make the fruits ripen quicker.
So try to keep the Bananas away from them.
6. Nuts & Dry fruits
Nuts & dry fruits have very high nutritional value.
You might think they are very expensive & need to be refrigerated.
Do not do this. Refrigerating them can changes taste & results in the loss of their nutritional value.
There's no need to refrigerate them. Store them in a cool spot, in an airtight container and consume whenever you want.
7. Kesar. You all know this.
Kesar has a good fragrance & is very expensive. You all know that.
It is fragrant, high in nutrients, antioxidants and extremely flavourful.
You may think it must be refrigerated because it is expensive.
If you do this then its taste & nutrients are all lost.
Don't do this. Instead store it in your kitchen at a nice spot to preserve its flavour.
Use it in milk, sweets etc. and enjoy the rich taste, fragrance and nutrients of Kesar.
You saw the 7 food items. Now let me ask you a question.
What about tomatoes, potatoes & garlic?
Let me tell you that you must never store tomatoes in the fridge.
Keeping tomatoes in the fridge ruins the texture and taste.
Onion becomes black in the fridge. Even garlic must not be kept inside.
It is better to store them at room temperature in your kitchen.
Keep them away from each other to preserve their taste.
Keep them in separate paper bags to ensure they remain fresh for long.
Plan your purchase and eat them while they are fresh.
If you buy in bulk as you do not want to go to the market often, then you lose flavour.
Buy in small quantities, be healthy, eat tasty food and live a long life.
The Deaf Community celebrates the International Week of the Deaf.
It was started by the World Federation of the Deaf (WFD) in 1958 in Rome, Italy.
It is celebrated every year by Deaf individuals across the world in the last week of September.
This year the theme of the 2020 International Week of the Deaf is,
“Reaffirming Deaf People’s Human Rights”. This means that everyone should unite to advocate & create awareness
about Sign Languages and various factors. Continuously highlighting these points will create awareness.
This will eventually lead to equal rights for ther Deaf and better life with the power of Sign Language.
Right now Deaf people in India are facing many barriers
due to inaccessibility, inadequate education, lack of interpreters, etc. Deaf individuals across India are suffering.
This is because Sign Language is not recognised in India.
The Deaf Community needs to unitedly create awareness and advocate about the importance of Sign language.
Through celebrations such as these, Deaf indivudals can showcase their human rights.
These Human Rights will ensure equality and ensure better employment, education, accessiblity on media platforms
and various opportunities for the Deaf Community.
From 21st September - 27th September, each day of the week will have a different theme.
We will be releasing a video everyday explaining the theme of the day.
So stay tuned and keep watching and share the videos with family and friends.
Sharing these with friends, families and colleagues will create awareness about the Deaf Community.
This will lead to development. This is done around the world.
Today 21st September's theme is “Sign Languages”
Sign language is the native language of Deaf people around the world.
There are more than 200 different sign languages used around the world such as ISL, ASL, BSL, etc.
There are more than 70 million Deaf people worldwide.
They all used Sign Language to communicate.
Sign Langugae is used by Deaf children, Deaf families,
Hearing parents use Sign Language to communicate with Deaf children, interpreters, teachers and many people use Sign Language.
When Deaf individuals meet, their communication begins with the use of Sign Language.
Through Sign language, Deaf individuals connect with each other, leading to growth of the community.
They share their culture and identity through signs.
Sign Langauge is used for teaching, in clubs, at work places, etc.
Thus ensuring the growth of the Deaf Community. Without it, there will be stagnation.
Hence, Deaf Individuals using Sign Language will benefit a lot.
The Deaf Community is very diverse. There are Deaf people that belong to different, religions, cultures, etc.
Across North, South, East and West of India, there is diversity among Deaf Communities.
Deaf individuals belong to various cultural backgrounds such as Muslims, Christianity, Buddhism, etc.
But they all use Sign Language. This is the same all over the world.
International Week of the Deaf wants to showcase the beauty of Sign Languages.
Just like spoken languages like English, Hindi, Marathi have their own grammar, Sign Language too has its own grammar.
International Week of the Deaf aims to highlight the richness of Sign Language and its equal status.
Showcasing this will demonstarate the importance of Sign Language to the Deaf Community.
Deaf individuals across the world face a lot of discrimination and are not allowed to use Sign Language.
We can over come this discrimination by creating awareness and advocating the importance of Sign Language.
It cannot only be done through advocacy but also creating awareness by training hearing individuals,
organising activities, showcasing stories in Sign Languages, etc.
People will see that the Deaf Community is happy and are entitled to Sign Language as their Human Rights.
When it is dully given to them it will lead to immese development.

Uganda in Africa was the first country to legally recognize sign language in 1995.
Sign Language received equal status to the spoken languages in Uganda.
After that only approximately 50 countries have formally recognised Sign Languages.
People around the world are advocating.
The advocacy for recognition of Sign Languages is important.
The Deaf Community have their own Human Rights and use Sign Language as a natural medium of communication.
Once Sign Language is recognised, Deaf individuals stand to receive many benefits.

in news, education, etc there will be accessibility as the language will be spoken.
Similarly in India, there is a large Deaf Community that communicates in ISL and demand its recognition.
This will ensure many benefits in the future. Hence advocating for it is important.
They deserve full recognition by the government and equal status to the spoken languages used in that country.
Sign languages grammar includes expressions, emotions such as anger, sadness, variation in tone, hand signs,
which is equal to the linguistic features of spoken languages.

The recognition of national sign languages is the first step for achieving human rights.
If Sign Language is made official, then the government will have to give them interpreters, education, accessibility etc.
Sign Language will lead to inclusion of the Deaf in the society.
Hence the legal recognition of sign language is necessary.

The names of 8 local railway stations have been changed.
How interesting that these 8 stations are being renamed.
This is because the railway stations were from the British era.
They are being named to honour Maharashtrian and Indian culture.
The initiative was proposed by Member of Parliament Rahul Shewale.
The proposal was given to Maharashtra Chief Minister Eknath Shinde,
Deputy Chief Ministers Devendra Fadnavis, Ajit Pawar and other cabinet members. It was approved on 13th March 2024.
The proposal was then sent to the Central Government & the Railway Ministry for its approval.
Here is the list of 8 stations and their new names:
1. Cotton Green will be changed to Kalachowki.
What does the word mean?
It is named Kalachowki because of a police chowki there, which was coated with black coal tar.
2. The name Charni Road will be changed to Girgaon.
It is named after the famous Girgaon Chowpatty area as ‘Giri’ means hill because of Malabar Hill which is close by.
‘Gaon’ means village. Hence, the name Girgaon.
3. The name Dockyard to be changed to Mazgaon.
Here is why. The name is formed by merging the Marathi words 'Mazha’ meaning 'my' and ‘gaon’ meaning village.
4. The name Kings Circle to be changed to Tirthankar Parshvanath.
It is named after a Jain temple dedicated to Lord Parshvanath located on Ambedkar Road near the station.
5. The name Curry Road to be changed to Lalbaug.
After the Lalbaug area which is famous for its 90 years old Ganpati Pandel, the Lalbaugcha Raja Ganpati.
6. The name Sandhurst Road to be changed to Dongri.
The name Dongri is derived from the Marathi word 'dongar’ which means hill.
7. The name Marine Lines to be changed to Mumbadevi after the famous Goddess and her temple.
8. The name Mumbai Central Station to be changed to Nana Jagannath Shankarsheth Station.
It is named after person born in 1803 in Thane.
He grew up to be a famous businessman, educationalist and philanthropist.
He played an important role in social and economic development of Mumbai. This is why the place is named after him.
Apart from this, Ahmednagar will be renamed as Ahilya Nagar.
This is to signifying the importance of Rani Ahilyabai Holkar who was born there.

The Election Commission (EC) said that for the upcoming general elections and a few state elections,  in 2024,
the various political parties will have rallies, campaigns, speeches etc for attracting the voters,
however, they should  avoid using derogatory and insulting words about people with disability (PwD).
The correct words as per the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPWD) Act 2016 should be used.
For example: For a Deaf individual, derogatory words like gunga, behra, dumb should not be used.
As mentioned in RPWD Act 2016, the term Deaf should be used.
The correct and respectful word, Locomotor Disability should be used instead of derogatory words like lame, langda, lula, apahij etc.
Instead of derogatory words like andha and kana, the correct word to be used is Blindness and low vision.
Retarded, pagal etc are derogatory words and should not be used. Instead repectful word intellectual disability to be used.
EC warned all political parties to go through the RPWD Act 2016 and use the correct terms to address people with disabilities.
Violation of these rules may lead to an imprisonment of up to five years under Section 92 of the RPWD Act 2016
Political parties must go through the RPWD Act and follow the same.
There several other guidelines as well.
Political parties should shed the attitudinal barrier about persons with disability and treat them with respect.
and also include more PwDs as party workers and members.
Speeches, campaigns and other activities should also be accessible to PwDs.
Parties should provide a training module on disability to their workers to ensure respectful communication with the PwDs.
They should also declare on their website that they will use disability sensitive language and promote respect and equality.
All campaign materials must undergo an internal review to ensure that they do not contain any ableist language.
These were the guidelines.

Most famous Mount Everest is unhygienic!

pick up their own poop and bring it back to the base camp in those bags. This way the mountain can be kept clean.
